## ▶▶ v646 — TRENDS GETS TABS, FEED FIRST — because the analyzer largely DUPLICATES Remix.
Jörgen, unprompted, one hour after v645: *"i started to think also that the remix is kind of the
same as analyze some video trend. im not sure anyone will use that, more use the remix instead."*
**He is right, and the code says it more strongly than he did.** Compared the two endpoints field by
field: **`remix.js` already returns AND `renderRemixResults` already DISPLAYS `whyItWorks` +
`originalSummary`** — so the "reverse-engineer why it worked" half of the analyzer is not merely
similar to Remix, it is DUPLICATED inside it. Remix is also a superset on both ends: **5 input
sources** (tiktok/youtube/article/paste/file) vs the analyzer's 2, and its output is a finished post
(`remixCaption`, `remixHashtags`, `suggestedDay`, `seriesParts`) where the analyzer stops at scripts.
**The analyzer's only genuinely unique value is TWO things: multiple angles (`ideas[]`) into the
Ideas list, and `teachBrandTrend` — the one button that feeds a trend to the brain.**
**THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE WAS MY OWN v644 DECISION: when I built the one actionable path out of a
trending post ("Make it mine →"), I routed it to REMIX, not to the analyzer.** If the natural
destination for "here is a post that's working, make it mine" is Remix, the analyzer is the odd one
out. Worth remembering as a general tell: **when a new feature's obvious wiring bypasses an existing
screen, that screen is a candidate for removal.**
**HE CHOSE A FOURTH OPTION over my three** (I offered fold-into-Remix / check the usage data /
sharpen the difference): *"lets just make the analyzer a second tab not highlighted one in trends."*
Nothing is removed, the duplication is simply demoted — which is the reversible call, and correct
given the usage question is still unmeasured.
**BUILT:** `.create-sub-tabs` (the Remix source-tab classes, so it looks native) with
**"What's rising" ACTIVE by default** and "Analyze a video" second; `#vlPanel-watch` holds
`#vlTrendMemory`, `#vlPanel-analyze` holds the quick card + manual panel + status + results.
**`vlTab(which)` is deliberately NOT persisted** — the feed is the front door every time, because
the analyzer should not become the default just because someone used it once. Anything navigating
here EXPECTING the analyzer calls `vlTab('analyze')` after `switchView` — **the "Try a viral twist"
nudge (ONB_STEPS) does exactly that, and would otherwise have landed on the feed while promising the
analyzer.** The coach's `pull_trends` action needs the feed and gets it by default.
**THE v645 FOLD IS REVERTED — the tab IS the fold.** `renderTrendMemory` is back to
`act + pull + body` (the `act` extraction from v645 stays: "Worth making yours" still leads its tab)
and the `.vl-watch` CSS is deleted. Subtitle back to the feed sentence; the analyzer's own sentence
moved INSIDE its tab, where it now also points at Remix for a finished post.
**TWO STALE SIM TESTS CAUGHT, and one would have been a guaranteed false fail:** `viral-lab` taps
straight to the analyzer, which had just moved behind a tab — its taps now include `vlTab('analyze')`
and it is told the feed being default is CORRECT; the `trends` test (rewritten only an hour earlier
for the v645 fold) was rewritten again for tabs, and now also checks BOTH tab directions switch.
**Verified by running the real `vlTab` against a stubbed DOM** (both directions + a garbage argument
falling back to watch), plus a structural check that the panels nest correctly, the analyze panel is
hidden at load, and the view's divs balance. 35/36 gates green, APP_VERSION → v646.
**STILL UNMEASURED, and one query settles it: `viral` and `remix` are metered as SEPARATE actions
(`guard(req,'viral')` / `guard(req,'remix')`), so `usage_events` can prove whether the analyzer is
used at all.** If it is not, the fold-into-Remix option (move `teachBrandTrend` + a "3 angles"
toggle into Remix, then shelve the analyzer via CS_SHELVED) is the next step — and it would make the
Trends screen purely the watch feed, exactly matching its name.

## ▶▶ v645 — THE TRENDS SCREEN PUTS THE DOING PART FIRST. Two jobs stopped fighting for one screen.
Jörgen: *"how to make the trends section easier to understand for a new user? like separate tabs
inside one function for drop your link and the trends?"* **He was right that it is two screens; the
question was where the split line goes, so I mocked three and let him pick.** The tell was in the
copy: the subtitle was doing both jobs in one breath (*"What's rising in your niche, competitor
moves, and the trends you teach it… Paste any blowing-up video and it reverse-engineers why"*).
**Copy working that hard is a screen telling you it is two screens.**
**THE ARGUMENT AGAINST HIS LITERAL VERSION (tabs split analyzer / trends): "Worth making yours"
belongs to BOTH.** It comes out of the trends pull but its button jumps to Remix — so under that
split it has no correct home. The better cut is **actionable vs passive**, which is the distinction
HE drew one message earlier ("you can actually USE something from trends, otherwise all are just
running topics that feed the brain"). He chose **B — action first, no tabs**, and keeping the name.
**WHY NO TABS, recorded so it is not re-litigated: v451 already ran the Shazam pass on this exact
screen** (one primary action on top, the rest folded behind a small link). Tabs would have fought
that pattern AND put a navigation decision in front of a user who has not yet seen what the screen
does. The Remix `.create-sub-tab` precedent does not transfer — those switch INPUT SOURCES within
one job, not between two jobs.
**BUILT:** `#vlTrendMemory` moved BELOW `#vlResults` (status/results are empty divs until you
analyse, so a fresh screen reads paste-box → posts → folded feed; after an analysis the breakdown
lands directly under the box that made it). The "Worth making yours" strip is built into its own
`act` string instead of being appended to `body`, because `body` is now folded. Everything else —
pull control, window chips, auto-pulled panel, competitor moves, taught trends — goes inside a
`<details class="vl-watch">`, closed by default, open-state remembered in `vl-watch-open`
(device-global raw localStorage, mirroring the `home-brain-open` precedent — this is a display
preference, not brand data, so it is deliberately NOT bkey-scoped). Subtitle rewritten to lead with
the action.
**THE ONE DECISION THAT MATTERS FOR NEW USERS: it does NOT fold when the watch half is empty** —
which is every brand until its first cron. Folding an empty section would hide the only thing that
explains what that half of the screen is for, and a new brand would look like a broken screen.
**VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE REAL FUNCTION against stubs in all four states a user can be in:** new
brand (no fold, invitation + pull button visible), full brand (folded, posts out front), posts but
all trends dismissed (posts + invitation, no fold), trends but no posts (folded). Plus: act strip
precedes the fold, the summary count line renders, and the open state round-trips both ways.
**AND THE STALE-TEST TRAP, caught before it cost a run:** `mobile-user.js`'s `trends` feature told
the driver to find the auto-pulled panel, the window chips and the pull button — all now INSIDE the
fold — so it would have reported this change as a bug. Rewritten to open the fold first, assert the
new order, and treat a missing "Worth making yours" strip as ACCEPTABLE (it only fills once the
scraper returns engagement data — asserting it would have manufactured a false fail).
35/36 gates green, APP_VERSION → v645.

## ▶▶ v644 — TRENDS GETS ITS FIRST ACTIONABLE THING: "Worth making yours". Zero extra spend.
Jörgen: *"as it's already pulling from X anyway there should be an area where it pulls the 5 most
viral posts in the user's niche that they can repurpose"* — then the sharper observation: **"i also
like that you can actually USE something from trends. otherwise all are just running topics that
feed the brain."** He is right: every other thing on that screen is passive.
**THE COSTING, RESEARCHED NOT GUESSED (docs.x.ai, Aug 2026).** xAI now has a dedicated **`x_search`**
tool — keyword + semantic + user search + thread fetch, engagement metrics, image AND video
understanding, `from_date`/`to_date`, and **`allowed_x_handles` (max 20)** which maps exactly onto
the bookmarked-creators idea. **$5 / 1k tool calls, but TOKENS DOMINATE** (grok-4.6 $2/1M in,
$6/1M out, and xAI's own docs warn a search workload runs 2-3× the naive token estimate). Estimated
at 30 brands daily: **Apify ~$18/mo · Grok x_search ~$30-50/mo NEW.**
**THE DECIDING FACT: option (a) is genuinely free.** The trends cron ALREADY runs the X pull every
night with the brand's keywords — it was just discarding the engagement fields at the end of
`fetchXPosts`. Keeping them costs nothing. **The honest limit, and the UI says it out loud: the
query is `sort:'Latest'`, so this is "the most-engaged of the 25 most RECENT posts", NOT a viral
leaderboard.** A true top ranking needs `maxItems` 100 (~$72/mo) or a second `sort:'Top'` query
(~$36/mo) — at which point Grok is better data for the same money.
**COST DRIVER IS CRON vs ON-DEMAND, NOT GROK vs APIFY** (worth remembering for v2): a passive feed
must be pre-pulled for every brand every night (~900 calls/mo); the bookmarked-creators version is
demand-driven — pull when the strip is opened, cache 24h — so it lands at **~$5-15/mo** AND each
call is cheaper because `allowed_x_handles` narrows the search.
**BUILT (a):** new `tweetEngagement(it)` in `_trends.js` follows the existing defensive
field-fallback pattern (`tweetText`/`tweetTs`/`tweetHandle`) — **the actor's output shape has never
been verified live, so it accepts camelCase, snake_case AND `public_metrics` shapes; all three
smoke-tested.** Score weights reposts ×3 ("someone passed it on" is the strongest signal), replies
×2, views/1000 as a tie-break only. `topXPosts()` ranks the FULL deduped pool (not the 8 that
survive the trends cap), requires real engagement + ≥40 chars + a link, and keeps the text
**untruncated to 600 chars** because a post you intend to REMIX needs its whole body, not the
180-char trend headline. Carried through `pullXTrends`/`pullAllTrends` as an array property, the
same way v453 carries `lanes`. Cron writes `auto_trends.topPosts` (capped 5, fields clamped).
**A ONE-LINE DIAGNOSTIC MAKES IT SHIPPABLE UNVERIFIED:** `x-lane: N posts, M with engagement data`
— and when M is 0 it says `ENGAGEMENT FIELDS NOT FOUND, top-posts strip will stay empty`. So the
first cron after deploy answers definitively whether the field names are right, and if they are
wrong **the strip shows nothing rather than presenting an unranked list as a "top 5".**
**FRONTEND:** `getTopPosts()` (TTL + link-validated) and a `.vl-top-*` strip in Trends — white
cards on the panel's cream so they read as things you DO, each with @handle, real numbers, and
**"Make it mine →"** = `remixTopPost(i)`, which switches to Remix, sets the paste source, fills the
text + link, runs `useSourcePaste()` and toasts. **Never make the user copy a URL across two
screens** (the v351/v355 auto-return doctrine).
**A BUG I INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT BY READING, NOT BY LUCK:** my first insert split the competitor-moves
block in two, leaving `${_cmAge}` (a `let` declared inside the first half) referenced from the
second — a guaranteed ReferenceError. Restored as one block with the new strip placed BEFORE it.
**ALSO CAUGHT: the empty-state branch ASSIGNS to `body` rather than appending**, so a brand whose
trends were all dismissed or TTL-expired would have had its posts silently overwritten — `_tp.length`
added to that guard.
**STILL TRUE AND FLAGGED IN THE UI: X only.** His brands post to Reels and TikTok; TikTok/IG would
need separate scrapers through `crawl-social` and real money. 35/36 gates green, APP_VERSION → v644.
**▶ v644b, caught by his question "where does this go?": ONLY THE CRON WROTE `topPosts`.** The
on-demand `pull-trends.js` (the "Pull fresh trends" button) already persists `items` into
`auto_trends` — v600b added that exact merge so a deployed fix would stop looking broken for days —
but it dropped the posts, and the frontend's in-memory merge copied `{at, items}` only. So tapping
the button would have fired the `x-lane:` diagnostic in the logs and shown NO strip: the same
"correct but invisible is indistinguishable from a bug" class as v642. Both ends now carry it.
**The important half is the GUARD, not the copy: `topPosts` is written ONLY when the pull actually
produced some** (`if (_tp.length)`), because `Object.assign` with an empty array would WIPE a good
set from the cron every time the X lane came back empty — no Apify token, a stalled run, a keyword
with no recent posts. The client mirrors it (`if (Array.isArray(...))`) so an absent key can't
overwrite either. Behaviourally verified 4/4 both directions.

## ▶▶ v643 — THE BRAND-LEAK PARALLEL AUDIT. 4 agents, 8 real fixes, and the BACKEND came back CLEAN.
Jörgen: *"the leaks between brands is also a super important thing"* + *"you probably need to run
several agents on this."* Four READ-ONLY audits on disjoint surfaces (frontend switch-state ·
localStorage namespacing · backend hydration · DB query scoping). **TWO INDEPENDENT AGENTS CONVERGED
ON THE SAME ROOT CAUSE from different directions — that convergence is the strongest signal in the
set and is why it is fixed first.**
**#1 THE KILLER — `_listLoadOk` was never reset at the top of `switchBrand`, so the guard that exists
to prevent list destruction was DISARMED during exactly the dangerous window.** It initialises
all-`true` and is only written inside the parallel loads. But `currentBrand = data` lands at ~6907
while `remixes`/`notebookNotes`/`productRefs`/`bookmarkCategories`/`promptHistory` still hold the
OUTGOING brand's data until ~6925-6929 resolve — a full `loadIdeasFromDB` await plus another round
trip. In that window `_listLoaded('remixes')` still returned true, so a save ran
**`_replaceBrandRows('remixes', NEW_BRAND, OLD_BRAND_ROWS)`: it deleted the new brand's ENTIRE list
and replaced it with the previous brand's.** Reachable from `remixContent` (no brandGate, 15-40s
generation), `sharpenRemix`, `saveFromTryAll`, any notebook or bookmark tap. Fix is ONE LINE — mark
all five unloaded at the top of the switch — and the existing guard then refuses the save and TELLS
the user instead of destroying data.
**#2 `ideaRedoRun` — the only ungated generator that also WRITES TO THE DATABASE.** `idea.id` is an
ARRAY INDEX, so after a mid-generation switch `findIndex` matched whatever idea now sits at that
index in the NEW brand: overwrote it with old-brand content, then `delete().eq('brand_id', NEW)
.eq('title', OLD_TITLE)` destroyed the new brand's real row. Flagged by BOTH the frontend and DB
agents; CLAUDE.md had it listed as open since v639. Now `brandGate()`d.
**#3 THE QUIETEST ONE — `brainAutoDistill` had no brand check.** It reads one brand's edit signals /
dismissals / approvals, awaits the distiller, then appends the resulting rules to the LIVE global
`settings.coachNotes` and saves. A switch during that call wrote **brand A's voice rules into brand
B's Voice Memory — which `fullBrandBlock` feeds into EVERY generation, permanently, with nothing on
screen to show it happened.** Trigger is ordinary: approve a few ideas, tap a stat filter.
**#4 CORRECTION TO THIS FILE: v639 claimed `sharpenIdea` "discards its result silently if the brand
changes mid-request". IT DOES NOT — there was no guard at all.** Two agents said so independently and
reading `sharpenNow` confirmed it. Its apply writes into `IDEAS[id]` (array index → wrong brand's
idea after a switch) and then runs a titled DELETE against that brand. Now gated. **A claim in this
file is not evidence; verify before trusting it.**
**#5 `disableDailyPush` deleted by `.eq('user_id')` ALONE** — turning the ping off on brand B killed
brand A's subscription and every other device's row, while `enableDailyPush` correctly inserts one
row per (user_id, brand_id). Now matches. Uses `.is('brand_id', null)` for the null case because
**PostgREST rejects `brand_id=eq.null`** — it does not match NULL.
**#6 `_ideaDelivery` / `_remixDelivery` survived the switch** while their Quick Post twin
`_tvDelivery` is correctly re-read per brand — that asymmetry is what proved it was an omission.
Switching from a faceless B2B brand to a face-on founder brand generated (and billed) a whole batch
in the wrong shape, with the toggle visibly showing the previous brand's setting.
**#7 `loadTeamData` was the ONE loader in the parallel block with no token guard** — it assigns
INTERNALLY rather than via `.then()`, which is why the v638 sweep missed it. A rapid A→B→C switch
could show brand B's members and **pending invite email addresses** under brand C.
**#8 `loadBlogPosts` kept the previous brand's posts on a cache MISS** — the no-brand guard was right
but `if (raw)` meant a brand with no cached value simply kept the old array, and a later save wrote
them under the new brand's key. `loadPAAState` already resets first; this was the one loader that did
not. Latent while blog is shelved, a real cross-brand write the day it is unshelved.
**▶ THE BACKEND IS CLEAN, AND THE NEGATIVE IS TRUSTWORTHY.** Across 45 files / 130 top-level
declarations there is **ZERO module-level mutable state holding brand or user data** — the only two
mutated bindings are integer timeouts set by cron-only endpoints. The agent **mutation-tested its own
scanner** (injected 4 leak shapes + 1 pure control; caught 4, no false positive) before trusting the
result, using a real lexer rather than brace-counting. `_brandctx` was traced end to end: the
ownership check runs BEFORE any query, fails closed on error, and the checked id is the same variable
interpolated into every read. Both cron per-brand loops declare all brand-shaped state inside the
loop. **Do not re-audit this surface without new evidence.**
**STILL OPEN from this round (verified, not fixed): `obResetForTesting` deletes children before the
parent and never `.select('id')`s, so a silent RLS refusal reports success (low likelihood,
total impact when it fires); `saveEditSignals` can file one brand's taste signals under another after
an await; `enableDailyPush` reads `currentBrand?.id` after four awaits; `brain_scan_offered` is the
last `bkey()` caller using raw localStorage, so it can still write the shared `::_none` bucket during
a slow boot (misfiled boolean only); `loadAllBrandsFromDB` and `loadTeamData` swallow read errors,
degrading the client-side ownership check (server-side filter still holds).**
35/36 gates green. APP_VERSION v642 → **v643**, both stamps moved (`v643-149e6cad`).

## ▶▶ v640-backend (api.4feafb18) — WHY THE SCRIPTS DIDN'T SOUND SPOKEN. A coverage hole, measured.
**Jörgen filmed a v640 Quick Post: "seems better yes but not so much. it is on point but just really
missing the angle that it needs to be read in and talked into video and it needs to sound organically
sounding text that flows like real organic human speaking."** The content was right, the FORM was
wrong. His script: *"Yes. Start with the messy workflow. No jargon needed. Sales follow-ups eating
hours. Tools that don't talk. Briefing is free."* — **5 of 10 sentences have no finite verb, zero
connective words, and it is 44 words against a 90-150 spec.** Noun phrases with full stops. You
cannot read that into a lens.
**THE CAUSE IS A COVERAGE HOLE, NOT WORDING — and it is the SAME CLASS as v612/v625/v626/v635.** The
`SPOKEN-SCRIPT SHAPE` rule lived ONLY inside `writingCraft`'s `if (opts.spoken)` branch, and
**`generate-ideas.js` does not call `writingCraft`** (it keeps its own tuned prompt — a fact this file
has flagged twice as a "coverage trap" without anyone checking WHAT it was missing). So the one rule
in the codebase describing how a spoken script should FLOW has never once reached the generator that
writes every script Jörgen films. `viral-rewrite` passed `{spoken:true}` and got it; Quick Post
didn't. **Same app, two standards for the same job.**
**MEASURED on the REAL assembled prompt (stub the LLM, run the real handler, capture `messages`):
0 flow rules present, 4 compression rules present** — clarityFlow's *"One idea per sentence"* +
*"Cut every word that isn't working"*, the video spec's *"short sentences"*, and *"Never pad"*.
Cutting pressure with no counterweight ⇒ the model strips every sentence to its noun phrase. **That
is the whole mechanism.** (One check "PRESENT" was my own false positive — clarityFlow's *"Active
voice, subject and verb up front"* is about word ORDER, not sentence completeness. Verified before
counting it. **A grep for a concept will match a rule that merely shares its words.**)
**FIX — `spokenShape()` is now its own export in `_brain.js`, rewritten from METAPHOR to MECHANICS.**
The old text was *"beats, not bullet points… a natural talk-track with real rhythm"* — **a model can
satisfy a metaphor and still emit telegraph fragments.** The new block is things a model can check
its own draft against: complete sentences with a subject and a verb (fragments belong to the hook and
the on-screen text, never the body); **keep the CONNECTIVE TISSUE** (so/and/but/because/which
means/the way it works is — the small joining words written copy strips and speech requires; two
facts side by side are notes, two facts joined by "because" is someone talking); the listener cannot
re-read, so name a thing before commenting on it and say the key line twice in different words
(redundant on a page, the only reason it lands out loud); vary the length; **count the words — under
the floor means you wrote notes, not a script**; and an explicit **"OVERRIDES THE COMPRESSION RULES
FOR SPOKEN SCRIPTS"** clause, because otherwise it is rule #5 fighting rules #1-4 and position
decides the winner. Appended in `generate-ideas.js` directly after `clarityFlow()` — **adjacency is
load-bearing**, the override names "the compression rules" and must sit next to them (lands at 63.7%;
the v640 brand block is still last at 82.1%).
**ALSO REMOVED THE CONTRADICTION CLOSEST TO THE TASK:** the video format spec itself said *"Script is
written to be spoken — short sentences"*. That is the instruction nearest the actual job and it
pulled the opposite way. Now *"full sentences of varied length joined by natural connectors, 90-150
words (that is a FLOOR, not a target to undercut)"*. Same in `formatSpec.video` and the micro spec.
Left alone deliberately: clarityFlow's own "Short sentences by default, then VARY the length" (the
written-copy rule the override explicitly names) and the STATEMENT spec (statements ARE short).
**`writingCraft`'s branch now DELEGATES to the same `spokenShape()`**, so the direct caller
(generate-ideas) and the writingCraft callers can never drift to different rules. **Verified by
running the real handlers: remix and viral-rewrite were upgraded automatically.**
**`sharpen.js` DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE — checked, not skipped.** It also avoids `writingCraft`, but
it already carries its own inline defence (*"For spoken/video scripts keep the natural, conversational,
story-like talk-track and every beat; do NOT compress it into terse statements"*) plus a hard
same-length-within-10% rule. Adding a "restore the connectors you compressed out" instruction to an
editor explicitly told to make the SMALLEST possible change would create a contradiction. **The right
lever for an old fragment script is Redo, not Sharpen.**
**NEW GATE G40 `scripts/verify/spoken-shape.mjs` closes the CLASS.** It assembles the REAL prompt (a
file-level grep would pass on an unwired import — only the assembled prompt proves delivery) and
asserts the rule reaches BOTH generate-ideas and the writingCraft path, that the block keeps its six
load-bearing mechanics, and that the video spec no longer contradicts it. **Mutation-tested 3 ways,
all caught:** unwire it from generate-ideas (**reintroduces the exact original bug** → red), gut the
rule to a one-liner metaphor (7 assertions red), restore "short sentences" to the video spec. Files
verified byte-identical after mutation testing. Asserts BEHAVIOUR + CONCEPTS, **never exact phrasing**
— my first draft checked for the old metaphor strings and reported ABSENT for wording I had just
deliberately improved (the v619 lesson, live).
**MY OWN GATE WENT RED TWICE AND BOTH TIMES IT WAS THE FIXTURE:** viral-rewrite 400'd because I sent
`originalScript/hook/format` when it takes an `idea` OBJECT, then again because `angle` must be an
OBJECT with `.hook` or `.angle`, not a string. **A red gate needs verifying exactly as much as a
green one — I debugged the handler's actual validation instead of "fixing" working code.**
**BACKEND-ONLY: app.html untouched, so NO APP_VERSION/BUILD bump.** The split stamp behaved exactly
as designed — phone stamp stayed `v640-774d7adb` (no needless ~196KB download to every device),
server stamp moved `api.7380706e → api.4feafb18`. 35/36 gates green (only `bug-scan.mjs`, the known
false positive). **STILL UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE: whether the output actually reads as human speech.
The mechanism is measured; the taste is Jörgen's call.**

### ▶ ROUND 2 (api.21c25e5b) — grammar was fixed, but it wrote a FEATURE TOUR. The missing counterweight.
Jörgen filmed the next one: *"ok it is better but it can be even better defenetly."* The new script —
*"You don't shop a freelancer feed. You put the messy problem in. Willo turns it into a brief, a
person reviews it, and you get 2-3 vetted experts. Names stay hidden until you pick."* — has a finite
verb in every sentence (round 1 worked) and 43 words is IN SPEC for micro. **But it is a walkthrough
of how the product works: problem in → brief → person reviews → experts → you pick. Five sentences
about Willo, none about what the listener is living through.**
**METHOD THAT FOUND IT — stop patching symptom by symptom and MEASURE THE WHOLE DELTA.** This was the
third time "a rule exists in `writingCraft`, generate-ideas doesn't call `writingCraft`" had bitten,
so instead of another one-off I diffed the two rule sets concept-by-concept on the REAL assembled
prompt. Result: **7 apparent gaps, and 6 were FALSE POSITIVES** — generate-ideas has its own wording
for hook rules, the AI-tell opener list, bar-not-webinar VOICE, the word-level humanizer, per-format
arcs, and a self-check. **Exactly ONE was genuine**, and it is the one that explains the script.
**THE GENUINE GAP: generate-ideas' own SELF-CHECK says "lean on the brand's REAL specifics — its pain
points, USPs, facts, vocabulary" — which pushes TOWARD describing the product — and `writingCraft`'s
counterweight ("about the READER's situation rather than a product pitch") never reached it.** Same
shape as round 1: **a rule with no counterweight.** That is now the signature failure of this prompt;
when output drifts, look for a one-sided instruction before looking for a missing one.
FIX: a `STAY IN THE AUDIENCE'S WORLD, NOT THE PRODUCT'S` block appended to that self-check and
explicitly outranking it — the brand's specifics are RAW MATERIAL for talking about the reader's
situation, not the subject; a chain of "you do this, then it does that" is a feature tour however
well the sentences are built; open inside the annoying/expensive/confusing bit of their week and let
the mechanism appear only as the resolution; **"if a script could be read aloud by a competitor with
their name swapped in, it was about the product"** (a test the model can actually apply).
**ALSO FOUND, and it was inviting the bug outright: the micro spec said "ONE surprising fact or
MECHANISM".** For a product brand "mechanism" reads as "how our thing works" — so the format spec was
literally asking for the feature tour. Now: *"ONE surprising fact about how something in the WORLD
works — never a walkthrough of how the brand's own product works, which is a feature tour, not a
fact."*
**THIRD FIX — monotone CONSTRUCTION, not length.** 3 of 5 sentences opened "You …" and every one was
subject-verb-object. Grammatical, and still a metronome. `spokenShape`'s "vary the length" does not
catch that, so it now reads *"vary the length AND the construction … do not start three sentences the
same way, and never run a column of identical subject-verb-object lines"*.
**LESSON WORTH KEEPING (cost me a wrong claim mid-round): my first delta grep used `writingCraft`'s
EXACT phrasing and reported 7 gaps. Six were rules present in different words. A concept-grep both
over-matches (v640: "subject and verb up front" matched a completeness check but is about word ORDER)
and under-matches (here). VERIFY EACH HIT AGAINST THE OTHER FILE'S OWN WORDING before claiming a gap.**
Gate G40 extended to 15 assertions (audience-world counterweight reaches the first draft + names the
feature-tour failure mode + construction variation). Mutation-tested 2 more ways, both caught; files
byte-identical after. 35/36 gates green. Server stamp `api.4feafb18 → api.21c25e5b`, app.html still
untouched. **ANSWERED for the record: importing more GitHub anti-AI rule-sets is NOT the lever —
skills run in Claude, not in his Vercel app, so only copied TEXT reaches users; and both round-1 and
round-2 bugs were missing counterweights, not insufficient rule volume (the prompt is already ~19k
chars / 8 rule blocks, where a 9th generic block mostly raises contradiction risk).**
### ▶ ROUND 3 (api.cb038b4d) — the WORKED EXAMPLE, built to be a floor and not a mould.
Built the example offered in round 2, but **Jörgen raised the right objection mid-build — "i can see
all being too similar thats a big risk how to fix that?"** He is correct, and it reframed the design.
**THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS: constraints on GRAMMAR are safe, constraints on STRUCTURE cause
sameness.** "Every sentence has a verb" and "use connectives" apply to all good speech and never make
two brands sound alike. **"Open inside the listener's week" is a structural mould** — apply it to
every brand and every script starts the same way. That rule was MINE, added in round 2, and it was a
live convergence risk. Three changes, not one:
**(1) `spokenExample(bc)` is CONDITIONAL — it fires only when the brand has no approved winner in a
spoken format** (video/micro/qna, reusing the existing `SPOKEN_EX_FORMATS`, requiring >80 chars of
body so a stub cannot count). That is exactly when `approvedWinnersBlock` returns 0 chars and the
prompt otherwise carries rules with NO demonstration at all — AI WILLO's configuration. **The moment
the user approves one script of their own, their post replaces it and the example never renders for
that brand again.** Behaviourally verified 6/6 (no posts → shows; only statement winners → shows,
because a statement teaches voice not script shape; video winner → hides; micro winner → hides; stub
winner → shows; missing field → shows).
**(2) THREE variants with deliberately DIFFERENT arcs** (a lived situation, a hard number, a
correction), one picked at random per request — verified 3 distinct over 300 calls, ~even spread. A
single fixed example teaches ONE arc to every new brand, which is structurally the same mistake as
the hardcoded "Alex Hormozi style" v640 removed. Rotating them makes the GRAMMAR the constant and the
STRUCTURE a free choice. Each is set in a mundane domain (plumbing quote / unsold stock / houseplants)
deliberately unrelated to any real brand here, written flat on purpose, and the block names what must
NOT be copied: the structure, the topic and the voice.
**(3) The round-2 subject rule was scoped so it cannot harden into an opening formula.** It now says
explicitly **"THAT IS A RULE ABOUT SUBJECT, NOT ABOUT SHAPE"** and offers a MENU of ways in (blunt
claim, hard number, belief worth correcting, question someone asked, thing you noticed, comparison,
small story, punchline first) — mirroring the proven hook-rules pattern — plus a within-batch check:
if several scripts open the same way you have turned a subject rule into a template.
G40 now 22 assertions. **Mutation-tested 3 more ways, all caught:** make the example unconditional
(kills the anti-convergence guarantee), collapse to one fixed variant, turn the subject rule back
into one opening formula. Files byte-identical after.
**MY OWN MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG FIRST — again.** The rotation check sliced from `indexOf('TOO
COMPRESSED')`, which is the SHARED heading, so it reported 1 variant over 80 calls and looked like
broken rotation. The code was fine; the check was reading the wrong bytes. Fixed to read the first
QUOTED line (the part that actually differs). **The gate now carries a comment saying so, because the
next person will slice the heading too.**
**A GATE I BROKE, AND THE ORDERING RULE IT ENFORCES:** `brand-prompt.mjs` went red — *"winners sit
close to the output instruction — 4589 chars away"* (limit 4000). My two self-check blocks sat AFTER
the brand block, pushing the approved winners out of the recency window v640 established. **Fixed by
moving the whole SELF-CHECK group UP to sit with the other rules, immediately before
`rulePrecedence()`** (which must stay adjacent to the brand block it names) — NOT by relaxing the
threshold. **STANDING RULE: rules go before the brand block, the brand block goes last, and anything
appended after it steals the winners' recency.**
**▶▶ AND A REAL MISTAKE OF MINE, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: I ran `brand-prompt.mjs --snapshot`
carelessly, which OVERWRITES `scripts/verify/fixtures/generate-ideas.before.txt` with the CURRENT
prompt. The fixture is UNTRACKED by git, so the original literal capture is gone permanently.** Its
three DELTA assertions then compared the code against itself and went red. **NEVER run `--snapshot`
except on genuinely pre-fix code.** Recovered honestly: added a **`--reconstruct`** mode that
re-renders the prompt through current code with the five fields the pre-v612 `buildMasterPrompt` is
documented to have dropped (approvedExamples, learnedSignals, competitors, channels, visualStyle) —
which reproduces everything `measure()` actually reads (brandChars, share, missing) without
pretending to be a capture. Baseline restored and assertions live again: **2189 → 3466 brand chars,
8.3% → 13.0% share, 7 fields missing in the before.** **This is more CONSERVATIVE than the lost
original**, which also captured the pre-v640 ordering, so the true historical delta was larger.
35/36 gates green. Server stamp `api.21c25e5b → api.cb038b4d`; app.html still untouched.
**STILL NOT DONE: `XAI_REASONING_EFFORT=medium`** (env-only, no deploy, currently `low` by Jörgen's
latency choice) — the one remaining lever that is not a prompt change.

## ▶▶ v641 — "VIRAL TWIST DIDN'T CHANGE ANYTHING": it worked, it was BELOW THE FOLD.
Jörgen sent two screenshots a minute apart, same micro-lecture, identical script: *"microlecture and
then viral twist. text seems the same."* **NOT a quality bug and NOT a dead button — the panel
rendered off-screen.** `#viralTwist-tv` (app.html ~12790) and `#tvRedoBox` sit AFTER the entire
`.tp-actions-row` in the markup, and on a phone those buttons are the LAST thing on screen. So the
angles panel **and its loading state** rendered entirely below the fold with nothing scrolling to
them: the button span its dots and, from the user's side, nothing happened. **He confirmed it
mid-investigation by scrolling — "a jep i can see the fold now".** Same class as the Viral Lab
results auto-scroll fix.
**ALSO WORTH KNOWING (and it is by design, not a bug): Viral Twist only PROPOSES angles.** The script
is SUPPOSED to be unchanged at that point — the text only changes after "Use this angle →" then "Use
this version ✓". So "the text seems the same" was two separate correct behaviours reading as one bug.
FIX: new **`_tvReveal(el)`** helper (smooth `scrollIntoView`, block:'center', try/caught) called at
FOUR points — `tvViralTwist` on the loading state AND on the result, `tvViralRewrite` on both, and
`tvRedoNotesOpen`. Revealing only the finished result would still leave the button looking dead for
the whole request, which is why the loading state is revealed too.
**CHECKED AND DELIBERATELY LEFT: `#tvApprovePraise` and `#tvDismissReasons`** (same dead zone) are
legacy markup — nothing ever un-hides them; both were superseded by full-screen `.dp-backdrop`
modals (`tvShowDismissReasons` builds one), which are visible regardless of scroll.
**GATE: extended `tv-dead-buttons.mjs`** — the right home, since its whole premise is "no Quick Post
action can be a silent no-op" and this is the same reported symptom in a different mechanism. Asserts
all three handlers call `_tvReveal`, that it is defined once, and specifically that the LOADING state
is revealed (not just the result). Function bodies are sliced up to the next top-level `function`
rather than brace-counted — **braces inside string literals make naive counting lie** (that trap has
cost this project three separate debugging rounds). Mutation-tested: strip the reveal from
`tvViralTwist` → 2 assertions red; app.html byte-identical afterwards.
**FRONTEND ROUND, so APP_VERSION bumped v640 → v641** and both stamps moved (`v641-cb2515b0`) —
unlike the three backend-only rounds before it, phones DO need this one.
**STANDING RULE THIS ESTABLISHES: any panel appended after `.tp-actions-row` is off-screen by
default. New output there must call `_tvReveal`, or it will be reported as a dead button.**

### ▶ SUCCESS-PATH TIMING LOG (api.179223c7, backend-only) — so the reasoning-effort test is measurable.
Jörgen: *"we can try the medium and see how much longer it takes and if it is better."* Checked first:
**every FAILURE path in `callXAI` logged a duration and the SUCCESS path logged nothing**, so a
latency comparison between effort settings could only ever have been "it felt slower" — which cannot
settle whether medium is worth the wait. Added one line on the success return:
`xAI OK <ms>ms · effort=<x> · reasoning_tokens=<n> · completion_tokens=<n> · model=<m>`.
`reasoning_tokens` is the number that actually moves with the setting (the v-earlier empty-200 bug
showed 2533 reasoning tokens / 0 completion tokens at the old implicit "high"), so it sits next to
the wall clock. Scope verified by reading the function, not by source order — `effort` (L82), `t0`
(L95) and `attempt` (L97 loop) are all in `callXAI`'s body, so the line cannot ReferenceError on the
success path. No PII, no bodies, one line per call.
**THE A/B THIS ENABLES (needs TWO deploys, which is the minimum for a real comparison): deploy with
effort still `low` → generate 3 posts = the baseline; then set `XAI_REASONING_EFFORT=medium` in
Vercel env → redeploy (env changes need one) → generate 3 more.** Then read both sets from the
production logs and compare ms + reasoning_tokens + the writing. `low` is the current default in
code, so removing the env var reverts.

## ▶▶ v642 — "SHARPEN CHANGED NOTHING": two correct behaviours that both looked like a dead button.
Jörgen: *"boring then video and then sharpen and original and sharpen stayd the same all."* **Neither
cause was a broken Sharpen.** (a) Sharpen is a DELIBERATELY light-touch editor — its prompt says
"make the SMALLEST changes that fix the critique" and hard-caps the result at the original length
("if you cut it to half you have FAILED") — so on a draft with no weak parts pass 1 returns `STRONG`
and the endpoint answers `{unchanged:true}`. That is a REAL outcome, and its only evidence was a
2.6s toast. **This got MORE likely today: the v640-round fixes made first drafts better, so Sharpen
legitimately has less to do.** (b) When it DID rewrite, `sharpenQuickPost` updates the fields IN
PLACE — and those fields sit ABOVE the `.tp-actions-row` button that was just tapped, so the change
landed off-screen while the toast flashed at the bottom. **Same fold class as v641, mirrored: the
twist's output was below the buttons, Sharpen's is above them.**
FIX: `sharpenNow` gained an optional **`o.onUnchanged`** callback (toast lengthened 2.6→3.2s), and
`sharpenQuickPost` now writes a persistent **`.tv-sharpen-note`** onto the card in all three cases —
rewrote (names WHICH fields changed, by diffing each field's text before overwriting it), ran but
came back identical, or already-sharp (explains that it is a light-touch editor and points at Redo
with notes / Viral Twist for a real change of direction) — then **`_tvReveal(#tvResult,'start')`**
scrolls back up to the rewritten text. `_tvReveal` gained an optional `block` arg for this.
**GATE: `tv-dead-buttons.mjs` extended again** (5 more assertions — same premise: no Quick Post
action may be a silent no-op). Mutation-tested: rename `onUnchanged` → red. app.html byte-identical
after. APP_VERSION v641 → **v642** (frontend round, phones need it).
**LESSON: an outcome that is CORRECT but invisible is indistinguishable from a bug. Any action whose
"success" can legitimately be 'I changed nothing' must say so somewhere that outlives a toast.**

## ▶▶ REASONING EFFORT — SETTLED WITH A NUMBER, DO NOT RE-LITIGATE: `low` is the ONLY viable setting.
Jörgen tested `XAI_REASONING_EFFORT=medium` in production. Result: *"takes yes too long"* **and a hard
failure.** The production log is unambiguous:
`07:30:11 POST /api/generate-ideas 500 — xAI FAILED after 90014ms on attempt 1 — TIMEOUT | model=grok-4.6`
**90,014ms — medium blew straight through generate-ideas' 90s `timeoutMs` (v627).** And note
**"attempt 1" with NO retry**: `callXAI` deliberately does not retry a hard timeout (it has already
burned the budget), so at medium ONE slow call is an instant 500 → the "AI is having a moment" toast.
**So medium is not a latency preference, it does not FIT the endpoint's time budget.** Raising the
budget is not the answer either: generate-ideas is 90+90 inside a 300s `maxDuration`, so a
medium-effort retry would risk the platform kill that v627 exists to prevent.
**CONCLUSION: `low` stays the default in code, and the env var should NOT be set.** The one remaining
non-prompt lever on output quality is therefore CLOSED — spoken flow is governed by the rules and the
worked example (v640 rounds 1-3), not by how hard the model thinks.
**NOTE: the v641 `xAI OK …ms · effort=… · reasoning_tokens=…` SUCCESS log is still UNPROVEN in
production** — every medium call failed, so only the pre-existing FAILURE line fired. It will prove
itself on the first successful generation back on `low`; if `xAI OK` never appears in the logs after
that, the line is wrong and needs checking.

## ▶▶ THE SIM NOW READS THE CONTENT (local, no deploy) — Jörgen stops being the screenshot pipeline.
**His idea, and it is the right one: "the sim should change accounts and try all these formats and
button through and see what changes in content, instead of me sending you screenshots."** Every
output defect found by hand this week was MEASURABLE, not aesthetic — verbless fragments, zero
connectives, 44 words against a 90-word floor, three sentences opening the same way, a script that
toured the product. Each cost him filming a take and me diagnosing from ONE sample.
**THE BOUNDARY, DELIBERATE: the sim MEASURES, it does NOT judge.** The vision driver has a track
record of being confidently wrong about content (it once decided Boring Electrolytes was a sourcing
company and marked on-brand posts off-brand). So `content-quality` produces its OWN verdict from
arithmetic and never reaches the driver; every flag prints the offending sentence and every script
goes into the report verbatim. Numbers narrow where to look; taste stays Jörgen's.
**NEW `scripts/qa/content-checks.js`** (standalone + self-testing, `node scripts/qa/content-checks.js`):
verbless-sentence candidates, connective density per 100 words, length vs the format's own floor,
repeated sentence openings, a product-tour signal, and cross-run convergence. **Its self-test runs the
THREE REAL scripts from this week — the fragment one, the feature-tour one, and the rewritten flowing
one — and asserts the checks separate them. A metric that cannot fail on the known-bad script is
decorative.**
**TWO OF MY OWN CHECKS WERE WRONG AND THE SELF-TEST CAUGHT BOTH.** (1) The verbless check flagged
*"That's the bit that's broken."* — a perfectly good sentence — because contracted copulas (that's,
it's, you're, there's) were missing from the finite-verb list. Then it flagged *"You only talk to the
one you choose."* because `talk`/`choose` were not listed either — **and no closed verb list will ever
be complete**, so the fix is STRUCTURAL: a sentence opening with a subject pronoun plus 2+ words has
a finite verb whether or not the word is in any list. None of the real fragments start that way, so
false positives went to zero with the signal intact. (2) The product-tour check gated on brand-name
mentions and scored the tour script CLEAN (it names "Willo" once, uses no "then") — while the earlier
walkthrough never named the brand at all. **Counting brand mentions is not the signal.** Rewritten to
what actually separates a tour from content: mechanism verbs present AND lived-experience markers
(you've/had/were/ended up) absent. **Its known limit is asserted in the self-test rather than hidden**
— the fragment script is too compressed to carry mechanism verbs and slips past this check, and is
caught by the verbless and length checks instead. The layers cover each other.
**HARNESS:** `content-quality` switches brand, generates each spoken format, and reads
`window._tvIdea` (the structured idea) rather than scraping the DOM. Top-level `await` is a
SyntaxError inside `new Function`, so all awaiting happens in an async IIFE that flips
`_qaContent.status` — **verified by constructing the tap through `new Function` exactly as the
harness does, with a negative control proving a real top-level await IS rejected** (my first check
used a `/^\s*await/` regex and lied, matching indented awaits inside the IIFE). Generations take
minutes, so the harness polls to completion instead of using the normal idle wait.
**A GATE CAUGHT ME BREAKING ITS OWN RULE:** `harness-coverage.mjs` went red — *"UNRESTORED:
_qaContent"*. Any `window._qa*` marker a taps body sets must be cleared in `clearLeftoverModals` or
it leaks into the next feature; that exact class once invalidated 29 features in one run. Added the
cleanup rather than exempting the new feature.
**HOW TO RUN IT:** `node mobile-user.js` includes it by default (that is the point). `SKIP_CONTENT=1`
drops it when the run is about a button, not the writing. `ONLY=content-quality node mobile-user.js`
runs just the content pass. `QA_BRANDS=3 QA_FORMATS=video,micro` tunes the harvest without editing
the file. Default is 2 brands × 3 formats = 6 generations, so it costs real credits and ~5 minutes.
**NOT YET RUN LIVE** — the analyser is proven against real scripts and the plumbing is verified, but
the end-to-end harvest against production has not happened. 35/36 gates green; local only, no deploy.

## ▶▶ v640 — SECOND PARALLEL ROUND (billing · output quality · API layer · Settings). 4 fixed, and the OUTPUT-QUALITY ANSWER finally has a mechanism.
**FIXED #1 — THE DELETE-BRAND × WAS BROKEN AND SWITCHED TO THAT BRAND INSTEAD.** The onclick was
built with `${JSON.stringify(escHtml(name))}` **inside a double-quoted HTML attribute** — the quotes
JSON.stringify adds TERMINATE the attribute, so the handler is `…deleteBrandConfirm('ID', ` = a
SyntaxError that never installs. `stopPropagation` therefore never ran and the click bubbled to the
row's own `switchBrand()`. Tapping × on a brand SWITCHED to it — and `deleteBrandConfirm` then refuses
to delete the ACTIVE brand, so the user ended up further from deleting it. This is the only
delete-brand affordance in the app, and `proof-brand-delete` stayed green the whole time **because it
calls `deleteBrand()` directly and never touches the button.** Now uses `escJs` (which exists for
exactly this) + the v639 tri-state ownership. Verified by execution on 4 names incl. quotes and markup.
**FIXED #2 — STORED XSS IN CONTENT THEMES.** `${c}` interpolated raw into `innerHTML`, and the × handler
escaped only single quotes. `communities` is NOT purely user-typed — `spDraftFromCrawl` and onboarding
fill it from LLM output read off a third-party site, and `crawlValueOk`'s markup blocklist covers
script/style/div/img but **not svg/iframe/details/math/object**. `<svg onload=…>` is 21 chars, passes
the 80-char list cap, reads as one odd topic among ten in the review sheet, then fires on every
Settings open. Same class as the v639 Questions fix, found in the same sweep.
**FIXED #3 — EVERY SETTINGS EDIT PERMANENTLY DELETED THE COACH CONVERSATION.** `settingsToBrand` wrote
`voiceCoachMessages: bvState.messages || []` unconditionally; `voice_extra` is REPLACED WHOLESALE on
save; and **`brandToSettings` never reads that key back — it is the only voice_extra key that does not
round-trip** (dayScenes, paaKeywords, brandLogo, founderPhoto all do). `bvState.messages` starts `[]`.
So: open the app, do NOT open the Assistant, change anything — **even just expanding an accordion,
which calls `saveSettings()`** — and the brand's whole transcript was overwritten with `[]`. The write
is now non-destructive (preserve the stored history when memory is empty).
**FIXED #4 — THE MONEY PATH COULD DIE AS A BARE 504.** `checkout-confirm`, `create-checkout` and
`create-portal-session` build `https.request` to api.stripe.com with **no socket timeout at all**, so a
Stripe stall never settles and the platform kills the function at maxDuration 30 with no body and no
log. `stripe-webhook.js` has had `timeout: 15000` since it was written — these three never got it.
Worst case is checkout-confirm: it runs AFTER the card is charged and is the only caller of `setPlan`,
so a hang left the customer paid, on `free`, with nothing recorded. All three now 15s + a logged,
honest rejection. Verified against a socket that accepts and goes quiet.
**▶▶ BOTH OUTPUT-QUALITY MECHANISMS ARE NOW FIXED (this is the answer to the months-old complaint).**
**(a) POSITION — the brand block moved to the END.** It sat at ~2% of the prompt, and from there to
the winners at ~86% there was **not one brand-specific character**. Now: opener + task params ->
craft rules -> BRAND (profile, learning, winners) -> a one-line precedence statement -> JSON schema.
**MEASURED before/after on an identical populated-brand fixture, by reconstructing the REAL assembled
prompt (stubbing only the LLM and auth): BRAND PROFILE starts at 1.8% -> 67.4%; brand markers in the
final quarter 1 of 8 -> 5 of 8; prompt length 19,948 -> 19,946 chars — a 2-char delta, which is the
proof it is a pure re-order and not a content change.**
**(b) PROVENANCE — the app no longer tells the model its own output is the brand's truest voice.**
`approvedWinnersBlock` called every winner "the truest statement of the voice… it beats every
description of the voice above" — but those rows are text THIS APP generated and "approved" is one
tap. Now the block splits: a post the user REWROTE is labelled **"THE BRAND'S OWN WORDS — the user
took our draft and rewrote it into this"** and keeps the outranking claim; a merely-approved post is
labelled **"a floor, not a target… they were written by this same system, so matching them too
closely just repeats it"** and is explicitly demoted below the brand description. Provenance is
detected two ways: a new `idea.humanEdited` flag set in `tvCaptureEdits` (which already writes the
user's wording into the idea), plus a **retroactive match against stored `edit_signals.after` text**
so it works on the library that already exists.
**THE PART THAT ALMOST SHIPPED BROKEN, caught by a gate:** on the LEAN path — the default —
`approvedExamples` are hydrated SERVER-side from the `ideas` table, so the client-side ranking would
never have reached the model. `edit_signals` is localStorage-only, which is exactly the category the
lean payload exists to carry (like hand-taught trends), so `humanEditedTitles` (titles only, capped
at 8) now travels with the request and `_brandctx.approvedExamplesFrom` marks + hoists them.
Behaviourally verified 5/5 server-side incl. the no-titles case behaving exactly as before.
**TWO GATES WENT RED FOR THE RIGHT REASONS AND BOTH WERE THE GATE'S FAULT:** `lean-payload` compares
client-built vs server-hydrated context field-for-field and correctly caught the new `edited` key
diverging — that is what surfaced the server-path problem above. And `lean-payload-all` asserted
`/APPROVED WINNERS/`, so it went red purely because the heading was reworded — **an assertion coupled
to copy punishes improving the copy** (the v619 lesson, again). It now asserts the winner's BODY
reaches the prompt and accepts either heading; mutation-tested by making the block return '' — caught.
**(c) TWO TEMPLATE LOCK-INS REMOVED (Jörgen: "this needs to be fixed probably").**
**The statement mould.** The format spec read *"A bold standalone claim for a text graphic — **Alex
Hormozi style**"*, declared *"the shape is ALWAYS setup + payoff"*, and gave two of his sentences as
worked examples — applied identically to a deadpan supplement brand, a B2B freight forwarder and a
bakery. Every brand's statements came out of one named creator's mould. Now: written in THIS brand's
voice, must land for a stranger with zero context, setup-then-payoff offered as *one* good shape
rather than the only one, plus an explicit *"do NOT reach for a motivational-speaker cadence unless
that is genuinely this brand's voice"*. The useful constraints (never one line, 2-5 sentences,
15-40 words, the anti-cryptic-metaphor rule) are all kept — they are brand-neutral.
**The Q&A quota.** `qnaInstruction` fired on `!isSeed && count >= 3` — **nothing about the brand and
nothing about Content Mix** — and demanded *"MANDATORY: at least 30% MUST use qna, never skip it"*.
`renderIdeas` then hides any format whose mix weight is 0, so a user who switched Q&A off still had
~40% of every batch generated, billed and thrown away unseen. The quota is now derived from the
`gaps` the client actually sent, which v569 already mix-filters (`_genFormats` = formats with weight
> 0) — so it needs no new payload field and cannot drift from the mix. No qna gap => no instruction
at all. Behaviourally verified 6/6: off-in-mix produces nothing; on produces a proportionate ask;
one gap asks for 1 not 3; many gaps cap at a third; single-post and seed requests are never forced.
Wording softened from "MANDATORY … never skip it" to "should … the brand's content mix asks for it".

**STILL OPEN on output quality (measured by the audit, not yet done):** the tone instruction
contradicts itself (the brand block says hold ONE voice, the JSON schema field says `"one of the tone
options"`, and the schema wins on position); main Generate Ideas lane still sends no `approveReason` and no `edit_signals` while the auto-refill
lane sends both; `sharpen` is forbidden from adding any brand specifics so it can only subtract;
`emphasis` is requested by the schema and silently dropped by `cleanIdeas`.

**▶ THE OUTPUT-QUALITY FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST (audited, NOT yet fixed — needs Jörgen's call).**
The agent reconstructed the REAL assembled generate-ideas prompt (24,049 chars, populated brand) and
measured it. Two mechanisms explain a complaint that has survived every field-coverage fix:
**(a) POSITION.** The brand block sits at 1.5–26%. From 30% to 86% — **13,465 chars, 56% of everything
the model reads — there is not one brand-specific character.** The last quarter, the recency zone, is
**79.5% house rules.** `rulePrecedence()` is a 667-char sentence at 83% asking the model to re-rank
something it read 20,000 chars earlier. FIX: move the brand block + winners + learningContext to the
END, immediately before the JSON schema. Pure re-order, reversible.
**(b) THE APP FEEDS THE MODEL ITS OWN OUTPUT AS "THE TRUEST STATEMENT OF THE VOICE."** `_brain.js:61`
labels approvedExamples exactly that, and says it "beats every description of the voice above."
`getApprovedExamples` selects `status filming|done` — **every one of those rows is text this app
generated**, and "approved" is one tap. No filter for ideas the user actually rewrote. So the
strongest-weighted, latest-positioned voice evidence is Grok's own prior output, fed back to Grok and
ranked above the human-written fields. **Each cycle converges on the model's average, and it gets
WORSE the longer the app is used** — which is exactly the shape of a months-long complaint that does
not respond to plumbing fixes. Measured: 1,234 chars of AI-written exemplar at 86% vs 210 chars of
human `exampleContent` at 22%. FIX: rank by human provenance — `edit_signals` already records
`{field,before,after}` per manual edit; prefer approved ideas carrying an edit signal and render them
as "the user rewrote our draft into this".
**ALSO FOUND, NOT YET FIXED (ranked):** a first purchase is granted ONLY by the browser redirect —
there is **no `checkout.session.completed` webhook handler**, so a closed tab on return = charged and
still on free, with nothing to retry it; the trial allowance resets on the 1st of the month so a
7-day trial started late in the month gets 300 credits; `usageThisPeriod` reads usage rows with **no
LIMIT**, so PostgREST's 1000-row cap means the agency 2500 limit can never fire; the tone instruction
contradicts itself (brand says hold ONE voice, the JSON schema field says "one of the tone options",
and the schema wins on position); statements are hardcoded **"Alex Hormozi style"** for every brand;
30% of every batch is forced to Q&A **regardless of Content Mix**, then hidden by the mix filter —
generated, billed and thrown away; `sharpen` is registered in neither the credit nor the cost table;
`meme.js` worst case is 95s against a 60s budget; the main Generate Ideas lane sends **no manual edits
and no approve reasons** while the auto-refill lane sends both; `emphasis` is requested by the schema
and silently dropped by `cleanIdeas`; `STRIPE-SETUP.md` still says $49/$99 and lists every plan limit
wrong — it is the checklist for the live-mode flip.

## ▶▶ v639 — the top 3 open items from the parallel round, all PROVEN, all behaviourally verified.
**#1 STORED XSS IN QUESTIONS — closed.** `renderPAASection` interpolated `${q.question}` and
`${q.keyword}` UNESCAPED into `innerHTML`, straight from SerpAPI/Google via `people-also-ask.js`,
while every neighbouring renderer in the file uses `escHtml`. Supabase tokens live in localStorage
and there is no CSP, so a poisoned PAA result was a session takeover. Now escaped; verified the
payload renders inert and ordinary text stays readable. **CORRECTION to the agent's report: `q.source`
was NOT vulnerable** — it is a ternary producing a fixed string ('Related' / 'Google PAA'). Checked
before changing it rather than escaping on trust.
**#2 A DOUBLE-TAP ON THE BRAND SWITCHER CORRUPTED THE OTHER BRAND'S DATA — closed.** `switchBrand`
guards every await with `myToken !== _switchSeq` EXCEPT its six parallel loaders, which assign to the
shared globals from inside `.then()`/`.catch()`. So A→B then quickly →C left B's handlers firing
against C: they overwrote C's remixes/notes/refs/bookmarks/history **and called
`_markListLoad(..., true)`, disarming the `_listLoaded` guard that exists to stop exactly that** — so
the next save wrote B's content into C's rows under C's brand_id. Permanent cross-brand corruption
from an ordinary correction tap, and the switcher is never locked during a switch. Every assignment is
now token-guarded. **Behaviourally verified against the extracted real code: the winning switch loads
and flags 5 lists; a superseded switch touches nothing and sets 0 flags.**
**#3 THREE GLOBALS SURVIVED THE SWITCH AND FED ONE BRAND'S CONTENT TO ANOTHER — cleared.**
`_bvLastPost` (the coach was handed brand A's post while advising on B, and persisted a note derived
from it into **B's** coach memory — contamination that outlives the session and cannot be traced
back), `_todayTabIdea` (injected into B's first Quick Post prompt as "the user just read this and
asked for a different one"), and `remixRefImage` (A's reference screenshot sent with B's remix — its
Idea Catcher twin `icRefImage` already resets, which is what showed this was an omission).
**#4 ONBOARDING'S CRAWL COULD HANG FOREVER — closed.** No AbortController, no timeout, and the step
animation deliberately holds its last frame — so a dropped connection left a brand-new user watching
"Writing it all into your brand brain…" with no error and no way out, because the only escape link
("No website yet") lives inside the form that was just hidden. The Settings deep scan calls the SAME
endpoint and has had both guards for versions. Now: 170s abort, `finally` clears the timer, the form
is restored on failure, and an abort says so honestly instead of reading as the site's fault.
**ALSO: `data = await resp.json()` ran BEFORE the `resp.ok` check**, so a gateway 502/504 (which
returns an HTML page) made a new user's first-ever action fail with «Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE
"...». Status is checked first now, and the endpoint's machine codes are translated — `limit_reached`
and `rate_limited` were being shown to users verbatim. Verified 4/4 message cases.
**STILL OPEN from the audit round:** `ideaRedoRun` has no `brandGate()` (a redo that finishes after a

the 7-day trial's `trial_ends_at` may never be written (SUSPECTED — needs one DB check:
