## ▶▶ v638 — THE PARALLEL AUDIT ROUND. 4 agents, and one of them found a WHOLE FEATURE silently losing everything.
**Jörgen: "parallel audit runs by subagents are a must from now. as other things cant find any issues."
He is right and this round proves it — four read-only agents on four never-audited surfaces
(onboarding→first post · the daily loop · silent failures in the secondary tools · multi-brand
isolation) returned more real defects in one pass than the whole preceding sequential session.**
**FIXED #1 — EVERY REMIX WAS SILENTLY DESTROYED ON RELOAD. A core daily tool, losing 100%.**
`saveRemixesToDB` mapped `sourceType`/`sourceUrl`/`sourceText`/`remixedText` — **four field names that
are set NOWHERE in the file.** What `remixContent` actually stores is the API's object:
`remixTitle`/`remixHook`/`remixScript`/`remixHashtags`/`seriesParts` + `platform`/`postUrl`/
`inputDescription`. So every remix was written as **four empty strings**; `loadRemixesFromDB` returned
a shape `remixHasContent()` has no field of, so every row was judged empty and filtered out; and
`renderRemixResults` then called `saveRemixes()` — **which deleted the empty rows. The feature cleaned
up its own evidence,** which is why this survived so long. Fixed both halves: the full object is
persisted as JSON in `remixed_text` (the content spans six fields, the table has one text column) and
the two genuinely-source columns are mapped properly; the loader rebuilds the object and falls back to
the legacy shape for pre-fix rows. **Verified by executing the REAL save + load + remixHasContent
round-trip: title/script/format/url all survive, plus a negative control proving an old empty row is
still correctly rejected (there is nothing in it to show — those are unrecoverable).**
**FIXED #2 — the ideas cleanup delete was still blind, on the path that runs on EVERY approve.**
Same shape I fixed in `_replaceBrandRows` hours earlier, still live in `_saveIdeasToDBNow`: the delete
checked only `error`, and **a PostgREST/RLS refusal resolves with ZERO ROWS AND NO ERROR.** A silent
refusal would add a full duplicate copy of the library on every approve / mark-done / dismiss. Now
`.select('id')`s and compares the removed count to the slice.
**FIXED #3 — Sharpen and Viral Twist left a duplicate that resurrected on reload. Found independently
by TWO agents.** Both rewrite `title`, but `_saveIdeasToDBNow` drops superseded rows strictly BY
TITLE — the old title is no longer in the written set, so its row is never captured, and
`loadIdeasFromDB` dedups by title so two DIFFERENT titles both survive. The user sees the version they
thought they replaced sitting next to the new one, and it accumulates. `ideaRedoRun` already did this
correctly; these two never got it. New shared `_dropRenamedIdeaRow(old,new)` — behaviourally verified
4/4 including "another idea still uses the old title -> do NOT delete".
**MY OWN GATE WENT RED FOR THE RIGHT REASON, TWICE, AND BOTH WERE THE GATE'S FAULT:** (a)
`data-integrity`'s stub Supabase had no `.select()` on a delete query, so the new chain deleted
nothing in simulation — fixed the stub to model reality AND added a `silentRefuseDelete` mode so the
gate can now PROVE the row-count check catches an RLS refusal; (b) its `extractFn` counted braces
naively and died on `charAt(0) === '{'` — **a brace inside a string literal** — reporting "unbalanced
braces" for valid code. Fixed to skip strings, templates, comments and escapes; verified against 4
hostile cases. **My own ad-hoc extractor hit the identical trap minutes earlier. Naive brace matching
over a 1.3MB file with string literals in it WILL lie to you.**
**STILL OPEN from this round, ranked (NOT yet fixed):** onboarding's crawl can hang forever — no
AbortController, no timeout, and the only escape link is hidden during the crawl (the Settings deep
scan of the same endpoint HAS both, so it is an oversight); a **stored XSS in Questions** —
`${q.question}`/`${q.source}` interpolated unescaped into `innerHTML` from SerpAPI data while every
neighbouring renderer uses `escHtml`; `switchBrand`'s six parallel loaders assign in `.then()` with
**no `myToken` check**, so a superseded switch clobbers the winning brand's lists AND flags them
loaded, disarming the `_listLoaded` guard, then saves them under the wrong brand_id; `_bvLastPost` and
`_todayTabIdea` are never cleared on brand switch, so the coach is fed brand A's post while advising
on B and persists a note derived from it into B's memory; `ideaRedoRun` has no `brandGate()`;
`remixRefImage` never resets (its Idea Catcher twin does).

## ▶▶ v637-backend (api.fcc11d08) — THE 4s SUPABASE CUT HIT A USER, NOT JUST THE CRONS.
**Read the logs after deploying v637 and found a NEW one, on a user-facing path:**
`/api/brand-voice-chat` — `store._req TIMEOUT after 4000ms — GET /auth/v1/user`, 09:34 today. That is
somebody asking the coach a question and getting an error, because the AUTH check was cut at 4s. The
endpoint has **maxDuration 90**. Same structural flaw as the crons, one layer closer to the user.
(The two cron timeouts have NOT recurred since the per-caller fix — that half is holding.)
**WHY THE DEFAULT WAS STUCK AT 4s:** the floor is set by the tightest endpoint that can reach
Supabase, and five of them — `checkout-confirm`, `create-checkout`, `create-portal-session`,
`stripe-webhook`, `usage` — reached it while **ABSENT from vercel.json's functions map**, so they ran
on Vercel's ~10s platform default. That is the same blind spot that hid `extract-article.js` from the
v606 audit and cost v627 a second miss. **Declaring them at 30s lifted the floor 10s → 20s**, and the
shared default doubled **4s → 8s** — which fixes brand-voice-chat and every other user-facing endpoint
at once, without touching them individually. Declaring them is also strictly safer on its own: an
undeclared endpoint that overruns dies as a bare platform 504 with no body and no log.
**THE NUMBER IS NOW COMPUTED, NOT CHOSEN.** `timeout-budgets.mjs` (G38) derives the floor from
vercel.json and fails if the default no longer fits — verified by mutation: 11000ms is refused, naming
`health.js at 20s` and showing the arithmetic. Both stale "WHY 4s" comments were rewritten rather than
left to mislead the next reader. **Do not raise this by hand and hope; the gate is the authority.**

## ▶▶ v637 — THE QA RUN SAID "THE APP DOES NOT WORK TODAY". IT WAS WRONG — but it found 2 REAL data bugs, both mine.
**RUN: 13 pass / 11 fail / 17 blocked / 0 hard errors / 229 BLOCKED TAPS.** Verdict: chain breaks at
pipeline. **That verdict is a FALSE NEGATIVE and the evidence is inside the run itself.** The new
`proof-taptargets` keys settle it: **`assistantCloseWorks: WORKS — x dismissed it`** next to
**`assistantClose: COVERED BY OFFSCREEN`**. The × is FINE. It is reported unclickable because
`.bv-overlay` is `position:fixed` while the evidence screenshot grows the page to full content height
(the report logs "captured page height changed ~204%" and "~299%"), so the driver's coordinates land
off-screen. Same root cause as v593's mascot bug, whose fix (`viewportShot:true`) was applied to the
`shrimp` feature ONLY — which is exactly why `shrimp` passed and 17 other features drowned.
**THE CASCADE: shrimp auto-pops (v582) → its "Answer" opens the Assistant → killOverlays did NOT close
the Assistant mid-feature (deliberate, the `assistant` feature needs it open) → it covered everything
for the rest of the run.** ONE harness limitation produced ~15 of the 28 non-passing results.
**HARNESS FIX: killOverlays now closes the Assistant unless `window._qaKeepAssistant`** (set only by
the `assistant` feature, cleared in clearLeftoverModals like every other _qaKeep* flag). A harness that
cannot dismiss an overlay must never be allowed to report that as an app failure.
**REAL BUG 1 — NOTEBOOK NOTES ARE DUPLICATING IN PRODUCTION, and it is my v634 code.**
`reload-persistence` measured **notes 74 → 149** across a reload. `_replaceBrandRows` deletes the
superseded rows with `.delete().eq(...).in('id', oldIds)` and checked only `error` — but **a
PostgREST/RLS refusal does NOT throw and does NOT set `error`; it resolves with zero rows.** This file
documents that trap and I wrote the delete without a `.select('id')` anyway. So cleanup silently
removed nothing, the insert had already written a full new copy, and every save left the old set
behind — 74 → 149 → 299 → … Fixed: the delete now `.select('id')`s and compares the removed count to
the chunk, treats a short delete as failure, and **says so to the user** ("Saved — but the old copy
couldn't be cleared, so you may see duplicates") instead of leaving it for a QA reload to find.
Affects every list routed through `_replaceBrandRows` (ideas, remixes, refs, bookmarks, prompt
history, notebook). **JÖRGEN: your notebook currently holds duplicates — they are safe to delete.**
**REAL BUG 2 — you could not delete your own brand. Also mine, also v634.** `deleteBrand` refused
up front on `!_brandIsOwned(brandId)`, and that helper returns **false for a brand it has not
loaded**, which is indistinguishable from someone else's brand. So a brand created this session got
"You can't delete a brand that was shared with you" — about the user's own brand. v634's own note says
"the client flag is NOT load-bearing: the server-side `user_id` filter is", and the code made it
load-bearing. Fixed with a THREE-state `_brandOwnership()` → mine / theirs / **unknown**; only
`theirs` refuses, `unknown` falls through to the authoritative `.eq('user_id', …).select('id')`, which
already returns an accurate message. Behaviourally verified 4/4 against the real source.
**LESSON, and it is the same one twice: a boolean that collapses "no" and "don't know" WILL eventually
refuse something legitimate — and a delete whose failure mode is "0 rows, no error" must verify the
rows, not the error.**
**CONFIRMED WORKING LIVE by this run (do not re-chase):** the v635 brain meters — `assistant` read
**"78% · 18 of 23 pieces filled"** (23, not the old hardcoded 14) and `proof-brain-meters` returned
`fieldCount: 23`, `oneList: WORKS`, `deepTracked: WORKS`; `proof-data-safety` returned all six WORKS;
`proof-escaping` 12/12; `proof-actions` FIXED (markDone 41→42); preflight clean on all four checks
including the new `+api.` backend stamp. **STILL OPEN: a junk brand "QA TEMP BRAND 37513" is in the
database (the probe created it, then the delete bug stopped its own cleanup) — delete it in Supabase.
Dark mode: "Make it better" renders dark ink on a dark fill. Sticky header clips scrolled post text.**

## ▶▶ v636-backend (api.8b41f40d) — THE 4s SUPABASE CUT WAS FIRING ON THE CRONS, and a "fixed" deploy check was not fixed.
**Read the production logs first, as always — and they had three real hits: the v628 4s Supabase timeout
firing on `send-daily`'s `job_heartbeats` write (x2, Aug 28) and `pull-trends-cron`'s approved-titles read
(x1, Aug 29).** Both endpoints run under **maxDuration 300**. A 4s ceiling inside a 300s budget.
**THE HEARTBEAT ONE IS THE WORST, because it breaks the monitor v627 just built:** the write failed, so
`/api/health` reported the cron as never-observed even though it HAD run — the exact false alarm the
never-run-vs-unreadable distinction exists to prevent, now caused by our own timeout.
**MEASURED BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING (and the measurement changed the answer):** my instinct was "4s is
absurdly tight, raise it." Wrong for half the app. The tightest callers — `stripe-webhook`,
`checkout-confirm` — make ~2 sequential Supabase calls inside Vercel's **~10s default** (they are absent
from the functions map), so 4s×2+1s = 9s barely fits and **raising it globally would trade a LOGGED
timeout for a SILENT platform kill on the money path.** The real defect is structural: **the timeout is
one shared constant while the budget is per-endpoint.**
**FIX = per-caller override, conservative default:** `store.setRequestBudget(ms)` / `usage.setRequestBudget(ms)`
(clamped 4s–60s so a typo cannot reintroduce the unbounded hang), and the two crons raise themselves to
**20s** at handler start. Module state in a Vercel function is per-function-instance — store.js inside
send-daily's container is not the copy inside stripe-webhook's — so this cannot leak across endpoints.
Behaviourally verified: default 4s, cron 20s, clamps both directions, garbage ignored.
**THE FLOOR IS NOW COMPUTED, NOT REMEMBERED (G38).** It had been worked out by hand FOUR times — v606 and
v627 each shipped an endpoint on the ~10s default without noticing, v628 computed it, and v637 had to
recompute it because v629 deleted the two endpoints that set it. `timeout-budgets.mjs` now walks every
endpoint that can reach Supabase (directly or via `_requireUser`/`_brandctx`), takes the tightest budget
as the floor, and fails if the shared default no longer fits — naming the constraining endpoint and
whether it is undeclared. Mutation-proven, including that the floor MOVES when you give that endpoint a
budget (so it computes rather than hardcodes). Current: 32 endpoints reach Supabase, floor is
`checkout-confirm.js` at 10s (undeclared), 4000ms fits (needs 9000ms).
**AND A "FIXED" ITEM THAT WAS NOT (G39): backend deploys were unverifiable.** The silent-skip checklist
says backend-deploy currency is solved because the stamp writes `api/_build.js` — but **the stamp hashed
app.html ALONE**, so a backend-only change produced an identical value and `curl /api/health` could not
distinguish old backend code from new. Today's work is backend-only; it would have shipped unprovable.
**Split the two questions, because they ARE different questions:** `sw.js BUILD` still hashes app.html
alone ("does the phone need the new app?" — folding the backend in would push a needless ~196KB download
to every phone on every backend deploy, the exact slow-line stall v309 fixed), while `api/_build.js` now
appends a hash of all 44 api files. Proven: a backend-only edit moves the server stamp and leaves the
phone stamp untouched.
**MY OWN GATE WAS CORRUPTING THE FILE IT TESTED — found by mutating it.** `build-stamp.mjs` appends a
positive-control comment to app.html, then called `process.exit(1)` on failure. **process.exit does NOT
run finally blocks**, so a red run left `<!--unlazy-control-->` appended to app.html and the next stamp
baked the corrupted hash in. It actually happened during this session (app.html briefly stamped
`v636-cdf16b72`); restored byte-exactly. Failures now throw, and it is verified that app.html is
byte-identical after a deliberately-failed run. **Rule: a gate that mutates a file to test it must
restore in `finally`, and must never `process.exit()` from inside the try.**
**ALSO THIS ROUND — G37, the deletion-damage gate.** v633-v636 removed three whole features and ~55KB of
app.html. Parsing proves the file is still valid JavaScript; it says NOTHING about whether a button still
calls a function that exists or a nav entry still leads to a view that exists — both break at TAP TIME,
in front of the user. `no-dangling-refs.mjs` measures it: **308 inline handlers all resolve, 7 switchView
targets all have markup, 0 NUL bytes.** So the day's deletions left no dead buttons. Mutation-tested 3
ways (point a button at a deleted function, point nav at a removed view, reintroduce a raw NUL byte).
Deliberately does NOT check `getElementById` targets — most elements are created at render time, so a
static check there is mostly false positives, and a gate that cries wolf gets ignored.
**SIM UPDATED IN THE SAME ROUND (`mobile-user.js`, local — NOT deployed).** Checked it for staleness
before spending a run on it: the deleted features were already gone from `ALL_FEATURES` (publishing
v633, blog v627, meme v444), so no false failures there. What was MISSING was coverage of the week's
most consequential fix. **New `proof-brain-meters` feature (40 total)** — a read-only PROOF probe (calls
the app's own functions, measures its own state, no vision judgement) asserting: all three completeness
meters derive from ONE list (`getBrainStats().facets === brainFieldKeys().length`), **all 7 deep fields
are tracked**, `BRAIN_CHIP_ORDER` is gone, the copy never claims "full/100%" while fields are missing,
and the Master Prompt / Custom Instructions UI is gone. **Verified against the source before shipping
it: `getBrandContext` returns 29 keys, minus 6 derived = 23 tracked, and all 7 deep fields are present
— so the probe should report `fieldCount = 23 fields` + `deepTracked = WORKS` on this build, which is
the baseline a future regression breaks.** DELIBERATELY READ-ONLY: blanking a field to watch the meter
drop is stronger evidence, but a debounced brand save could persist the blank — destroying real brand
data to test a meter is a bad trade. Also fixed two stale references (a comment describing the deleted
Custom Instructions accordion, and a dead `closeAutopost` call from the removed publishing feature).
**MY OWN MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG TWICE while verifying this** — the first regex returned 0 keys for
`getBrandContext` (silently, so it "proved" the deep fields were missing), and my simulation script
printed `deepTracked = WORKS` on a hardcoded final line regardless of the result. Both caught by
re-reading the script rather than the output. **A verification script needs verifying as much as the
code it checks — if it cannot fail, it proved nothing.** A third check (resolving every function the
taps call) was written, found to match comment prose and DOM built-ins, and DROPPED rather than shipped
noisy — G37 already covers dead handlers properly.
**SECOND SIM ADDITION — `proof-data-safety` (41 features), covering the reachable v634/v635 fixes that
had NO test** (Jörgen: "we should get the maximum out of the run so we know all works what you fixed").
Two are TRUE BEHAVIOURAL checks — `bvFieldAllowed('targetAudiance')` must refuse the model-typo field
that used to update the ring and say "Saved ✓" while `settingsToBrand` dropped it forever, and
`spBrandPalette()` must return the brand's colour rather than the shrimp default (every user's
split-screen rendered in cream/ink/lavender for months because it read colours off `getBrandContext`,
which never carried them). Four are WIRING checks that read the function's own source at runtime and
SAY SO rather than overclaiming: switchBrand still flushes the debounced save before switching (or an
in-flight edit lands on the WRONG brand), saveNotebookToDB keeps its never-loaded guard + write-before-
delete, pullReviews still validates and shows the review sheet, and no rule-saving path truncates
`coachNotes` on save. **Verified against the real source before shipping: 6/6 assertions pass on this
build, including TWO NEGATIVE CONTROLS proving the cap regex can actually fail and does not match the
comment prose.** Also confirmed `targetAudience` really is a `defaultSettings()` key (33 keys), so the
whitelist probe cannot false-fail.
**A STALE TEST WOULD HAVE REPORTED MY OWN FIX AS A BUG:** the `assistant` feature still demanded the
ring read "N of 14 pieces filled" — v635 made that total 23. It now reads whatever the app computes and
only fails on nonsense (filled > total). **That is the harness-breaks-its-own-test failure that has
cost this project whole rounds before; check every hardcoded expectation after changing a number.**
**THE `slice(-25)` LESSON, THIRD TIME IN ONE DAY:** three separate greps "found" the removed 25-line
truncation still present in `bvAcceptSuggestion`/`brainKeepRule`/`nbSaveAsRule`. All three hits were
the COMMENT describing its removal. Brace-matched bodies + an executable-pattern regex
(`coachNotes\s*=\s*<ident>\s*\.slice\s*\(`) showed the fix is real and live. **Assert on the
executable pattern, never a bare string — prose about a fix matches a grep for the bug.**
**REDUNDANCY CHECK (Jörgen: "the sim is doing one check 4 separate times at least with Assistant").
He was right that something was duplicated, though narrower than it looked: TEN features open
Settings/Brain/Assistant, but most only START there and test different things (dark-mode walks 8
screens, tour tests the tour, shrimp tests the mascot). Reading the actual test CONTENT found exactly
ONE true duplicate: `settings` and `settings-deep` had identical taps (`toggleSettings()`) and
settings-deep is a strict superset — it expands four sections AND does the change-a-value-confirm-toast
check that was all `settings` did. The only unique content in `settings` was anti-false-positive
framing (the gear force-opens by design; the AI Engine control does not navigate), which is guidance,
not a test — folded into settings-deep, then `settings` deleted. 41 -> 40 features, ~8 driver actions
and one screenshot saved, and one fewer chance of leaving the Settings overlay open to contaminate the
next feature. Verified: CRITICAL_PATH does not reference it, nothing else names it, and the cross-run
delta iterates the CURRENT results (so a feature present in the previous run but removed since is
simply never visited — no crash, no phantom "fixed" entry).
**NOT redundant, checked and kept:** quick-post vs quick-post-formats (the first is on the critical
path, the second walks 3 formats), remix vs remix-sources (quick lane vs article/YouTube lanes),
pipeline vs pipeline-tools (critical path vs teleprompter/B-roll), ideas vs idea-actions (generate/
approve/filters vs Sharpen/Viral Twist/Redo), brain vs proof-brain-meters (editability vs the meters).
**LESSON: "same starting screen" is NOT the same as "same test" — judge redundancy by reading the test
content, not by grouping on the taps.**
**WHAT THE SIM STILL CANNOT REACH (do not read a clean run as "everything is verified"): the crons
(today's Supabase timeout fix, send-daily's brand context, trend prefTexts) — they do not run in a
browser session; the money path — deliberately blocked by the harness's own safety rules; real filming
and the video render — headless Chromium has no camera; and the server-side ownership checks. Those are
verified by the production logs, the billing-honesty gate, and Jörgen filming one take, respectively.**
**PREFLIGHT NOW CATCHES THE STALE BACKEND:** because the server stamp gained its `+api.<hash>` half,
running the sim before deploying will correctly HALT with "STALE BACKEND", which it could not detect
before today.
**app.html is UNCHANGED this round** (APP_VERSION stays v636) — backend + scripts only, which is precisely
the case the new server stamp exists to make provable. **35/36 gates green** (only `bug-scan.mjs`, whose
remaining hits are the known false positives).

## ▶▶ v636 — THE "MASTER PROMPT" GOOGLE DOC REMOVED — it was OUTRANKING the brand brain.
Jörgen spotted it in Settings and asked whether it was even needed ("or it can even be an obsticle
probably"). It was worse than an obstacle. `_brain.js` appended the synced doc **labelled
"MASTER BRAND DOCUMENT (primary reference for voice, product knowledge, angles)", LAST in the
prompt — the strongest position — up to 4000 chars.** So a stale linked Google Doc silently
outranked the 23 curated brand fields above it. **Two sources of truth for brand voice, rigged so
the LESS-maintained one wins** — the same defect class as v612/v625/v635, and the app's own help
text already admitted it ("Optional — most brands never need this. Your Brand Voice fields and
Voice Memory already steer the AI").
**REMOVED, all of it:** the `_brain.js` render block (the critical one — proven: a sentinel doc no
longer appears in the prompt and the brand fields still do), `_brandctx` hydration, the Settings
"Custom Instructions" accordion (it contained ONLY this), `syncMasterPrompt`, all settings plumbing
(defaults / settingsToBrand / brandToSettings / getBrandContext / BRAIN_DERIVED_KEYS / the crawl
prefill list / the getBrainStats freshness read), and **a mascot tip that actively told users to go
set one up** ("Pro tip: link a Master Prompt Google Doc… Set it up").
**TWO THINGS FOUND WHILE REMOVING IT:** (1) **`remix.js` made a LIVE Google Docs fetch on every
remix** (`fetchGoogleDoc`) for a local variable **nothing in that file ever read** — the content
only ever reached the model via `fullBrandBlock`. Dead compute plus a third-party network call per
remix. (2) The `fetch-gdoc` branch in `crawl-brand.js` carried an **SSRF-guard BYPASS**
(`if (action !== 'fetch-gdoc')` skipped `assertPublicHttpUrl`) — removing the branch removes the
bypass. `extractDocId` deleted with its only caller. `crawlgdoc` LEFT REGISTERED in `_usage.js` but
marked retired: removing the key would make a stray caller default to 1 credit as an unknown action.
**DB columns `master_prompt_url` / `voice_extra.masterPromptContent` are NOT dropped** — nothing
reads or writes them now, so existing rows are inert. No SQL needed.
**SIX RATCHETS CORRECTLY WENT RED and were updated, not silenced:** one-brand-renderer (sentinel
27/27), brand-prompt (ZKEY_MASTERDOC), lean-payload-all, backend-hardening (fetchGoogleDoc timeout
+ byte cap + the 8000 cap), spend-cap (the gdoc branch's own logUsage), harness-fixes (the
'advanced' accordion — now asserts it is GONE rather than what it contained). **That is the gates
working: a feature removal should turn every gate that asserted the feature red.**
**MY OWN MISTAKE, THREE TIMES IN ONE ROUND:** I removed lines by filtering on a substring, which
tore the middle out of multi-line expressions and left `spend-cap`, `brand-prompt` and
`backend-hardening` with syntax errors. **Never delete source lines by substring match — read the
surrounding expression and replace the whole statement.** Also: my first spend-cap guard tested for
`fetch-gdoc` anywhere in the file, which matched the REMOVED-comment I had just written; it now
tests for `action === 'fetch-gdoc'`, i.e. real code rather than prose about it.

## ▶▶ v635 — WHY THE OUTPUT FELT GENERIC: THE APP SAID "BRAIN FULL" WITH 7 FIELDS EMPTY.
The OUTPUT side was already proven (23/23 settings fields reach every generator via
`fullBrandBlock`, gated by `one-brand-renderer.mjs`). So this audit went at the INPUT side, and
found the likely answer to the months-old "the output isn't good enough".
**#1 THE BIG ONE — three completeness meters, all disagreeing, NONE counting the deep fields.**
Settings `getBrandCompleteness` (13 checks), the Assistant ring `getBrainStats` (14), and the
"still to learn" chips `BRAIN_CHIP_ORDER` (11) — while `fullBrandBlock` reads **23**. All three
omitted **originStory, socialProof, channels, visualStyle, webMentions, categoryGripes,
reviewInsights**; the ring also omitted tones + communities. So a user hit **"14 of 14 · 100% ·
your brand brain is full. Every post now sounds like you"** with seven whole sections of the model's
brand profile blank — **and the app stopped asking for exactly the fields that carry a brand's
specifics rather than its adjectives.** Measured on a 14-shallow/7-deep fixture: before 13/13=100%
and 14/14=100% and ZERO chips asked; after **16/23=70%** with all 7 named. Now all three derive from
ONE list built off `getBrandContext()` minus derived keys (`brainFieldKeys()`), so it CANNOT drift —
proven by adding a field to getBrandContext and watching 23→24 with no meter edited. `BRAIN_CHIP_ORDER`
deleted. Copy never says "complete"/"full" unless it is. `brandBrainBare()` re-anchored to
`coreFilled<=4` to preserve its v613 calibration exactly (verified both directions).
**`_brainFacets()` had THREE HARDCODED `true`s** (Weekly themes / What the feed rewards / AEO) and
keyed the tone facet off `exampleContent||coachNotes||tagline` instead of `settings.tones` — a
completeness display that could not show incomplete. On an empty brand it lit 3 facets; now 0.
**#2 THE DAILY PING GENERATED FROM HALF A BRAIN.** `send-daily` hand-rolled
`select=brand_name,voice_extra` — the JSONB half only — so every COLUMN was missing: **usps,
targetAudience, tones, communities, competitors, bannedTopics, website, tagline** (+ approvedExamples
and learnedSignals, which aren't in voice_extra at all). And the CRON path never sends `brandId`, so
`_brandctx` hydration couldn't fire either. **The one post the app pushes unprompted every day, under
"Today's post is ready", was the most off-voice thing it produced — no tone rules, no audience, no
product facts, no banned-topic guardrail.** Now uses `loadBrandContext(brandId, {trusted:true})` —
that flag exists for exactly this caller, which already verified ownership via v634's
`authorizedBrandId()`. Measured: brand block 1224 → 1819 chars, missing fields 8 → 0.
**#3 "Pull customer reviews" OVERWROTE hand-written text with no gate** — no `crawlValueOk`, no
`openBrainReview` sheet, no empty-check, while the copy directly above it promised "you review
everything before it saves to your brand brain". Every neighbouring fill path had all three.
**#4 BRAND COLOURS HAVE NEVER REACHED THE VIDEO RENDERER.** `spBrandPalette`/`spBrollVars` read
`bc.brandColorPrimary` off `getBrandContext()`, which never carried it → `hex()` always null → the
early return always fired. Every user's split-screen video rendered in Content Shrimp's own
cream/ink/lavender regardless of their colours. Fixed by reading `settings` directly (the Carousel
Maker already did) rather than adding dead payload to every generate request.
**#5 the Assistant's "Apply" could write a field name that goes nowhere** — `settings[s.field] = value`
with no whitelist, so a model typo (`targetAudiance`) updated the ring and said "Saved ✓" while
`settingsToBrand`'s fixed key set silently dropped it forever. Also tones weren't validated against
`TONE_OPTIONS`, so an off-list tone showed as nothing-selected in the grid, **could not be removed**
(toggleTone only handles known ids), and was still rendered to the model as a voice law.
**#6 Voice Memory silently truncated to 25 lines — and it was FOUR sites, not the two reported**
(`bvAcceptSuggestion`, `brainAutoDistill`, plus `brainKeepRule` and `nbSaveAsRule`, found by a
control check). A user with 26+ hand-written rules lost the oldest on a background timer while the
toast said "learned N new things". Now nothing the user wrote is ever evicted; only auto-rules are
capped, and it says when it skips. Verified 30+3 = 33 kept vs 25 before.
**#7** a debounced edit was lost on brand switch (`switchBrand` never called `flushBrandSave()`,
so the pending timer wrote brand A's keystrokes into brand B's row). **#8** Founder/Creator claimed
"Used in Statement posts" and was read by nothing — `bvFounderName()` was guessing a name out of the
login email while a correct one sat two taps away; now it prefers `settings.founderName`.
**REFUTED FROM THE BRIEF (recorded so it is not re-chased):** the chip list did NOT omit
`avoidWords`/`exampleContent` — both were present. It omitted brandName, website, coachNotes, tones,
communities and the 7 deep fields.
**ROUND-TRIP TABLE PROVEN CLEAN:** all 23 model-facing fields are editable → written by
`settingsToBrand` → read by `brandToSettings` → exposed by `getBrandContext` → rendered by
`fullBrandBlock`. No voice field the user types is dropped. `voice_extra` is replaced wholesale on
save and NOTHING server-side writes it (grep-verified), so that is safe.

## ▶▶ v634 — AUTH/ACCESS AUDITED FOR THE FIRST TIME. TWO LIVE CROSS-ACCOUNT HOLES, BOTH OUTSIDE RLS.
**RLS ITSELF IS HOLDING** — three real client queries traced end to end (`switchBrand`,
`loadIdeasFromDB`, `loadTeamData`) are protected solely by policy with no service-role shortcut, and
`security_health()` watches it daily. **Both holes were in code that runs AROUND RLS.**
**#1 LIVE READ LEAK — `push_subscriptions.brand_id` is attacker-controlled and `send-daily` reads it
with the SERVICE ROLE.** The column has NO foreign key and NO constraint; the insert policy checks
`user_id` only; and `send-daily` did not even SELECT `user_id`, so no ownership check was possible.
Any signed-in user could insert a row carrying **someone else's brand_id** and receive a daily post
generated from that brand's entire `voice_extra` brain (painPoints, productDetails, originStory,
coachNotes, masterPromptContent…), plus their post count. **The brand uuid is not secret — the
`lookup_invite` RPC is granted to `anon` and returns it to anyone holding any invite code**, so
removing the member or revoking the invite does NOT close it. It was also **completely unmetered**:
send-daily calls generate-ideas with `CRON_SECRET`, which sets `_isInternal`, and the usage gate is
`if (_user)` — false. Fixed: `user_id` selected, one `authorizedBrandId(sub)` resolves the column
through `userCanAccessBrand`, a failed check degrades to the EXISTING generic-push path, and it logs
`SECURITY —`. **Proven: pre-fix the attacker's push contained the victim's brain; fixed, 0 brand rows
read and the legit subscriber's push is byte-identical.**
**#2 LIVE DESTRUCTIVE — `deleteBrand` wiped every child row BEFORE the brand, ignored every child
error, then reported failure.** A PostgREST/RLS refusal does NOT throw — it resolves `{error}`, which
the loop never inspected. So a failed `brands` delete showed "Couldn't delete that brand" with the
library already gone, and there is no undo (the local snapshot holds status only, not content).
Worse: the × rendered on every non-active brand, that list is **own + member** brands, and members
ARE granted DELETE on the child tables — **a collaborator could wipe the owner's whole library while
the app said the delete failed.** Fixed: `brands` row deleted FIRST with `.eq('user_id', …)` +
`.select('id')` so an RLS refusal (**0 rows, NO error**) is caught; children only touched after that
is confirmed; `_owned` tagged at `loadAllBrandsFromDB` (the only place ownership is knowable — the
row objects carry no `user_id` downstream). The client flag is NOT load-bearing: the server-side
`user_id` filter is. 45/45 checks, 7 mutations, 7 caught.
**#3 `saveNotebookToDB` was the LAST delete-before-write path** and its loader turned a failed read
into `[]` — on a second device (no localStorage key) that meant the next saved note **deleted every
note in the database**. Every other list already had three protections; notebook had none. Routed
through the same `_replaceBrandRows` + `_listLoaded` helpers.
**#4 `loadBrandContext` failed OPEN** — `if (opts.userId)` meant no user id = no check, and
`generate-ideas` passes `null` on the CRON_SECRET path. Now requires `opts.userId` unless explicitly
`{trusted:true}`. **generate-ideas needed NO change: the cron path never sends `brandId`** (send-daily
posts `{count, brandContext}` only), so that branch was unreachable — verified, not assumed.
**#5 a team MEMBER could overwrite the OWNER's Gemini key** — the batch2 trigger raises on a
non-owner but **exempts the service role**, and `meme.js` gated on `userCanAccessBrand` (owner OR
member) then PATCHed through the service role. The trigger's own comment stated the assumption the
endpoint broke ("no client code ever writes this column"). save-key now requires ownership.
**DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED — PKCE.** The audit recommended `flowType:'pkce'` for magic links (fixes
email-scanner link consumption + device binding). **REJECTED for now: PKCE binds the link to the
browser that requested it, and on mobile the email app opens links in its own in-app webview — so it
could lock users out entirely.** Revisit only with a real device test.
**STILL OPEN, needs Jörgen's SQL (flagged, not silently swallowed):** brand-first deletion can leave
ORPHANED child rows — once the `brands` row is gone the child RLS predicate no longer matches, and
that denial returns 0 rows with no error, so the loop cannot even detect it. `notebook_notes` has
`brand_id not null` with NO foreign key. Complete fix = `ON DELETE CASCADE` FKs on ideas/remixes/
notebook_notes/product_refs/competitors/prompt_history/edit_signals, or a `delete_brand()`
SECURITY DEFINER RPC. Also: `push_subscriptions.brand_id` still has no FK — the app-layer check is
now the only thing holding; and `brand_invites` has **no expiry** and `redeem_invite` never checks
the caller's email, so an invite code is valid forever to anyone who has it.
**CONFIRMED APPLIED: `security-fixes-batch1b.sql` IS live** — `/api/health` returns 21/21 with
`no_permissive_brand_policies` and `no_permissive_write_policies` both ok; a missing batch1b would
light both up (brand_invites' `USING(true)`). Do not re-push it.

## ▶▶ v633 — THE WHOLE PUBLISHING SYSTEM DELETED (Jörgen: "publer is not in the game anymore,
people post directly now only … only posting directly per post stayd"; asked to confirm scope he
chose **delete everything** — he posts by hand via copy / the phone share sheet).
**THE AUDIT THAT PRECEDED IT FOUND THE APP WOULD HAVE POSTED TO EVERY ACCOUNT IN HIS WORKSPACE.**
`doPublish` sent no `accountIds`, `publish-now` forwarded `undefined`, and `publer.js` fell back to
`(creds.accounts||[]).map(a=>a.id)` — ALL of them. There was **no account picker anywhere in the
app** (grep: `accountIds` appeared zero times in app.html). One tap on "Post now" would have put the
identical caption + 1:1 image on every Instagram / Facebook page / LinkedIn / TikTok / YouTube in
that Publer workspace, **including a client's**. Not an edge case — the happy path. `publer.js`
already refused that fallback for `is_test` connections, so the danger was understood and simply
never applied to live ones. Second-worst: the dedupe key was the idea **TITLE**, and Sharpen /
Viral Rewrite rewrite the title in place — with **Sharpen and Publish in the SAME button row** —
so publish → sharpen → publish silently bypassed the unique index and posted twice.
All six were fixed and behaviourally proven (3-account fan-out refused, 0 HTTP; frozen publish key
survives a reload) — and then the whole subsystem was deleted, so those fixes are now history, not
live code. Recorded because the CLASS matters: **a "safe default" that resolves to "everything" is
the most dangerous shape in the codebase.**
**DELETED:** endpoints `publish-now`, `connections`, `autopublish`, `publish-log`, `auto-publish`;
adapters `registry/publer/wordpress/wix/webhook`; `_publish/render.js` + `_publish/fonts/`; both
dev scripts; ~55KB of app.html (60 identifiers, the publishing view, every Publish button, the
Settings Posting-Channels + Auto-Pilot rows, the publish-key ledger). 48 → **43 endpoints**.
**KEPT — deleting these breaks the app, verified by dependency map BEFORE touching anything:**
**`_publish/store.js`** (required by 14 files incl. `_brandctx`, `_requireUser`, `health`, `meme`,
`send-daily`, `pull-trends-cron`, `video-beats` — it only lives in that folder by accident of
history), **`_publish/crypto.js`** (meme.js encrypts the user's own Gemini key with it), and
**`connToken()`** — despite the `conn*` name it is NOT publishing: it backs the global fetch
wrapper that attaches auth to EVERY `/api/` call. Deleting it would have broken authentication
app-wide. Also kept the `.conn-*` CSS (shared by the bookmarks + notification overlays).
**THREE LIVE BREAKAGES THE SWEEP CAUGHT:** `health.js` still probed `/api/connections` (a 404 would
have read as a health failure), `mobile-user.js` told the QA driver a Publish control MUST exist
(would have failed every future run), and `public-exposure.mjs` required the deleted `render.js`.
**Public copy corrected:** index.html ×2 + llms.txt ×1 still advertised "one-tap publishing" and
"Auto-publish to your channels" — both now false.
**`@napi-rs/canvas` is now unused** (`_publish/render.js` was its only requirer anywhere). NOT
removed from package.json — that needs a matching package-lock update or the Vercel install
desyncs. Safe to drop in a dedicated pass.
**ORPHANED TABLES, no SQL written (Jörgen's call):** `brand_connections`, `brand_autopublish`,
`publish_jobs`. If they are dropped, ALSO remove `brand_connections` from `ZERO_POLICY_ALLOWED` in
health.js and the table names from `deleteBrand` in app.html — both still reference them on purpose
so existing rows are not orphaned.
**RATCHET FIXED AGAIN (same lesson, third time): `public-exposure.mjs` asserted
`Object.keys(functions).length >= 30`** — an assertion that breaks the moment endpoints are
legitimately retired. Replaced with a NAMED check that eight long-running functions keep their
`maxDuration` (the actual risk: silently reverting to the ~10s default). Mutation-tested.
**A RAW NUL BYTE was reintroduced into app.html** (a literal `\x00` in a `.join()`), making the
file read as BINARY to grep/diff. Replaced with the `\u0000` escape — identical at runtime, plain
text on disk. **Check `open('app.html','rb').read().count(b'\x00')` after any hashing work.**

## ▶▶ v632 — the 4 filming leftovers closed, and #1 turned out to be SHARPER than reported.
**THE REAL BUG: reopening the teleprompter within 2.4s ARMED A TAKE WITH NO RECORD TAP.**
`tpCountdown` ran a bare `setInterval` nothing cancelled, so after a close the stale callback still
fired: reopen (same OR a different post) inside the countdown window and `startTpRecord()` ran —
camera live, `.recording` on, timer and scroll going, no countdown shown, nobody touched Record.
Also left the Record button disabled for the 30s failsafe, since `_disarm` only ran inside the
callback. Now `window._tpCountdownIv` is cleared by `closeTeleprompter`, the callback re-checks
`.open` **at fire time on every tick**, and every give-up path calls the published `window._tpDisarm`
so the button always comes back. **Correction to the audit's wording:** the "stays closed" case did
NOT arm a take — `tpEnsureCamera` already refuses to keep a stream when the overlay isn't open, so
that path only leaked a stray `getUserMedia` + a toast. The REOPEN case is the one that armed.
**Proven against a pre-fix snapshot, 3 scenarios: pre-fix 3 FAIL (reopen `armed=TRUE`), fixed 3 PASS.**
Mutation-tested both halves separately — dropping the fire-time re-check fails `closed-directly`,
dropping the close-time cancel fails `reopen`.
**`_limit` leaked a timer per call** — 6 guarded awaits left **8 live timers** per render, now 0.
**ImageBitmaps are now freed** when a cache entry is dropped or overwritten, behind two guards the
agent had to discover: **(a) `tvApprove` stores the SAME array under a second key** (`'_tv'` → the
new state id), so a naive free would strip the photos off a post about to be filmed; **(b) a
`beatsCacheClear()` from `switchBrand` landing MID-RENDER** would close a bitmap `spRenderBeat`
hasn't consumed yet — deferred via `_csRendering`/`_csFreePending`. `_img` is read in exactly one
place (`spRenderBeat`, before `rec.start()`), which is what made a safe release point provable.
**The teleprompter now closes at render start.** Judged safe on real evidence, not assumption:
`tpBeatTimes` reads only snapshotted plain arrays + `tpVoiceWords` strings (never layout),
`closeTeleprompter` destroys no DOM (`.open` just toggles display), Retake is already unreachable by
then, and **`startTpRecord.onstop` already runs this exact sheet AND render with the teleprompter
closed** on the closed-mid-record path — an already-supported state. `.br-backdrop` has
`backdrop-filter:blur(3px)`, so leaving it open meant compositing a full-screen overlay every frame
during the heaviest moment in the app.
**STILL OPEN (small):** `stopTpScroll` dereferences `#tpPlayBtn` unguarded while every neighbouring
line is null-checked — safe only because that element is static markup.

## ▶▶ v631 — THE FILMING PATH AUDITED FOR THE FIRST TIME. Two live bugs, one silent and brand-crossing.
Largest never-audited surface in the app, and the one Jörgen personally uses. Nine findings, all
verified against the code before touching anything, none refuted.
**#1 LIVE — DOUBLE-TAPPING RECORD PRODUCED AN UNPLAYABLE FILE.** `tpRecordTap` was re-entrant:
during the 2.4s countdown `tpMediaRecorder` is null/inactive so the guard never fired, the button
was never disabled and still read "Record", and `.tp-countdown` is `pointer-events:none`. Two taps
= two `startTpRecord()` ~200ms apart; the second reset `tpRecordedChunks` and overwrote
`tpMediaRecorder`, **orphaning recorder A which kept recording**, and BOTH recorders'
`ondataavailable` pushed into the SAME module-level array → the Blob was two interleaved container
streams. The user performs a whole take and gets a file that will not play. Fixed with an
`_tpArming` mutex + disabled button + a `finally` disarm + a 30s failsafe so it can never latch off.
**Proven by mutation: fixed = 1 recorder, mutant (guard removed) = 2 recorders both writing.**
**#2 LIVE + SILENT — the graphics cache was keyed by a MUTABLE ARRAY INDEX.** `_beatsCache[id]`
where `id` is the array position (`reindexIdeas` sets `s.id = i`). Nothing invalidated it, so
(a) Sharpen / Viral Rewrite rewrote `script` in place and filming then composited **pre-sharpen
on-screen text**, with stale `cue` strings that no longer matched the speech → beat timing silently
fell all the way back to even spacing; (b) `switchBrand` rebuilds `state` with index ids and did not
clear the cache → **filming idea 3 in brand B composited brand A's graphics.** Jörgen runs two
brands daily. Now keyed brand + id + script fingerprint (djb2), validated on read, stale entries
DROPPED; `switchBrand` clears it. Mutation-proven: fixed rejects after sharpen AND after brand
switch, mutant accepts both.
**#3 the recorder's `onstop` was the one unguarded handler on the path** — a throw lost the take
with no message, AND `stopTpRecord`'s wrapper `await orig(ev); resolve()` meant a rejection left
that promise NEVER settling (`stopTpCamera` awaits it). The OTHER onstop in `closeTeleprompter` was
already correctly wrapped — the guarded shape existed 300 lines up and this one never got it.
Now try/catch + a last-ditch `tpDownloadBlob` so a performed take is never lost, and `finally{resolve()}`.
**#4 Retake destroyed the take BEFORE the retake armed** — permission revoked / camera grabbed by
another app / MediaRecorder throwing left the user with nothing. Now the blob is held and restored
with "your last take is safe" if nothing starts rolling.
**#5 the render frame loop had no kill flag** — only `vid.ended || t>=dur` exited it. With rVFC it
died by accident (the catch pauses the video); **without rVFC the rAF fallback composited 1440×2560
frames for the life of the page** after a cancel or stall, on a phone, exactly while sharing.
**#6 THE SPLIT SCREEN PROBABLY RENDERED SILENT ON iOS.** Audio is added via
`vid.captureStream()`/`mozCaptureStream()` — **Safari has neither**, so no audio track was added and
nothing detected it (the drift probe only compares durations). User films a talking head, waits
through a 2K render, gets a silent clip labelled "ready to post". Now refuses on the OBSERVED FACT
(zero audio tracks), never a browser sniff, routing into the existing loud-fail sheet which already
offers the plain video. **TRIGGER UNVERIFIED — needs a real iOS device to confirm.**
**#7** `await stopped` was the one un-time-boxed await, directly under a comment claiming "EVERY
await here is timeout-guarded" — and by then the watchdog and deadline were already cleared.
**#8** after sharing, `tpEndTake` removed `cam-on` but not `open` and never restored
`body.style.overflow` → the user stared at a black overlay with their script and no camera, page
scroll-locked. Every single time. **#9** a zero-byte take was announced "Filmed ✓".
**MY FOLLOW-UP FIX: the agent's #2 fix introduced a SILENT degradation** — a sharpened Quick Post
made `cached` null, and because that lane's offer hung entirely off `cached`, the split-screen
option just vanished with no explanation. `haveIdea` now resolves BOTH lanes via `_beatsIdeaFor`,
so the offer still appears and the graphics are refetched. TDZ checked by offset (`_spIdea` is
declared before the statement gate that uses it).
**ARCHITECTURAL VERDICT, recorded so it stops being re-litigated:** the long-proposed `beginTake()`
refactor WOULD have structurally prevented #1, #4 and #6-blur-reentrancy — they are all one defect,
"no single owner of the take lifecycle, so nothing can say we are already arming". It would NOT
have prevented #2, #5, #7 (those live in the render/platform layer). Still worth building.
**STILL OPEN in this path:** `tpCountdown`'s interval is not cancelled if the teleprompter closes
mid-countdown (the take arms behind a closed overlay); `_limit` leaks a timer per call; ImageBitmaps
are never closed; the teleprompter sits open behind the render sheet.

## ▶▶ v630 — 13 MORE CALL SITES OFF THE FULL-BRAIN UPLOAD: 237KB → 13.5KB (94%).
The client was still mailing the whole brand brain on 13 actions. Converted to `leanBrandFetch`
(client sends `brandId` + only what the DB cannot know; server hydrates via `_brandctx`):
auto-refill **19,754→2,630** (fires after EVERY approve, silently, in the background),
PAA→post 20,047→2,923, Notebook-develop 17,623→**417**, Idea Catcher 17,634→428 and 17,872→666,
Redo-with-notes 18,242→1,028, scenes 17,389→**183**, viral-rewrite 18,028→822, sharpen 18,330→1,116,
video-beats ×2 17,912→706, viral-analyze 18,638→1,432, **Assistant chat 17,611→405 (re-uploaded on
EVERY message)**. At his measured 0.5 KB/s, auto-refill alone drops ~39s → ~5s of upload.
New hydration+424 added to `video-beats.js`, `viral-analyze.js`, `brand-voice-chat.js`;
`generate-ideas` gained `exFormat` and `sharpen` now threads `format` so format-matched winners
survive the conversion.
**PROMPT EQUIVALENCE PROVEN, not assumed:** a harness lifts the REAL call expressions out of
app.html, drives them through the REAL `leanBrandFetch` into the REAL handlers with only the LLM and
DB stubbed, and diffs the assembled prompt. All 13: **byte-identical prompts, 24-25/25 sentinel
brand fields, hand-taught trends kept, dismissed auto-trends still suppressed.** Mutation-tested so
it can fail (breaking `exFormat` flags exactly the 3 format-matched callers and nothing else).
**PRE-EXISTING BUG FOUND WHILE CONVERTING: the scenes feature 500'd on EVERY call.** `handleScenes`
referenced `_usage`, a `const` declared INSIDE the exported handler → `ReferenceError` **after** the
Grok call had been paid for and parsed, so it burned a generation every time and always said
"Failed to generate scenes". Reproduced against the unmodified file first. Fixed with an inline
`require('./_usage')`. **Same block-scope class as the v622 `_isNetFail` bug — a top-level function
cannot see a `const` declared inside a handler.**
**LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE:** `fetchPAAQuestions` + `pullWebTrends` (they use the brand as a RELEVANCE
FILTER with a documented fail-open, not as a voice source — a hard 424 would turn a gracefully
degrading research tool into one that fails outright), `loadSettingsExamples` (cached per brand,
fires once ever), `expandField` (occasional Settings button). Those last two are the best remaining
candidates. `generateTodayTabPost` line ~12108 is its full-context FALLBACK and must stay a raw
fetch — that is the 424 recovery path, not an oversight.
**RATCHET FIXED: `lean-payload-all.mjs` asserted `ideaSites.length === 1`** — an assertion that
breaks every time the code it guards improves (the v618 lesson, again). Now identifies the Ideas-tab
site by `window._ideaDelivery` instead of counting, and `KNOWN_UNHYDRATED` is emptied since
viral-twist/rewrite have hydrated since v625.

## ▶▶ v629 — SEVEN DEAD ENDPOINTS DELETED (Jörgen spotted them: "leftovers ... not needed").
Audited every endpoint for real callers with a STRICT pattern (`/api/<name>` not followed by a word
char or hyphen — a loose `\b` counts `/api/generate-ideas` as a hit for `generate`, which is how
these survived earlier sweeps). **Deleted: `engine-test`, `generate`, `swap` (three 410 stubs),
`inspiration`, `listen`, `search-images` (dead features, ~21KB), `render-graphic`.**
`render-graphic` was safe because the LIVE manual publish (`publish-now.js`) requires
`_publish/render` DIRECTLY — render-graphic was a separate HTTP wrapper nothing ever called.
`_publish/render.js` STAYS. 55 → 48 endpoints.
**KEPT ON PURPOSE, do not delete:** `send-daily` + `pull-trends-cron` (invoked by Vercel Cron, so
they have no in-repo caller by design), `stripe-webhook` (invoked by Stripe), and **`auto-publish`**
— it is a deliberately SHELVED feature with `AUTO_PILOT_SHELVED = true` and a documented revival
path ("flip to false alongside CS_SHELVED"); it is unscheduled and returns immediately, so it costs
nothing, and deleting it would destroy the revival.
**WHY THIS MATTERED BEYOND TIDINESS:** `search-images` and `inspiration` called `guard()` but were
absent from vercel.json's functions map, so they ran on the ~10s platform default — they were the
binding constraint that forced the v628 Supabase timeout down to 4s. With them gone the floor rises
to the declared 30s minimum, so that timeout could be relaxed if a stall ever proves too eager.
**LESSON: "no caller in the repo" does NOT mean dead.** Cron paths and webhook receivers are
invoked from OUTSIDE the codebase. Check vercel.json `crons` and the payment provider before
concluding an endpoint is junk.

## ▶▶ v628 — THE HANG NOBODY COULD HAVE DIAGNOSED: every Supabase call had no timeout.
`_usage.sbRequest` and `_publish/store._req` opened https requests with NO timeout. `sbRequest`
runs on the `guard()` path = **every authenticated endpoint**; `_req` backs getUser,
userCanAccessBrand, _brandctx and the whole publish layer. **`checkLimit` fails OPEN on an error —
but a HANG IS NOT AN ERROR**, so if Supabase ever stalled rather than erroring, every endpoint in
the app would hang to its maxDuration and die with no body and no log, and the fail-open safety net
would never fire because nothing rejected. Now **4000ms** on both + **20000ms** on `uploadPublic`
(a third untimed request the agent found in the same file). Proven by a real TLS server that
accepts and never answers: 9/9 checks, and the pre-fix code **never settles** (killed at 25s with
no output). **THE ARITHMETIC THAT SET 4s, worth keeping:** the binding constraint is NOT the 30s
floor in vercel.json — `search-images.js` and `inspiration.js` call `guard()` but are **absent from
the functions map**, so they run on the ~10s default. Same blind spot that hid `extract-article.js`
in v606 and again in v627. `timeout-budgets.mjs` already models this (`md[name] ?? 10`).
**MEDIA DOWNLOADS WERE UNBOUNDED:** `transcribe-url.downloadFile` buffered the ENTIRE file before
checking the 25MB cap and had no timeout — a long/slow video hung to the platform kill or OOM'd.
Now the cap is enforced INSIDE `resp.on('data')` (destroys response + request), and one absolute
wall-clock deadline is threaded through the whole redirect chain so 5 hops cannot each get a fresh
budget. Measured: rejects at **26.2MB of a 60MB payload in 46ms**; the pre-fix pattern was still
unsettled at 6s holding all 60MB. Budget: 2+15+40+50 = 107s under a 110s budget under the 120s cap.
**Deliberately NOT hidden: the Apify fallback cannot fit** (its own `waitForFinish=90` + 40 + 50 =
180s) — it was already over budget before this change; it now surfaces a named "took too long" at
~110s instead of a bare 504. Lowering waitForFinish would break runs that currently succeed.
**`userMessage()` added** so raw `socket hang up` / DNS noise stops reaching the user verbatim
(the frontend renders `data.error` as-is); hand-written messages pass through unchanged.
**FRONTEND:** 4 inline `background:#fff` (2 components) that dark mode could never override —
teleprompter lip-sync nudge buttons (whose glyph came from the UA and rendered LIGHT under
`color-scheme:dark`, i.e. invisible on white) and the PWA install card, fixed as a UNIT because
converting only the card would have left `#1a1a1a` title text on a `#1C1C1C` card.
**`loadPAAState` — the scanner's claim was PARTLY WRONG and the real bug was worse.** The
`JSON.parse` was already inside a try; the actual defects were (a) a value that PARSES into the
wrong shape was assigned unchecked, so `renderPAA`'s `.filter()` threw OUTSIDE any try = the real
screen-killer, (b) one shared try meant a corrupt value on brand B left brand A's questions in
memory = **cross-brand bleed**, (c) nothing cleared the bad value so it failed identically forever.
Oracle: 11/11 pass after, **4/11 before**. New `lsDel()` helper (top-level declaration, hoisted —
a `const` inside the try would ReferenceError from its own catch).
**localStorage audit: 39 write sites read one by one; only 4 were per-brand data on a bare shared
key** (remixes, product refs, prompt history ×2) — all write-only caches whose readers are dead or
DB-backed, so no user data moves. **33 left alone as correctly device-global.** Two judgement calls
recorded and NOT changed: `SETTINGS_KEY` (written during onboarding BEFORE a brand exists, so
`lsSet` would silently drop it) and `stmt_tpl` (its reader is a parse-time IIFE, so namespacing only
the write would silently stop persisting the choice). Both need a boot-order change first.
**Dev scripts moved OUT of `api/`** → `scripts/dev/` (which .vercelignore excludes), require paths
and usage lines fixed. `api/_publish/` now holds only real modules.

## ▶▶ RESOLVED 2026-08-27, DO NOT RE-CHASE: the crons were never broken — the MONITOR was missing.
Health reported all crons "never observed", which reads exactly like a dead cron. **Cause: the
`job_heartbeats` table did not exist** — `sql/job-heartbeats.sql` sat in the repo unrun, and
`store.heartbeat()` try/catches its own failure, so every write vanished and health had nothing to
read. Jörgen ran the SQL; within 2 minutes `send-daily` wrote `status:'ok', due:0` — **proving the
hourly cron had been running correctly the whole time.** `pull-trends-cron` (daily 05:00 UTC) shows
`never-run` until its first run after the table existed; that is CORRECT, not a fault.
**Also dropped: a stray `public.bid` table** (one column `id`, one bare uuid, referenced nowhere in
the app) — it was the table failing `no_unexpected_denyall_tables`. `cs_blog_posts` was NOT the
culprit; that guess was wrong and the table is gone with the blog anyway.
**LESSON: "the job never ran" and "nothing was recording that it ran" look identical from the
outside. Check that the MONITOR exists before concluding the JOB is dead** — v627's health fix now
distinguishes them explicitly (`never-run` vs `unreadable`).
**MY DEPLOY-BREAKING MISTAKE, worth remembering:** deleting the blog endpoints left
`api/cs-blog-cron.js` in vercel.json's `functions` map, and **Vercel HARD-FAILS the deploy** with
"the pattern … doesn't match any Serverless Functions". `parse-all.mjs` now fails on any
vercel.json functions/crons/rewrites entry pointing at a missing file (mutation-tested).

## ▶▶ v627 — A USER COULD PAY AND GET NOTHING, AND NOTHING ANYWHERE WOULD SAY SO.
Backend audit found the worst bug on the money path. **`setPlan()` (`_usage.js`) swallowed every
failure — `catch(e){ return false }` with NO log — and all three callers DISCARDED the boolean.**
So: `checkout-confirm` returned **`{ok:true, plan:'pro'}` after the plan write had failed** (card
charged, plan not applied, user told it worked), and `stripe-webhook` returned **200 to Stripe on a
failed write — which tells Stripe "delivered, do not retry"**, so a cancelled customer kept paid
access forever and a paying customer stayed on free. Both directions, zero log lines, invisible
until a customer complains. Fixed: setPlan logs; checkout-confirm returns 500 + an honest message;
**the webhook now returns non-2xx so Stripe RETRIES — that retry is what heals it.** Deliberately
NOT 402 on checkout-confirm: the global fetch wrapper opens the upgrade modal on any 402, and
"please upgrade" is the worst thing to show someone who just paid. Verified by discrimination —
identical events differing only in setPlan's result now yield different status codes.
**`stock-photo.js` called `guard()` and ignored it** — no `_g.over` check, no `logUsage`, the ONLY
handler in the app doing this. Both halves missing means each hid the other: with no usage row,
`used` stays 0 forever, so the gate could never fire even once added. Any signed-in account could
drain the Pexels quota unbounded. Now metered (429 for burst / 402 for real limit — it fires ~6 at
a time per render, so a 402 would wrongly say "out of posts"); `logUsage` is awaited BEFORE any
header/body write and try/caught so a metering hiccup can't cost the user their photo.
**TWO SEQUENTIAL LLM CALLS, EACH DEFAULTING TO 240s, UNDER A 300s CAP** — `sharpen` (critique +
rewrite) and `generate-ideas` (main + the avoid-words guardrail regeneration, which powers Quick
Post/Ideas/Idea Catcher/Notebook/PAA/auto-refill). 480s worst case vs 300s = **platform kill, bare
504, no app error, no log** — the failure mode that hid a bug for a week. Now explicitly budgeted
(sharpen 60+120, ideas 90+90). **`extract-article.js` was ABSENT from vercel.json's functions map
entirely**, so it ran on the ~10s default against a 90s internal worst case — the v606 timeout
audit only compared endpoints that were IN the file, so this one was never checked. Now 120.
**THE TRAP INSIDE THAT FIX, worth more than the fix:** the agent first used named constants
(`timeoutMs: GEN_TIMEOUT_MS`) — **the ratchet greps `/timeoutMs\s*:\s*(\d+)/`, could not see them,
and PASSED vacuously against the 240000 fallback.** Green for the wrong reason, and it would have
stayed green through any future regression. Literals inlined. **Same lesson as v626: a check
satisfiable by a NAME rather than a VALUE is not a check.**
**SILENT-FAILURE SWEEP, frontend (app.html):** 6 confirmed dead/invisible controls fixed —
`spExpandField` (no `resp.ok`, console-only catch), `memeDownload`/`memePublish` (bare returns; an
unguarded `toDataURL` threw and killed the handler so the button did literally nothing),
`blogEditSave`, `doPublish` (every error branch wrote into `#pubMsg` — a detached node swallowed
them all), `refShotPick`. **Plus a permanent hang nobody had found: `resizeImage` had NO
`img.onerror`, so an undecodable image never settled the promise — every `await resizeImage(...)`
hung forever and the picked file just vanished.** All four callers guarded. Also `handlePromptRefUpload`
called `saveRefs()` — **a function that does not exist anywhere in the file** (latent, unreachable).
**WRITES THAT REPORTED SUCCESS THEY NEVER ACHIEVED:** `store.rest()` resolves on EVERY status, so
an unchecked call is indistinguishable from success. Disconnecting a channel said "done" while it
stayed connected and publishable; Auto-Pilot OFF could silently not persist; the Gemini key toasted
"saved ✓" then the next generate said "add your key first" (that confusing symptom, explained).
All now status-checked. **`send-daily` wrote an `'ok'` heartbeat when its subscriber READ had
failed** — a total daily-push outage reported as a healthy run — and had no per-subscriber budget,
so past ~5-10 due users the cron was platform-killed mid-loop and everyone after silently missed
that day (they are NOT retried: `send_hour` only matches once).
**FOUR HEALTH CHECKS THAT COULD NOT FAIL** (`health.js`): `cron_auto-publish_fresh` was permanently
green for a job that is shelved AND unscheduled AND has never run; **"never observed" scored as a
PASS for every cron — but a heartbeat row SURVIVES deploys, so it is only ever absent if the job
has NEVER once completed**, which is the loudest signal there is and is exactly how a cron died
daily for 7 days here undetected; health never read `last_status`, so an honest `'error'`/`'partial'`
heartbeat was invisible; `config_llm_key` passed on GROQ, which cannot write text any more.
Now discriminates 5/5 states (never-run / fresh-ok / error / partial / stale).
**BLOG RETIRED ENTIRELY (Jörgen: "the blog feature thing we dont need at all").** Deleted
`_csblog/blog-index/blog-post/sitemap-blog/cs-blog-cron` (zero references anywhere);
`generate-blog.js` is a 410 stub because shelved UI code still references it. **AND A LIVE PUBLIC
BUG FOUND DOING IT: SIX "Blog" links on index/faq/terms/privacy/refunds pointed at `/blog`, which
404s** — every visitor who clicked Blog hit a Vercel error page. My first grep covered 3 files and
missed 3; **grep ALL shipped html, not a remembered subset.**
**▶ CORRECTION TO A STALE NOTE THAT COST REAL TIME: `cs_blog_posts` DOES exist now** (the endpoints
returned 200, not 404) and the SQL is **NOT needed — do not push it a fourth time.** The blog was
already switched off at the routing layer by an earlier session (rewrites + cron removed from
vercel.json) and this file never recorded it, so every session re-diagnosed a dead feature.

## ▶▶ v626 — THE COACH WAS READING A DIFFERENT, SMALLER BRAIN THAN EVERY OTHER TOOL.
Asked "how much brain does each button reach", measured it, and the Assistant came back an outlier.
`brand-voice-chat.js` built its OWN 18-line brand snapshot instead of calling `fullBrandBlock` —
**measured 20 of 28 brand fields, a 91-character brand section**. The eight it could never see:
**website, reviewInsights, webMentions, categoryGripes, learnedSignals, channels, competitorMoves,
approvedExamples.** So the coach knew the voice and the product but not what you'd recently approved,
what your competitors just did, or what your customers actually said. After: **28/28, 2779 chars.**
**THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT AS v612 AND v625, THIRD TIME.** v612: `generate-ideas` had its own
`buildMasterPrompt` that dropped approvedExamples/learnedSignals/competitors/channels/visualStyle.
v625: viral-twist/rewrite got no brand at all. **A second renderer never announces itself — it just
falls behind the first one one field at a time, and the only symptom is output that feels generic,
which is exactly the complaint this project has been stuck on.**
**NEW RATCHET `scripts/verify/one-brand-renderer.mjs` (G34)** closes the CLASS, not the instance:
(1) it renders a sentinel fixture through `fullBrandBlock` and fails if the SHARED renderer itself
ever drops a field (every generator would lose it silently and at once); (2) it fails if ANY
`api/*.js` reads ≥6 distinct `bc.<field>` by hand without calling `fullBrandBlock` — so a brand-new
second renderer goes red the day it is born. `people-also-ask` is exempt by name and on purpose: it
finds what the PUBLIC searches for, and seeding it with the brand's own words would echo the brand
back at itself. It also asserts the coach still HAS its persona / memory / action buttons / web
search, so "fix the brain reach" can never quietly gut the feature.
**MY ORACLE FAILED ITS OWN FIRST MUTATION — and that is the reusable lesson.** M1 rebuilt
`brandBlock` by hand while keeping the import and the variable name; my check asked only "does a
variable called brandBlock exist and does the word fullBrandBlock appear in the file" → **it PASSED
a mutant that had removed the entire fix.** Tightened to assert where the value COMES FROM
(`brandBlock = fullBrandBlock(`). **A check that can be satisfied by a NAME rather than by
BEHAVIOUR is not a check.** 5 mutations, 5 caught after the fix.
**MEASURED REACH, all surfaces (for the next time this is asked):** Quick Post, Ideas, Remix, Viral
Twist, Viral Rewrite, Sharpen, Blog, Meme, Idea Catcher, Notebook-develop, PAA-to-post, auto-refill,
scenes, redo — all **28/28** via the shared renderer. Assistant **20/28 → 28/28** (this fix).
Questions/PAA **0/28 and correct** — it is a research tool, not a writer; a post generated FROM a
question goes through Quick Post at full reach.

## ▶▶ v625 — CAUGHT A REGRESSION I INTRODUCED: VIRAL TWIST WAS WRITING WITH **NO BRAND BRAIN**.
The lean-request work converted `tvViralTwist`/`tvViralRewrite` to `leanBrandFetch` — but **neither
endpoint implemented the `brandId` protocol**, so they received `brandContext: {recentTrends}` and
`fullBrandBlock` rendered a BRAND PROFILE containing nothing but a trends line. **Viral Twist was
generating with no brand brain at all — silently, producing generic output that still LOOKED fine.**
Strictly worse than before the change, and the 424 safety net could never fire because there was no
hydration to fail. Measured: prompt 322 chars → **1011** after hydrating, brand name absent → present.
Fixed in `viral-twist`, `viral-rewrite` and `sharpen` with the same branch `remix.js` uses.
**THE LESSON, and it is the whole day in one line: a performance change silently deleted the product's
core value, and nothing would have told us.** The output would just have drifted generic — exactly the
complaint this project has been stuck on for months.
**NEW RATCHET `scripts/verify/lean-hydration.mjs` (G32):** it reads every `leanBrandFetch('/api/x')`
call site OUT OF app.html and asserts that `api/x.js` hydrates AND can 424. Convert a new call site
without hydrating its endpoint and the gate goes red naming it. Mutation-tested three ways, including
converting a fresh endpoint (people-also-ask) to lean — caught.
**THREE MORE DEAD BUTTONS, reachable by the most ORDINARY flow in the app.** `tvApprove()` nulls
`_todayTabIdea` but **never clears `#tvResult`**, so the whole card stays on screen. Approve → tap
Teleprompter / B-roll / Make Slides = nothing at all, while Viral Twist and Post it (already on
`tvActiveIdea`) worked — same row, same tap, different outcome. All three now resolve or warn.
`tvMakeSlides` was worse than dead: its guard sat on the CALLER (`if (window._todayTabIdea) tvApprove()`),
so with no post it skipped the warning AND fell through to `_tvLastStateId` — a PREVIOUSLY approved
post — i.e. it could open the slide maker on the WRONG post.
**STILL FULL-UPLOAD (flagged, one line each): `/api/sharpen` plus seven more `generate-ideas` callers —
auto-refill, PAA, Notebook develop, Idea Catcher ×2, idea redo, scenes.**

## ▶▶ v623-v624 — THE 52-SECOND WAIT WAS OUR OWN UNSET DEFAULT. + 4 DEAD BUTTONS.
**CONFIRMED WORKING IN PRODUCTION 2026-08-27 (Jörgen: "okay now worked" then "i did quick post test atm yes with viral twist and sharpen and worked").** So generate + BOTH refine tools are verified live on his phone. Before, 06:33:
one call, `xAI EMPTY 200 after 52771ms`, zero words. After, on v624 with `reasoning_effort: low`:
generate-ideas 200 at 06:55:32 and **viral-twist 200 at 06:55:58** — 26s apart, no empty responses,
no retries, no errors in the window. Both fixes verified by log evidence, not by assertion.
**THE BIG ONE, and the v-earlier EMPTY-200 logging is what caught it.** Production log:
`xAI EMPTY 200 after 52771ms — completion_tokens: 0, reasoning_tokens: 2533`. **Grok spent 52 seconds
reasoning and wrote NOT ONE WORD**, then the retry fired — which is most of "why does it take so long".
Cause: **we never sent `reasoning_effort`, and xAI defaults it to `"high"`** (verified on docs.x.ai, not
from memory) — the depth meant for maths proofs and competition problems, applied to writing a social
post. So every post this app has ever written ran at max-but-one reasoning depth, buying latency and
empty responses rather than better copy. **Now `reasoning_effort` defaults to `low`** (Jörgen: "everywhere
quick then… noone wants to wait"), env-overridable via **`XAI_REASONING_EFFORT=low|medium|high|xhigh`
— so the level can be changed in Vercel env with NO deploy** if the writing degrades. Reasoning cannot
be disabled entirely; `presence_penalty`/`frequency_penalty`/`stop` are REJECTED by reasoning models —
this file sends none, keep it that way (the oracle strips comments before checking, because matching my
own explanatory comment made it fail against correct code).
**MY MEASUREMENT NOTE: he tried to RUN the log line I quoted** (`zsh: command not found: xAI`). Quote a
log line as a fenced block or say "log line, not a command" — a pasted diagnostic reads as an instruction.
**FOUR DEAD BUTTONS (v623).** "pushed viral twist, didnt work" — and the logs showed **no viral-twist
request at all**, while `/api/connections` and `/api/speak` succeeded seconds later, so the connection
was fine and the request was never made. Cause: `_todayTabIdea` is nulled BOTH on approve AND at the top
of "Try Another", so a FAILED regeneration (exactly the empty-200 above) leaves the previous post on
screen with the variable null — and `tvViralTwist`/`tvPostIt`/`tvViralRewrite`/`tvApplyTwist` each did
`if (!i) return;` **silently**. No spinner, no error, nothing. New **`tvActiveIdea()`** falls back to
`_tvIdea` (the post on screen, never cleared) **but only while the result card is actually rendered**, so
it can never act on a post the user is no longer looking at; **`tvApprove` deliberately keeps the strict
guard** — nulling the idea is what prevents a double-approve — but now warns instead of doing nothing.
Behaviourally verified across all 4 states; 4 mutations, 4 caught.

## ▶▶ v621-v622 — IT WAS NEVER THE PAYLOAD OR THE AI. THE LINK DROPS THE RESPONSE.
**Three "this is the fix" claims in a row were wrong, and the data killed all of them.** On v620, with
the lean 2.9KB payload live and his connection at **6.36 KB/s** (50× faster than earlier), Quick Post
still failed — and the logs showed **three generate-ideas calls, ALL 200**, one answering in ~4 seconds.
Then the real clue: the phone said **"Failed to fetch"**, which is a NETWORK-layer failure, categorically
different from our AbortError timeout and from an HTTP error. **The mobile link severs the connection
AFTER the server has answered.** Not size, not the model, not stale code (he confirmed v620), not the
240s timeout.
**v621 = INSTRUMENT INSTEAD OF GUESS.** `window._tvPhase` records `sentBytes`, `headersMs` (fetch
resolves on RESPONSE HEADERS = upload + server time) and `bodyMs` (the download). The timeout message
now NAMES the phase: *"the server never answered this phone"* vs *"replied in Ns but the download
stalled"*. One sentence tells us which half of the world to look in — after three rounds of not knowing.
**v622 = SURVIVE THE DROP.** A network-level failure is retried ONCE (`_isNetFail`: TypeError /
"failed to fetch" / "load failed", but **never** an AbortError — the user's 4 minutes are up — and
**never** a 4xx/5xx — the server has spoken). Verified behaviourally: abort→false, Failed-to-fetch→true,
HTTP 500→false. Raw "Failed to fetch" replaced with plain English naming the connection.
**A BUG I ALMOST SHIPPED, caught by my own scope check:** `_isNetFail` was declared `const` INSIDE the
`try` and called from the `catch`. `const` is block-scoped → `ReferenceError` in the handler → **the user
would have seen NOTHING on any failure.** Moved above the try. **Any helper a catch block calls must be
declared outside that try.**
**LESSON ON BRITTLE ASSERTIONS:** the "Quick Post reports the timeout" check used a fixed character
window between `_timedOut` and `textContent`; it had to be widened twice as that branch legitimately
grew. **An assertion that needs re-tuning every time the code it guards improves is a bad assertion** —
now scoped to the catch BLOCK (distance-independent). Mutation-verified: deleting the toast fails,
rewording passes, and removing one of three redundant surfaces passes because the property still holds.
**STILL NOT FIXED AND CANNOT BE FROM HERE: his connection.** The app now survives one drop; it cannot
stop the drops. **The real fix if this persists is IDEMPOTENCY — client sends a request id, server
stores the generated post against it, a retry returns the stored result instead of regenerating.** That
turns a lost response into a 3KB re-fetch instead of a wasted generation. Needs a table, so it needs his
SQL — not built.

## ▶▶ v620 — QUICK POST STOPPED MAILING THE BRAND BRAIN ON EVERY TAP. 23,033 → 2,892 bytes.
v619's timeout fix was not enough: he timed out AGAIN at 240s on 0.13 KB/s, and the logs again showed
**`/api/generate-ideas` 200 at 04:44:09** (his 7:44 screenshot) — four successful server responses now,
every one of which his phone never received. **Root cause was never the AI or the timeout: the client
re-uploaded the ENTIRE brand snapshot on every generate**, ~13KB of `getBrandContext()` + ~2KB avoid-list,
when the server already holds all of it and `brandId` was right there. Measured: **23,033 → 2,892 bytes
(87% smaller) — 173s → 22s of upload at his speed.**
**NEW `api/_brandctx.js`** hydrates the brand from `brands` + `ideas` (service role, AFTER
`userCanAccessBrand`) in 5 parallel narrow queries; the two winner queries reproduce
`getApprovedExamples`' `slice(-3)`/`slice(-2)` server-side instead of dragging the library over the wire.
`generate-ideas` merges the client's thin context ON TOP. **`brandId` is the discriminator and NO existing
caller sent it, so every other path is byte-identical — old clients on the SW cache keep working.**
**THE TRAP THIS DESIGN EXISTS TO AVOID — three client-only sources, not one:** `getTrendStore()`
(hand-taught trends) is localStorage-only, **`getAutoTrends()` subtracts localStorage
`auto_trends_dismissed`** (rebuild it server-side and every off-topic headline the user already ×'d comes
BACK), and `approveReason` + `tv_recent` have no columns. So the client still sends the **final merged
`recentTrends` array** and the server never rebuilds trends — provably lossless, no mirrored merge logic
to drift. `learningContext` stays client-built for the same reason (a server version loses the
"— loved: …" annotations); only the avoid-list is split, via a `<<CS_AVOID_LIST>>` marker so the
"they just rejected this" block stays last.
**HONESTY GUARDS:** `await flushBrandSave()` before the request (debounced saves); `_brandSaveOk===false`
falls back to the full upload; a missing/stale row returns **424 → the client re-sends full context once**,
so it can NEVER silently write a brand-less post. One extra round trip in that rare case, no double-charge.
**THE AGENT CAUGHT TWO OF ITS OWN DEAD MUTATIONS** — one `perl` substitution never applied (grep errored)
and "passed" against unmutated code; the real mutation then STILL passed because the marker sat on a title
