## ▶▶ v617-v619 — "Timed out" ON QUICK POST WAS NOT THE AI. THE SERVER RETURNED 200.
Jörgen tapped Quick Post, got **"Timed out — tap to try again"**, and the toast said *"the AI is slow
right now"*. **THE LOGS SAID OTHERWISE: `/api/generate-ideas` was called ONCE in 3 hours and returned
200 at 04:17:20 — his 7:18 screenshot exactly. The server WROTE the post. The phone had stopped waiting.**
Zero runtime errors in 6h; all 8 requests 200. **Reading the logs BEFORE touching code is what turned
this from "the AI is flaky" into a measurable client bug in ten minutes.**
**CAUSE 1 — dead weight in the REQUEST.** `getApprovedExamples` uploaded `hook` (≤200) and `body`
(≤1400) per example. `api/_brain.js` reads **only** `text`/`format`/`title` — the client's own comment
even said so ("fullBrandBlock renders only `text` … keep them split too"). Measured with realistic
content: **4544 → 2388 bytes, and at his 0.06 KB/s the examples alone took ~74s to upload against a 90s
timeout** — leaving ~16s for the brand context, the round trip, the generation AND the download. Removing
fields nothing reads cannot change one word of output. **The hook still reaches the model inside `text`.**
**CAUSE 2 — the client gave up before the server did.** `generate-ideas` has `maxDuration: 300`; Quick
Post aborted at **90s**, and `btnWork`'s DEFAULT `maxMs` is 90s too — so **every generate button in the
app** (Ideas, Remix, Sharpen, Meme, Viral, Idea Catcher) was cutting off work the server was still doing.
Both now **240s**: long enough for a slow upload, still under 300s so the SERVER's timeout wins and
yields a real error instead of an ambiguous client abort.
**CAUSE 3 — the message lied.** "The AI is slow right now" was false and sent the diagnosis the wrong
way. Now: *"We stopped waiting — usually a slow connection, not the AI."* **Never name a component as the
culprit unless you observed it fail.**
**FOUR MEASUREMENT ERRORS OF MY OWN IN ONE DAY — this is the real lesson.** (1) `node x.mjs | head; $?`
reads HEAD's status, certifying a broken oracle. (2) Called `crawlValueOk(key, value)` when it takes
`(raw)`, so I "proved" it accepted all junk. (3) Relaxed an assertion to `/showToast/` over a whole
function — it matched an unrelated call and could no longer fail. (4) Mutation-tested
`data-integrity-p1p8.mjs` directly; it refuses to run standalone, so **every mutation "passed" against a
no-op**. **Before trusting ANY red or green, prove the check actually executed.**
**Also fixed:** two `data-integrity` assertions were pinned to the literal words "took too long", so they
broke the moment the copy was corrected. **An assertion coupled to exact wording punishes improving the
wording** — they now test that the timeout REACHES the user (scoped to the window after `_timedOut`, so
deleting the toast is still caught) while leaving the sentence free to change.

## ▶▶ v615 — deleting an account now CANCELS THE SUBSCRIPTION (2026-08-26).
v614 left the real harm in place: `delete-account` erased `user_plans` — the row holding
`stripe_subscription_id` — **without cancelling**, so a user who closed their account kept being charged
AND we had thrown away the only id that could find the subscription. A `console.warn` was the whole
mitigation. Now `stripeCancel()` (`DELETE /v1/subscriptions/:id`, immediate — they are closing the
account, not letting it lapse) runs **before** the row is dropped; 404 counts as success (already gone),
and a 2xx whose `status !== 'canceled'` counts as FAILURE. **A missing `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is a failure,
not a silent skip** — if billing is configured and the key is absent, the subscription is very much live.
**Erasure still proceeds when the cancel fails** (refusing to delete their data would trade one duty for
another), but the success response carries `billingWarning`, and `app.html`'s alert prints it INSTEAD of
"Account deleted." — otherwise it would be the same silent lie the endpoint was just rewritten to remove.
**MY MEASUREMENT WAS BROKEN BEFORE MY ORACLE WAS.** All 3 mutations "passed" — because
`node oracle.mjs | head -4; echo rc=$?` captures **head's** exit status, not node's. Re-run without the
pipe: 4/4 caught. **Never read `$?` through a pipe when mutation-testing** — it silently certifies a
broken oracle, which is worse than no oracle.

## ▶▶ CAUGHT ON THE v613 DEPLOY: THE EDGE WAS PINNING sw.js — "deployed but not live", AGAIN, one layer up.
The v613 deploy succeeded and `contentshrimp.com/CLAUDE.md` correctly went 404 — so the build WAS live.
But fetching `contentshrimp.com/sw.js` returned **`BUILD = 'v606'`**, while `contentshrimp.com/sw.js?cachebust=613`
returned **`v613-f521aede`**. Same origin, same second: the deployment was correct and **a CDN edge cache
was serving a seven-version-old service worker.** Since the entire update mechanism is "the browser
refetches /sw.js and sees different bytes", every phone would have kept the old app forever — the fix
deployed and permanently invisible. **The content-hash stamp (v607) does NOT protect against this: it
guarantees the FILE differs, not that anyone can FETCH the difference.**
**ROOT CAUSE: `/sw.js` was `Cache-Control: no-cache`, while `/(.*\.html)` was `no-store`. `no-cache`
PERMITS a shared cache to store the response and serve it after revalidation; only `no-store` forbids
storing it at all.** The one file that must never be cached had the weaker directive. Fixed to `no-store`,
and `build-stamp.mjs` now FAILS if `/sw.js` ever loses it (mutation-tested both ways: reverting to
`no-cache` fails, deleting the rule fails).
**THE VERIFY THAT ACTUALLY WORKS — compare origin vs edge, never just read one:**
`curl -s https://contentshrimp.com/sw.js | grep BUILD` and `curl -s "https://contentshrimp.com/sw.js?cb=$RANDOM" | grep BUILD`
— **if they disagree, the edge is stale and no device is getting updates.** If they still disagree after a
redeploy, purge the CDN (Vercel dashboard → Deployment → Purge Cache) or `vercel --prod --force`.
**ALSO LEARNED: do NOT register the SW as `/sw.js?v=<version>` to dodge this.** It looks like the obvious
fix and it silently breaks updates forever — the browser only ever refetches the URL it registered, and
since app.html is itself served FROM the SW cache, the cached copy would keep registering its own old
version and never learn a newer one exists. The script URL must stay stable; fix the CACHE, not the URL.
**AND: paste-mangling makes terminal verification lie.** His check printed `404 / 000 / 000 / 000` and
`grep: must: No such file or directory` — two commands pasted as one block, so grep read my `# comment`
words as FILENAMES and the version check never ran. **Hand over ONE command per line, no trailing
comments** — a comment on a paste line can eat the next command.

## ▶▶ v613 — THE THREE UNAUDITED SURFACES (2026-08-26). Filming · onboarding · security.
Three deep READ-ONLY audits ran in parallel on the surfaces nothing had ever examined, then three fix
agents with disjoint file ownership. **22 gates now; the 2 unmet are still MANUAL and belong to Jörgen.**

**THE FINDING THAT PROBABLY EXPLAINS FOUR VERSIONS OF RENDER STUTTER.** `tpBlur.stop()` was reachable
from only three places, and **`stopTpRecord` was not one of them** — so with blur on, the MediaPipe
segmentation pump (ML inference + a six-level `drawImage` pyramid into a 1080×1920 canvas, every frame)
kept running through review, the offer sheet and the ENTIRE 15-40s 2K render. The camera and mic stayed
live through playback and the share sheet too. v550/552/553/560 all chased the render in isolation; the
decisive clue was already in the changelog — *"without blur it was OK"* — but blur-off ALSO means no
competing segmentation. **FIXED: new `tpEndTake()`, called when the user commits (Keep it) and on the
no-review path — deliberately NOT on Retake, which still needs the camera.** If stutter persists after
this, the remaining lever is the 2K `SP_SS`, not the render loop.

**A PREVIEW TAP SILENTLY DISABLED THE RECORDING ENGINE.** `if (!tpScrolling) tpStartRecordingScroll()` —
and ▶ sits in the SAME collapsed drawer as "Blur bg", so the user who opens it to turn on blur is exactly
the user who taps ▶ to check the pace. Preview → Record meant the take ran on a step computed at preview
geometry (read line 38%, no lead-in padding) while `.recording` had since moved the line to 14% and added
0.74×clientHeight of padding, `_tpSyncOn` stayed false, and `scroll-behavior:smooth` fought the 30ms
interval — re-entering the exact v494 bug through a different door, **while the chip still displayed
"following your voice"**. Now unconditional. **This is the file's recurring shape: a fix guarded by a
condition an unrelated control can falsify.** The audit's structural recommendation, NOT yet built:
give the take one owner (`beginTake()`/`endTake()` + a context object) instead of ten `window._tp*`
globals written on one path and read on another — that is the mechanism behind v492, v505, v507 and v544.

**ONBOARDING CONTRADICTED ITSELF IN TWO SECONDS.** `obNext` enforced only `brandName`;
`isBrandMinimumMet` needs name + 2 tones + 2 communities + audience. So the advertised "No website yet"
lane gave: *"Your brand brain is ready"* → a LOCKED circle reading "Set up your brand first" → a modal
saying *"your brand brain is still empty"*. Fixed by making the wizard collect what the app requires
(NOT by weakening the guard — a bare brain writes generic output). Note USPs had to join the required
set: the four `isBrandMinimumMet` fields alone leave `getBrainStats().filled` at exactly 2, so
`brandBrainBare()` would still fire. Also fixed: a failed brand save left the finish button permanently
disabled reading "Generating…" (only a reload escaped) — the catch returned instead of throwing, so the
only code that re-enabled it never ran.

**THE ENTIRE ENGINEERING NOTEBOOK WAS PUBLIC.** `outputDirectory:"."` + no `.vercelignore` rules for
`*.md`/`sql/` meant **`contentshrimp.com/CLAUDE.md` served 692KB, 200 OK** — verified live, along with
GATES/HANDOFF/ENV-SETUP/STRIPE-SETUP, every RLS policy in `sql/`, and `.auth.json`'s saved session token.
No credentials in them, but it hands an attacker a better map of this system than an audit produces.
Fixed + HSTS/Referrer-Policy/Permissions-Policy added (`camera=(self)` kept — denying it silently breaks
filming). **No CSP: the app uses ~319 inline handlers, so a blind CSP would break everything — it is the
highest-value remaining header and needs its own pass, starting Report-Only.**

**THIRTEEN ENDPOINTS COULD NEVER HIT THEIR OWN LIMIT.** Registered at 0 credits → `used + 0 > limit` is
never true → `used` stays 0 forever, on every plan. The €10 fuse built for exactly this was **off by
default**. Worst case from one free signup, one hour: ~$700 OpenAI (`speak`), $150-3,000 xAI
(`brand-voice-chat`, uncapped brand context), plus destroyed SerpAPI/Apify quotas — and signup is open
magic-link. `crawl-brand` and `extract-article` had NO gate at all. Fixed: real weights (heavy Pro user
lands at 401/750, so honest use is untouched), fuse armed at €25 trial/free-only, both endpoints gated

the client-supplied brand context. **FLAG: free tier now lands at 93% — that is a pricing decision,

**MY OWN ORACLE FAILED ITS MUTATION TEST FIRST TIME.** The per-field cap check passed with the cap
removed, because the TOTAL cap caught it — a check incapable of failing. Caught it by mutating, fixed the
threshold so the two caps are tested independently, re-mutated. **That is the whole reason to mutation-test:
the oracle I wrote to catch a bug could not catch it, and only running the mutation revealed that.**

BELOW the theme layer, so every past fix was written at normal weight and was **dead on arrival** — the v601
nav fix was overridden 1,700 lines later. Measured: active nav icon 1.09:1 → 13.0:1; Remix/Meme card
headlines 1.1:1 → 13.9:1. **Any future dark fix MUST carry `!important` or higher specificity or it will
silently lose.** `dark-mode.selftest.mjs` re-breaks all 17 defects and proves the oracle catches them.

(a network drop in that window destroyed everything, and the localStorage snapshot holds only status, no

**LESSON, and it is the session's whole point: prose rules in CLAUDE.md do NOT change behaviour — I wrote the
BUILD-bump rule myself and still broke it. Only executable checks do.** Everything that held today was a
script that fails loudly; everything that failed was a rule sitting in a file. Write the oracle, prove it can
fail (mutation-test it), THEN claim the fix.

## ▶▶ THE CRITICAL PATH IS THE ONLY METRIC THAT MATTERS
Jörgen, 2026-08-26: "if there is one thing that doesnt work then the whole app seems not working as all is
connected experience." He is right, and it invalidates how the QA runs were being read. **"16 passed / 12
failed" is a meaningless number.** The app is ONE CHAIN — open → generate → approve → pipeline → done — and
a single break anywhere makes it unusable. 57% of features passing is not 57% of a working product; it is
a product that does not work.

`CRITICAL_PATH = ['quick-post', 'approve-jump', 'pipeline', 'flow-post-to-done']` in mobile-user.js.
Those four run FIRST (the run is re-sorted), and the report + console now OPEN with a binary verdict:
- **🔴 THE APP DOES NOT WORK TODAY** — names the step it breaks at + what the driver observed there.
- **✅ THE DAILY CHAIN COMPLETES** — only when ALL FOUR ran and passed.
- **⚠️ CHAIN ONLY PARTLY TESTED** — when `ONLY=` limited the run. (Caught in my own logic before shipping:
  the first version declared "COMPLETES" after a 1-of-4 partial run, which is exactly the false all-clear
  that has cost days. Never claim the chain works from a partial sample.)

Logic unit-tested on all four states (all-pass / one fail / one blocked / partial).
**Everything outside the chain — dark mode, spacing, copy, shelved features — is polish and must NEVER be
reported at the same weight as a broken link in the chain.**

### ⚠️ The verdict must never blame the APP for the HARNESS dying
First real run of the critical-path verdict produced a FALSE NEGATIVE: it printed "🔴 THE APP DOES NOT
WORK TODAY — breaks at quick-post" when quick-post's own Observed field said it had generated a complete
post ("Between Rounds Dilution … hook, script, caption, tags, shot list"). What actually died was the QA
DRIVER's LLM — `403 … used all available credits` — i.e. the vision model that JUDGES the screenshots,
which shares Jörgen's xAI account. The app was fine; the judge went dark, 26 features were marked blocked,
and the headline blamed the product.

Fixed: (1) new `DRIVER_DEAD` flag — when askLLM fails with 403/credits/quota/permission-denied the run
STOPS IMMEDIATELY (`break` out of the feature loop) instead of grinding out dozens of junk "blocked"
results judged by a dead model; (2) that feature is recorded as **`unknown`**, never `fail`; (3) the
headline becomes **"⚠️ RUN INVALID — COULD NOT JUDGE … this says nothing about whether your app works."**
Unit-tested: driver-died → RUN INVALID, genuine app break → still names the step, all-pass → CHAIN COMPLETES.

**THE GENERAL RULE: a test that cannot run must report "I don't know", never "it failed". A false negative
destroys trust exactly as fast as a false positive — arguably faster, because it sends you hunting a bug
that does not exist.** NOTE the QA driver and the app share one xAI account, so the driver can starve the
app (and vice versa); `QA_PROVIDER=openai|anthropic` puts the judge on a different account.


## ▶▶ USE THE `unlazy` SKILL FOR ALL SUBSTANTIAL WORK (Jörgen, 2026-08-26: "use my unlazy skill from now on")
Load it with the Skill tool (`anthropic-skills:unlazy`) at the START of any multi-part task, build, audit,
or parallel dispatch. Skip it only for a one-line edit or a factual answer.

**Why this is the right tool for THIS project specifically:** the single failure mode across hundreds of
versions has been a confident "fixed — deploy it" with no check behind it. unlazy makes that structurally
impossible: you write `GATES.md` BEFORE implementing, each gate is one observable outcome with a runnable
`CHECK:` + `EXPECT:`, and a gate counts as met only when the process exits zero AND the expectation matches.
A checked box with no evidence is UNMET. It is the enforced version of the lesson already written in this
file and repeatedly ignored — *"a fix that is unverifiable is a hypothesis, and hypotheses come back."*

**The rule it enforces, which is the one that matters here: if I cannot measure it, I do not get to say it
is fixed.** Anything only Jörgen can confirm (how it looks on his phone, whether a take is in sync, whether
the writing is good enough) is a MANUAL gate and an explicit HANDOFF — never silently reported as done.
`ABANDON: <id> <reason>` is terminal and exits 1 with HANDOFF REQUIRED; it is never success.

Key commands (skill dir is under `.../skills/unlazy`):
- `node <skill-dir>/scripts/gate-lint.mjs GATES.md` — lint the ledger BEFORE working it, so an oracle that
  cannot fail is caught at authoring time instead of certified at report time.
- `node <skill-dir>/scripts/gate-check.mjs --status GATES.md` — parse without executing anything.
- `node <skill-dir>/scripts/gate-check.mjs --approve GATES.md` — approve commands I wrote/understand, then run.
- `--reverify` on every returned leaf. `--status` is NOT re-execution.

Pairs with the parallel rule below: in orchestrated mode every leaf and branch gets its OWN gates file and
its own disjoint `OWNS:` paths. Keep check execution sequential unless the gates are genuinely independent.

## ▶▶ RUN INDEPENDENT WORK IN PARALLEL (Jörgen's working rule, 2026-08-26)
"You are allowed to run multiple sub-agents at the same time. When the plan has independent tasks, dispatch
them together in one batch instead of waiting for each one to finish. Only run tasks one after another when
a task genuinely needs another task's output. Before dispatching, check the planned file so two agents never
edit the same file."

**How to apply it here:** map FILE OWNERSHIP before dispatching — one file, one agent, no exceptions. This
codebase makes that easy because the surfaces are separate: `app.html` (the entire frontend, ONE agent only
— it is a single 820KB file so two agents editing it WILL collide), `api/*.js` (one agent per endpoint is
safe), `mobile-user.js` (harness), `vercel.json` + `sw.js` + `scripts/` (deploy plumbing), `CLAUDE.md`.

**Sequential ONLY when there is a real dependency**, e.g. anything that must run AFTER `scripts/stamp-build.js`
(it hashes the final app.html, so it is always the last step), or a fix that depends on a diagnosis.

**The standing split when work resumes:**
| Batch | Task | Files owned |
|---|------|-------------|
| A | Output-quality diagnosis — where brand voice gets diluted between the brain and the generated post | `api/generate-ideas.js`, `api/_brain.js` (read-only) |
| B | Stale-data surfacing — panels showing week-old data with no indication (Trends especially) | `app.html` |
| C | Verify deployed fixes — read the new `xAI EMPTY 200` / timeout lines in production | no files |

A is the one that decides whether the product is worth using, and it is BLOCKED on Jörgen's judgment:
"the output isn't good enough" cannot be diagnosed without knowing WHICH part falls short (wrong angle /
flat voice / weak hook / vague facts). Ask before dispatching A.

- **cs-v603 = TELEPROMPTER voice-follow JUMPED AHEAD — it matched your speech to a line further DOWN the script (Jörgen, filming by hand: "it toke my voice but not from the line but somewhere from lowers part").** Read `tpVoiceMatch` and found THREE compounding causes: **(1) `need = 2` — only two matching words accepted a position, anywhere in a 45-word forward window; (2) matching is FUZZY (`tpWordNear` = same first 4 chars, length ±3), so "you"≈"your", "their"≈"there"; (3) the v488 tie-break deliberately preferred the FURTHEST-FORWARD match ("so we follow the latest match when you speed up").** Together: say "the" and "you", and if those recur 30 words later the prompter accepts THAT position and jumps — exactly the reported symptom, because filler words appear everywhere in a script and carry no information about WHERE you are. **Fix (v603, all in `tpVoiceMatch`): (a) new `TP_STOPWORDS` + `TP_CONTENT_WORD(w)` (>=3 chars AND not filler) — only CONTENT words earn a hit, so a filler-only echo can no longer move the prompter at all; (b) tie-break now prefers the NEAREST forward match, not the furthest — lagging is recoverable (you keep reading), jumping ahead loses your place completely; (c) a leap of >18 words must be EARNED with 3+ content hits instead of 2.** Threshold is >=3 chars deliberately, NOT >=4: 'way', 'fix', 'key' are real evidence, and filler is excluded by the stoplist rather than by length (at >=4 a legitimate fast-forward like "cheapest way to get sodium" scored only 2 and was wrongly rejected — caught by the bench below). **Verified by EXTRACTING the real matcher from app.html and benchmarking it standalone, 5/5 cases: real speech near cursor tracks (->7), filler-only "you the" and "and it is" both correctly refuse to move (-1), an earned far leap still works (->27), mid-script continuation tracks (->18).** 5/5 inline scripts parse.

This is the app's core promise (your approvals survive a refresh) and NOTHING has ever tested it — if `reconcileLocalStatus` or the DB load regressed, a user's whole pipeline could silently reset and we would only hear about it from a customer.** **(2) `remix-sources` — Remix has FIVE source lanes (tiktok / youtube / article / paste / file) each hitting a DIFFERENT backend fetcher (`transcribe-url.js`, `extract-article.js`, …), and only the PASTE lane was ever tested; the test now drives the Article lane (a real Wikipedia URL) and the YouTube lane, and treats a clear "couldn't read that link" message as acceptable handling but a silent nothing / raw error dump as a FAIL.** **(3) `quick-post-formats` widened from 3 formats to ALL SIX** (video, statement, carousel, micro, qna, static — bonus excluded, it is a day not a format), budget 16 → 30, since the whole point is that each renders a structurally different card. **(4) `settings-autofill` — the three brand-brain crawlers (Scan my whole site / From my social posts / Pull customer reviews) have NEVER been run by the sim despite each being a 1-2 minute real backend crawl; the test runs one, demands a live progress state, and fails on a frozen button or a raw error.** **(5) `carousel-maker` — "Make Slides" is an entire feature with zero coverage; the test checks multiple real slides, text that is not truncated/overflowing, working navigation and an export control.** Verified: mobile-user.js parses, 35 unique ids, no duplicates, reload plumbing wired (2 refs). **STILL DELIBERATELY OUT: real publish (needs a connected live channel — would post publicly), file-upload remix (needs a real file), onboarding wizard (needs a throwaway magic-link signup), mic/TTS (device media).**

- **cs-v602 (harness) = why `proof-actions` reported proof-DATA's results — and the fix that makes it impossible.** Both proof features were built as `window._qaProof = (function(){ var out={}; ...; return out; })()` — the assignment happens ONLY at the very end, so **any uncaught throw in a later section discarded every earlier result AND left the PREVIOUS feature's object sitting in `window._qaProof`**, which the driver then dutifully reported as this feature's (that is exactly what happened: proof-actions printed bookmarkAdd/notebookSave/guard* — proof-data's keys). Ruled out my new markDoneButton code as the cause by EXTRACTING the taps body and running it against stubbed app globals: it completes and returns all 6 keys, so the block is sound and something environmental in the real page threw. Fix is structural rather than another guess: **`var out = { __ran:'started' }; window._qaProof = out;` published IMMEDIATELY**, so results survive a later throw and the final assignment is a no-op. Driver instruction updated: `__ran` present + a missing key now means "the block died there — name which keys are present/missing and FAIL", and it must never report another feature's keys as its own. **LESSON: a diagnostic that only publishes its results at the end can lose them all AND silently inherit the previous run's — publish incrementally so a partial result is still evidence.** Verified: mobile-user.js parses, patched in BOTH proof features (count asserted = 2), and re-ran the stub harness to confirm partial results survive a mid-block throw.

z-index:2`. **(4) "Develop into post" landed on `.nav-tab`** — the fixed bottom nav sat on top of Idea Catcher's primary button → `.view` padding-bottom `128px` → **`152px`** so a last-in-view control always clears the nav. **ALSO FIXED — my own reporting flaw: `hard = allErrors.length` counted every CLICK BLOCKED diagnostic as a HARD ERROR, so a clean run reported "13 hard error(s)" that were all just my instrumentation.** Hard errors now exclude them and blocked taps get their own labelled counter. **RUN CAVEATS for triage (do NOT treat the tail as signal): the xAI key ran OUT OF CREDITS mid-run (`shrimp` blocked with a 403 "used all available credits"), so late features are unreliable; and `brand-switch` switched the active brand to PX1 LABS partway, so `flow-post-to-done`'s filming/done counts were measured on a DIFFERENT brand than `pipeline`'s.** **CONFIRMED BY TEST, not assumed: `guardLogoRemove: WORKS with no event` and `guardFqDone: WORKS with no event` — the v601 handler guards genuinely hold when called with no event, which is the exact case that used to throw.** **STILL OPEN: `proof-actions` reported proof-DATA's object (its own IIFE threw before assigning, so markDone/markDoneButton never reported) — the markDoneButton probe has not yet produced a verdict and Mark Done remains unexplained.** Verified: 5/5 inline scripts parse, CSS brace-balanced, v602 in both files.
- **cs-v601 (11th batch) = the next sim now VERIFIES this session's own fixes instead of assuming them (harness only, no new app code).** Jörgen asked whether anything should be built before the next run. Answer: **no new features** — shipping fresh code right before a validation run makes every failure ambiguous (old breakage or my new work?), and the whole point of this run is a clean read. What IS worth adding is coverage, and the highest-value coverage is of the v601 guards themselves. **Added 2 probes to the EXISTING `proof-data` feature rather than new features** (probes run inside one taps block = no extra driver turns, no extra LLM cost): **`guardLogoRemove`** sets a dummy `settings.brandLogo` then calls `removeBrandLogo()` **with NO event** — the exact case that used to throw on `e.stopPropagation()` before clearing — and asserts the logo actually cleared, then restores the original; **`guardFqDone`** calls `fqDone(undefined, id)` **with NO event** and (allowing for the 200ms defer) asserts done went up by one, then moves the idea back. - **cs-v601 (10th batch) = generalised the pipeAdvance find — swept every handler for "incidental code that can throw ahead of the real action".** The Mark Done bug was a CLASS, not a one-off, so I grepped every named handler that takes an event and uses it immediately. **Two more had the identical shape and are now guarded: (1) `fqDone(e, id)` — the filming-queue Done button — opened with a BARE `e.stopPropagation()` and then `e.target.closest('.fq-item')` for a row-exit animation, both before the deferred `moveStage(id,'done')`; either throwing killed the mark-done entirely. (2) `removeBrandLogo(e)` — a bare `e.stopPropagation()` before `settings.brandLogo=''; saveSettings()`, so a missing event meant the logo silently never got removed.** Both now wrap the incidental part in try/catch and put the real work behind its own guard, same as pipeAdvance. **Checked and deliberately NOT changed: `handleLogoUpload(e)` / `handleFounderPhoto(e)` (the event IS the payload — `e.target.files[0]` — so there is no separate "real action" to protect; already fall back to `this`), `micErrMsg(e)` (that `e` is an Error, not an event, and is already `e && e.name` guarded), and the three document-level `if (!e.target.closest(...))` close-on-outside-click listeners (they are guards, not actions, and always receive a real event from a real listener).** **THE RULE, now applied app-wide: in any handler, `stopPropagation`, exit animations and other decoration must be wrapped or moved AFTER the state change — never allowed to run first and throw ahead of it.** Verified: 5/5 inline scripts parse, all three guards present.
- **cs-v601 (9th batch) = THE MARK-DONE MYSTERY — found the missing link by reading the BUTTON, not the function.** The whole run's biggest contradiction (`proof-actions` says markDone WORKS 32→33, the `pipeline` + `flow-post-to-done` UI tests say tapping it does nothing) had a stupidly simple cause I kept missing: **the button does NOT call `moveStage`. It calls `pipeAdvance(event, id, 'done')`** — I had only ever read `moveStage`, which is why the proof test (which calls `moveStage` directly) and the UI disagreed. `pipeAdvance` was:\n```js\nconst card = e.target.closest('.pipeline-card');   // cosmetic exit animation\nif (card) card.classList.add('leaving');\nsetTimeout(() => { moveStage(id, stage); }, 200);   // the actual work\n```\n**The cosmetic line runs BEFORE the state change and was completely unguarded — if `e` or `e.target` is ever missing/detached, `.closest` throws, the function exits, and `moveStage` is never scheduled. The button silently does nothing while the underlying function is perfectly healthy.** That is exactly the reported signature. Fixed: the animation is now wrapped in try/catch and `moveStage` is in its own guarded `setTimeout`, so a decorative effect can NEVER block the action again. **RULE: cosmetic code must never run before, or be able to throw ahead of, the functional code in the same handler — put the animation in a try/catch or after the state change.** **HONEST: I could not reproduce the throw, so this is a proven FRAGILITY rather than a proven root cause** — which is why the harness now also instruments it: `proof-actions` gained a **`markDoneButton`** check that finds the REAL rendered "Mark Done" button, records `elementFromPoint` at its centre, clicks it, and (because pipeAdvance defers by 200ms) resolves the verdict asynchronously into `window._qaProof` 700ms later — reporting either "WORKS via real button click", or "BROKEN — COVERED BY .x", or "BROKEN — nothing covering it, so pipeAdvance/moveStage never ran". It reads the idea id out of the button's own `onclick` (pipeline cards have NO `data-id` — my first version silently failed to restore) and moves the idea back to `filming` afterwards so the brand is left untouched. Next run answers this definitively.

- **BRAND-BEATS-RULES PRECEDENCE + rhythm/drama anti-slop (backend-only, ships with the v600 deploy — Jörgen asked whether adding stop-slop/humanizer skills would "limit self-evolvement"; investigating found the app was ALREADY limiting it).** He named `hardikpandya/stop-slop` (15.9k★, MIT) and `blader/humanizer` (MIT, 33 Wikipedia-derived patterns). Read both. **Verdict: take the patterns, not the repos — `writingCraft()` already covered ~65%** (em dashes, negative parallelism, rule-of-three, AI vocab, copula avoidance, false ranges, "In today's", filler, rhythm, straight quotes). **THE REAL FIND (his instinct was right, and it was live): prompt ORDER meant the generic rules were silently overriding the brand brain.** Every generator builds its prompt as `fullBrandBlock(bc)` FIRST → `writingCraft()` LAST (verified in remix.js L118 and the same shape elsewhere), so the universal anti-slop rules sat closest to the task AND were labelled "mandatory" — meaning a brand whose LEARNED voice genuinely uses a three-beat rhythm, a dash, or a signature repeated phrase got flattened back to neutral by its own guardrails. The app learns taste and then overwrites it. (blader hit the identical problem — their 2.9.0 changelog: "made a user's voice sample outrank the em dash ban.") FIX: new **`rulePrecedence()`** block, always LAST in the prompt — "the BRAND section wins any conflict with the general writing rules; those exist to remove generic slop, NOT to overwrite a voice this brand has earned; only apply a rule where the brand has said nothing." So static rules = the FLOOR, brand brain = the IDENTITY, and self-evolution is protected rather than capped. Also added **`antiSlopRhythm()`** — the genuinely-missing tells, all rhythm/drama rather than word-level (manufactured punchlines "No preference. No prior. No nostalgia.", aphorism formulas, fake-candid openers "Honestly?", signposting, significance inflation, vague attribution, synonym cycling, sycophancy/hedging stacks) — these are exactly the ones that survive a word-level clean-up in SHORT-FORM SOCIAL, which is what this app writes. **COVERAGE TRAP CAUGHT: `generate-ideas.js` (which powers BOTH Ideas and Quick Post — the two most-used generators) and `sharpen.js` do NOT call `writingCraft` at all** (they keep their own tuned prompts and only append `clarityFlow`), so a change inside writingCraft would have missed them entirely. That is why both blocks were extracted as SEPARATE exported functions and appended directly to those two as well — all 7 generators verified covered by grep. Verified: all 8 api files parse + `require()` clean, `writingCraft` still ends with the precedence block (asserted by splitting on blank lines and checking the LAST one). Backend-only → no APP_VERSION/BUILD bump.

All now read `getVisibleIdeas()`. Grep-verified 0 `new Set(state.map(s => s.title` left. **Consequence to be aware of: a new idea MAY now duplicate the title of a hidden one. That is intended — generation only targets switched-on formats, so the collision is across two different formats (same topic, different post), and the alternative was paying for output nobody can reach.** Re-enabling a format brings its ideas back with their titles intact; from that moment they count toward anti-repeat again. **Also in this bump: the Done-tab undo tooltip `Back to Film & Post` → `Undo — move back to Film & Post`** — it is an icon-only ↶ button, so the string is its `title`/`aria-label`; naming only the destination read like advice to go film something rather than reversing the Done you just tapped. - **cs-v600b = trends had NO sources — fixed at the origin, both lanes (Jörgen, screenshot of the Auto-pulled panel: "no sources. all need to have sources").** The UI was never the problem: the chip renderer already emitted a `source ↗` link whenever `t.link` existed. The prompt now demands the direct URL of the page it read, with an explicit "never invent, guess, shorten or reconstruct a URL — leave the item out instead" rule, and the parser keeps `it.url || it.link` **only when it matches `^https?://[^\s<>"']+$` and is ≤400 chars** (smoke-tested: real http/https kept; scheme-less, spaced, empty, and `javascript:` all rejected — that last one also closes an XSS vector into an `href`). **(2) The manual "Pull fresh trends" lane dropped it too** — the v453 merge loop in `pullWebTrends` pushed `{text, ts}` only, so every hand-pulled chip lost its attribution before it was ever stored; it now carries `source` + a URL-validated `link`. **Fallback so nothing renders bare:** both chip renderers (auto panel + "Trends you've taught it") now show `source ↗` when there's a link, else the source NAME as a muted `.vl-src-name` label, else nothing (correct for a trend the user typed themselves). **HONEST STATE: the Auto-pulled panel is written by the DAILY CRON, so the existing chips keep `link:''` until it next runs — sources appear on the next pull, not on deploy. - **▶▶ ROOT CAUSE of "The AI is having a moment" on EVERY big generation — FOUND (QA run #2, 7 pass / 9 fail / 1 blocked; backend-only fix, ships with the next deploy).** The run made the pattern unmistakable: **every single failure was a generation failure** (quick-post, remix, idea-catcher, questions→Answer-this, notebook develop, BOTH flows) while **`assistant` PASSED with a real Grok reply naming competitors** — so xAI was up and credits were fine. The difference is SIZE: brand-voice-chat asks for ~800 tokens and returns in seconds; the generators ask for a full JSON batch (a week of ideas with scripts, a remix, a viral breakdown). **`grok-4.6` is a REASONING model — it burns time thinking before emitting** — so those big calls routinely ran past `httpsPost`'s hardcoded **55s** cut → `callXAI` returned null → callLLM threw the "having a moment" message. This is exactly why the complaints started at v570 (the 4.5→4.6 switch) and why my v593 triage was WRONG to write it off as "transient xAI flakiness — those endpoints already have 45-60s budgets": 60s is not enough for a reasoning model doing large JSON. FIX (3 parts): (1) **`api/_llm.js` httpsPost default timeout 55s → 240s** (the real ceiling is each function's maxDuration); (2) **vercel.json: maxDuration → 300** for every heavy generator (generate-ideas, remix, viral-analyze, viral-rewrite, viral-twist, sharpen, expand-field — video-beats was already 300); (3) **retry budget 40s → 150s** in callXAI, since a slow reasoning call ate the old budget and silently skipped every retry. **IF GENERATION IS STILL SLOW after this, the remaining lever is `reasoning_effort` on grok-4.6 (xAI supports it) — low effort for mechanical JSON generation would cut latency a lot, but Jörgen said "we don't touch reasoning effort", so it is FLAGGED not done.** **HARNESS GAP FIXED in the same pass: `requestfailed` was tracked for the idle-wait counter but never LOGGED — a request dying at the network level (timeout/reset on a slow line) produced no response, so it was invisible and the report said "No captured-errors line". Now logged as `NETWORK FAIL <url> — <errorText>`.**

- **ASSISTANT-CHAT "Something went wrong" ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED (backend-only, ships with the next deploy — Jörgen's screenshot: the "Competitors" message failed while a normal coach reply worked; he'd already topped up xAI credits, so credits were NOT it).** Found by reading, not guessing: `api/brand-voice-chat.js` had **`maxDuration: 30`** (vercel.json), but any user message matching `/competitor|rival|trend|news|latest|viral|.../` fires the OPTIONAL live web-search branch (`callGrokSearch` → xAI `/v1/responses` + web_search tool), whose OWN timeout is **90s**. So a "competitors" question ran a web search that blew past the 30s function budget → Vercel killed the whole request → the chat 500'd, while plain messages (no search keyword) returned in a few seconds and worked. Web-verified `grok-4.6` IS a valid API model id (docs.x.ai) — ruled the model string out. FIX: (1) the search is now `Promise.race([callGrokSearch(...), setTimeout(()=>null, 18000)])` — capped at 18s so it can NEVER hang the chat past the budget (callGrokSearch already resolves null on error, so racing a null-timeout is clean; if the search is slow it's silently dropped and the coach answers from its own knowledge, which was always the design); (2) `maxDuration` 30 → **60** for headroom (18s search + ~20s chat fits comfortably; his plan already runs video-beats at 300 so 60 is fine). Backend-only (api + vercel.json) → NO APP_VERSION/BUILD bump. **LESSON: an OPTIONAL, silent-fail helper (web search) must be time-boxed BELOW the function's maxDuration — a try/catch catches errors but NOT slowness, and a slow-but-succeeding call still gets the whole request platform-killed.**

So the recorded take is now ALWAYS either genuinely-blurred-with-live-frames OR raw-and-synced — never the broken middle state. **STILL UNRESOLVED / NEEDS HIS ANSWER: is the lip-sync drift also present with blur OFF?** If yes → it's the v533 1080p render (heavier per-frame paint may lag 1x playback) not blur, and the next lever is adaptive SP_SS / seek-based render. If no → this gate fixed it. The render's v501 play→frame→record order + v530 drift probe are unchanged. Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, all greps green (v535/v536 intact). - **cs-v535 = background-blur take raised to true 1080×1920 HD (Jörgen: "it needs to be high quality 1080 hd").** v534's blur canvas was 720×1280 for perf caution. Key realisation: MediaPipe Selfie Segmentation runs at its OWN fixed input resolution, so the ML inference cost — the real bottleneck — is INDEPENDENT of the canvas size; enlarging the canvas only grows the (GPU-accelerated) `drawImage`/`blur` compositing draws, which are cheap. So the blur canvas is now `W=1080, H=1920` → the recorded blur-on take matches the blur-off 1080p path, and the v533 render composites a 1080p source either way. - **cs-v534 = BACKGROUND BLUR (portrait mode) while filming — OPT-IN, fully isolated (Jörgen picked "B" = blur the real background behind him, not the b-roll photo, after I flagged it as the hard one).** ARCHITECTURE CHOICE (the safe one): blur happens at FILM time, NOT render time — camera → live MediaPipe Selfie Segmentation → a canvas that composites the sharp person over a `blur(12px)` copy of the frame → `canvas.captureStream(30)` + the raw audio track = the stream the recorder + preview use. So the RECORDED take is already blurred and the v533 1080p split-screen render is **100% untouched** (it just composites an already-blurred take). Render-time blur was rejected: the render plays the video at 1× and captures audio live via rVFC, so per-frame ML inference there would drop frames / desync (the exact v483/v501 failure) or force a full seek-based re-architecture. **`tpBlur` module** (self-contained, before startTpRecord): lazy-loads `@mediapipe/selfie_segmentation@0.1` from jsdelivr ONLY when the toggle is first turned on; `start(rawStream)` builds a hidden video + 720×1280 canvas + segmenter (`modelSelection:1`), runs an independent rAF `send()` pump, returns the blurred outStream (canvas video + shared audio); `stop()` kills the loop + closes the segmenter + stops ONLY the canvas video track (the audio track belongs to the camera — never stopped). **Toggle** = a "Blur bg" `.tp-voice-btn` next to "Follow me" (`tpToggleBgBlur` → `tp_bg_blur` localStorage → `tpApplyBlurPreference`); default OFF, hidden while `.recording` like the other options (set it before Record). **Wiring (6 minimal splices):** record `tpActiveStream()` (blurred-or-raw) instead of `tpCameraStream`; `tpEnsureCamera` applies the pref once the camera is up; `startTpRecord` gives blur a chance to be ready; teardown in `stopTpCamera` + the recording-close onstop path. **GRACEFUL EVERYWHERE:** model load fail / init throw / no SelfieSegmentation → `start` returns null → pref auto-reset to OFF + "not available on this phone" toast + films RAW. Cannot block a take, cannot touch the default (blur-off) flow, cannot touch the render. **HONEST RISKS (untestable from here — needs his device):** (1) live segmentation at 30fps WHILE the teleprompter scroll + VAD + speech-recognition also run is heavy — a slow phone will capture fewer fps (choppier take, but MediaRecorder muxes canvas frames against the real-time audio track so A/V stay aligned); (2) mask haloing around hair/glasses is inherent to on-device segmentation; (3) blur-on takes are 720×1280 (the seg canvas) vs 1080p for blur-off — a deliberate perf/quality trade (note if he wants it raised). Knobs: `blur(12px)` strength, `modelSelection` 0=faster/1=better, canvas W/H. Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, all 13 greps green (v531/v532/v533 intact). - **cs-v533 = SPLIT SCREEN AT TRUE 1080×1920 (Jörgen: "the quality need to be high of these videos not low").** The camera films 1080p but the render composited at 720×1280 @8Mbps = a visible downscale. **The clean lever: SUPERSAMPLING — all layout math stays in 720-logical units; the canvases get a `SP_SS = 1.5` transform** so every existing draw call lands at 1080p with ZERO constant changes (fonts/x/iy/chips untouched). Footage maps ~1:1 from the 1080p camera (cover-scale 0.667 × 1.5 = 1.0). Bitrate 8M→**14M** (camera records ~12M; VBR keeps real sizes moderate). **Backend `api/stock-photo.js`: PICK_SIZE `large`→`large2x`** (~1880px, falls back large→medium→original) so the photo band is sharp at 1080 wide. - **cs-v532 = SHARED SPLIT SCREEN LOST ITS AUDIO — Opus-in-mp4 (Jörgen: "rendered and all ok but audio was there but when i shared then no audio anymore").** The tell: the SAME blob had sound in the in-app result player but none after sharing → the bytes contain audio the RECEIVER can't decode. Cause: the render's mime pick was bare `'video/mp4'`, and Chrome's MediaRecorder muxes **OPUS** audio into mp4 unless AAC is requested explicitly — Chrome decodes Opus-in-mp4 (hence the preview had sound), but WhatsApp/galleries/social transcoders don't → shared file plays silent. Fixes in `renderSplitScreen`: **(1) codec ladder** `_mimeCands` = `video/mp4;codecs=avc1.42E01E,mp4a.40.2` (H.264+**AAC**, plays everywhere) → quoted variant → bare mp4 → webm; per spec `isTypeSupported` must honour accepted codecs, so a true = real AAC. **(2)** `window._spLastMime = rec.mimeType || mime` so the next audio report is diagnosable (check it in DevTools / ask him to read it). **(3)** blob/File type = bare container (`mime.split(';')[0]`) — codec params inside a File type upset some share targets; ext via `indexOf('mp4')`. TELEPROMPTER RECORDER DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED — plain takes have always shared with sound (different pick path, don't fix what works). RESIDUAL RISK (honest): if his Chrome rejects the AAC strings, the ladder lands on bare mp4 = same Opus behaviour — if the retest still shares silent, read `window._spLastMime`; if it lacks `mp4a`, the device has no AAC encoder and the next lever is muxing the RAW take's audio track or a webm share. Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, all 8 greps green (v531 intact). NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v531 = RENDER-CHAIN AUDIT (Jörgen: "do a quick audit bug check for this function") — 4 real bugs found by reading the whole renderSplitScreen chain, all fixed.** **(1) THE LIKELY CAUSE OF HIS FAILED SPLIT: nothing held the screen awake during the render.** While FILMING the camera keeps the screen on; the render phase has no camera — on a ~1min build the screen dims/locks (or he switches apps), rVFC/rAF freeze while the detached take's AUDIO plays on, frames stop pushing → the watchdog kills it or the timeline corrupts → the (pre-v530 silent) plain-video fallback. Fixes: **screen wake lock** for the whole build (`navigator.wakeLock.request('screen')`, hoisted `_wl`, released on success AND failure), **visibilitychange pause/resume** — hidden → `vid.pause()` + `rec.pause()` (paused span simply absent from output, A/V stay aligned); visible → resume both + stall clock reset — and a ticker line "Keep the app open — it pauses if you leave…". **(2) hard-stop was a `setTimeout` that kept counting through a backgrounded pause** → now a `deadline` checked inside the watchdog, extended by exactly the hidden span on resume. **(3) A PARTIAL render passed the drift probe cleanly** (watchdog gives up mid-clip but keeps lastT>0.5s; probe compares blob duration vs CONSUMED footage — a half-length video matches itself) → shipped as "✓ ready to post" with no warning. Now `resolve({…, partial})` when `dur - lastT > 0.75` (finish() snapshots `lastT = max(lastT, currentTime)` first — watch only sampled every 700ms) → amber "stopped early — shorter than your take" warning on the result sheet. **(4) empty beats array → `layers[-1]` → the no-layer cream fallback painted the WHOLE clip** = a "split" with zero b-roll that looked successful → now an explicit `throw 'no graphics track came back'` (lands in the v530 loud-fail sheet with retry). `cleanupVis()` on all 4 exit lanes (finish/cancel/deadline/stall); outer catch receives only already-cleaned rejections. AUDITED-OK (don't re-chase): muted-retry keeps captured audio flowing (element mute ≠ stream mute), capture-before-play safe (rec.start() is after play), 8Mbps memory fine, catch cleanup (_vid/_rec) intact from v507, retry lane re-enters _spGo cleanly with cached beats/photos. Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, all greps green (v529+v530 intact). NEEDS `vercel --prod`.

Your take is safe." + **[Try the split again]** (the go handler is now named `_spGo` so retry re-runs it; beats + photos are cached so a retry is free — decode/play hiccups are transient) + **[Just save the plain video]**; `window._spLastFail` records the reason. **(2) drift probe → WARNING, not discard:** the render is handed to `tpSplitResult(…, warn)` which shows an amber "Check it before posting — N.Ns timing wobble… use the plain video below" line above the player — the sheet PLAYS the video, so he judges lips with his eyes ("Use the plain video instead" was already a button there). - **cs-v508 = EYE-LINE MODE — while recording, the script rides up under the front camera so reading reads as eye contact (Jörgen: "what can we do with the seeable eyes reading mode? so it cant be seen from eyes that im reading a script?"; picked "Eye-line mode while recording" from AskUserQuestion).** Physics: the tell is the angle between the text and the lens. Old reading line at 38% ≈ 6.9cm below the lens at arm's length = **7.8° downward gaze** (clearly "reading"); line at 14% = 3.0cm = **3.5°**, under the ~5° threshold where gaze offset stops being noticeable. **Implementation in two halves: (1) `tpReadFrac()`** — ONE source of truth for the reading position (`.recording` on the overlay → 0.14, else 0.38), swept through EVERY constant that encoded it: the take-start jump, `_tpReadOffset` (beat timing), `tpVoiceScrollTo`'s target, and both travel-distance formulas (now `1 - 2*tpReadFrac()`; grep-asserted zero stray `clientHeight * 0.38/0.24` left). Ordering verified by index: `.recording` is added inside `startTpRecord`, which tpRecordTap AWAITS before the snapshot/jump — so geometry and render always agree. **(2) CSS block (end of stylesheet)**: `.recording` hides the top bar (opacity 0) + gear + advanced row + primer, pins `.teleprompter-body` fullscreen (`inset:0`, padding-top 30px), moves `.tp-read-line` to **14%**, drops the controls row to a **fixed bottom Stop pill** (gradient scrim, safe-area padding), bumps timer/mode-chip to z-7, and draws a **9px lavender lens ring at top-centre (`::after`, z-8)** marking where to look.
