NOTE: primer `display:none` while recording happens BEFORE the `_tpWordTops` snapshot (same class), so word positions are measured in the layout that's actually on screen. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, CSS braces balanced, all 17 greps green, angle maths computed. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v507 = SELF-AUDIT of today's work (Jörgen: "do we have any other bug on what we have done today? check.") — found 4, fixed 4, and the worst would have re-triggered his #1 complaint at ~22s into every long take.** **(1) THE v506 NOISE FLOOR CLIMBED INTO HIS VOICE.** `noiseFloor *= 1.002` every 30ms tick regardless of speaking → +7%/s; with continuous speech (rms ~0.09, no pause >300ms) the threshold crosses the voice level at **~22 seconds** and the gate closes — the script would have STOPPED mid-take while he talked, i.e. the exact "doesn't match my speed" complaint, reintroduced by my own hardening. Floor now adapts ONLY during silence (`+= (lvl-floor)*0.05`, clamped [0.0005, 0.05]) and freezes while speaking — simulated 40s continuous read: old gates at 22s, new never gates. **(2) RETAKE state leak.** `tpVoiceCursor = 0` lives only inside the FULL `tpBuildVoiceIndex` build; a Retake (and a preview-play-then-record) reuses the DOM so the index early-returns via `voiceIndexed='1'` → the matcher searched forward from the END of take one (zero matches all take), `tpVoiceLastAdvanceDone` stayed true, and the `.said` fading from take one persisted on screen. tpRecordTap's v505 snapshot block now resets cursor/flag/`_tpSyncTargetY` + strips `.said` EVERY take. **(3) VAD freeze modes.** An AudioContext created after the 2.4s countdown can start `'suspended'` (no direct gesture) — analyser then reads pure zeros → rms 0 < threshold → gate → 0 → **script frozen forever**. Now: `ctx.resume()` on suspended, `tpVadLevel()` returns null unless `ctx.state === 'running'`, and a pure-zero rms (<0.0005 — a real mic never reads digital zero) also returns null; null = gate stays OPEN, so a broken tap degrades to timed scroll, never to a frozen script. **(4) Cancelled/failed render kept PLAYING HIS TAKE OUT LOUD.** `renderSplitScreen`'s catch was bare `reject(e)` — the detached `<video>` (muted=false, needed for captured audio) kept playing after cancel/watchdog-fail, audible until the clip ended, recorder possibly still running, blob URL leaked. Hoisted `_vid/_rec`, catch now pauses+revokes+stops. **Checked and CONFIRMED OK (don't re-audit): scroll track cleared both stop paths + fresh per take; `_tpWordTops` re-snapshotted per take (offsetTop is scroll-independent); watchdog under `_tpSyncOn` loses only the corrector; slider live-read mid-take; v501 `lastT` hoist + play→frame→record order; preview play button legacy path; `:has()` on Chrome 151; the VAD tap cannot disturb MediaRecorder (same stream, zero-gain sink).** Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, all 15 greps green, floor behaviour simulated old-vs-new. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v506 = THE SCRIPT NOW FOLLOWS HIS ACTUAL VOICE — closed-loop on the mic level, recognition demoted to corrector (Jörgen, 4th pace report: "the script running speed doesnt still sync with how my reading and saying speed is… why its so hard to get it right. but if you fix this then the lipsync and motiongraphics cant suffer all needs to sync perfectly").** **WHY IT TOOK 4 ROUNDS (own it): every prior fix made the metronome more accurate (geometry v488, inputs v492, platform overrides v494) — but an open-loop metronome can never match a human. The only closed-loop signal was speech recognition, which is unreliable on his device. The fix is a closed-loop source that ALWAYS exists: the audio level of the stream being recorded.** New **`tpStartRecordingScroll()`** replaces `startTpScroll` for takes (tpRecordTap only; the preview play button keeps the old path): a 30ms loop where **(1) feedforward** = geometry pace at **125wpm of SPEAKING time** (deliberately lag-biased — a waiting script is recoverable, a script that scrolled your line away is not); **(2) voice gate** = **`tpVadStart()`** taps `tpCameraStream` with AudioContext→Analyser→zero-gain→destination (muted pull, no echo, zero conflict — it's the SAME stream MediaRecorder consumes), `tpVadLevel()` returns RMS, adaptive noise floor (fast down, +0.2%/tick up, cap .05), threshold `max(0.012, floor*2.5+.004)`, **380ms grace** so word gaps don't stall, `gate += (want-gate)*0.16` easing → **talk = move, pause = the script rests and WAITS**; **(3) recognition correction** = `tpVoiceScrollTo` under `_tpSyncOn` no longer scrollTo's — it sets a **forward-only `_tpSyncTargetY`**, and the loop (only while the match is <2.6s fresh) adds `min(err*0.07, 9)`px when behind or scales by `max(0.25, 1+err/500)` when ahead — smooth steering, no jumps. Integration hardening: the v497 creep bridge is gated off under `_tpSyncOn`; `tpVoiceFallback` under `_tpSyncOn` just flips the chip to 'timed' (the loop never stops moving — losing recognition now loses only the corrector); `stopTpScroll` clears `tpSyncIv` + `_tpSyncOn` + `tpVadStop()` (AudioContext closed both stop paths via stopTpScroll). **Graphics + lipsync unaffected by construction: beats cue off the ACTUAL scroll (v505) so they inherit whatever the script does; lipsync is the v501 record-ordering, untouched.** Simulated vs a real pattern (118wpm, pauses of 2.5s+4s): old metronome finished 15s early / 40% ahead mid-take; the engine rests through both pauses and lands the last line at his last word. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, all 21 greps green, engine simulated. NEEDS `vercel --prod`. **If pace STILL feels off after this, the next question is exactly which chip ('following your voice' vs 'auto-scroll') and whether pauses still move — the failure modes are now separable.**
- **cs-v505 = GRAPHICS NOW CUED OFF THE SCRIPT'S OWN MOVEMENT — the beats land on the line he's actually reading (Jörgen: "how script moves and how motiongraphics moves are not in sync again. what the hell. fix and harden.").** **I HAD BEEN FIXING THE WRONG SYNC.** v483/v501 chased lips-vs-audio; his complaint was graphics-vs-script. **The real defect: beat timing depended ENTIRELY on `window._tpVoiceTimeline`, which is only written inside `tpVoiceScrollTo` — i.e. only when speech recognition successfully matched words.** No voice-follow, no recognition, a non-English locale (the v494 bug), a fallback to timed scroll, or beats cached without a `cue` field → `tpBeatTimes` returned null → `renderSplitScreen` fell back to `Math.floor(t / per)`, **dividing the clip evenly by beat count**. Graphics on a metronome, unrelated to the words. Fix: cue them off **the scroll position**, which is literally "how the script moves" and exists in BOTH modes. **(1)** `tpRecordTap` now always runs `tpBuildVoiceIndex()` (was voice-follow-only) and snapshots `window._tpWordTops` (every word's `offsetTop`) + `window._tpReadOffset` into plain arrays, so the renderer still has them after the DOM is gone. **(2)** `startTpRecord` samples `tpBody.scrollTop` every **150ms** into `window._tpScrollTrack = [{y,t}]` (capped 4000, cleared in BOTH stop paths alongside `tpRecTimerInterval`). **(3)** New **`tpBeatTimesFromScroll()`**: cue → word index (`tpCueWordIndex`, ≥60% word match, forward-only, reuses `tpWordNear`) → that word's y → interpolate the moment the scroll passed it. Bails to the next strategy if the script never scrolled (>20px range required). **(4)** New **`tpBeatTimesByPosition()`** as a last resort — places each beat at `dur × (wordIndex / totalWords)`, still script-aware, instead of even spacing. **Priority is now scroll → voice timeline → script position → even**, with `window._tpBeatSrc` recording which one ran. Simulated a take with a deliberate 6s mid-script pause: even spacing fires beat 3 at 15.0s when he only reaches that line at 20.0s; scroll-cued lands it at 20.0s. **LESSON (again): a feature that silently degrades to a dumb fallback reads as broken. The fallback chain must stay meaningful all the way down — and the primary source must be the one that ALWAYS exists (scroll), not the one that usually works (recognition).** Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, all 14 greps green incl. an index assertion that the scroll path is tried before the voice path, timing simulated against a paused read. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v504 = ONE GUTTER across the whole teleprompter (Jörgen: "buttons need to be long or short enough to lign up overall from sides so all is consistent… look all the buttons here and distance from sides and between eachother").** Measured from his screenshot: **three different left edges and two different right edges.** Causes, all separate: `.teleprompter-top` padded 16px, `.teleprompter-controls` **12px** (mobile override), `.teleprompter-body` **24px**, and `.tp-script` was `margin: 0 auto` inside that — centred at ~75px. On the right, the invisible **`.tp-adv-spacer` (44px)** existed only to keep Record optically centred, which stopped the button ~68px short of the right edge while the primer bar ran past it to 24px. Fix = a v504 block (appended after v503, verified by index to sit after the mobile controls override, the base body padding, AND both `.tp-script` rules): **every row padded to G = 16px** (top · controls · advanced · body), **`.tp-adv-spacer { display: none }`** so Record reaches the same right edge as everything else, and **`.tp-script { margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0 }`** so the script left-aligns on the gutter. **The script KEEPS its narrow 17ch measure** — short lines are the point of a prompter — it just anchors to one left edge instead of floating in the middle, which is also better for the eye than centred text. Result at 390px: every left edge 16, every right edge 374, Record spans 70→374 beside the 44px gear. Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, CSS braces balanced, cascade order asserted against all four rules it overrides, all 7 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v503 = the Record button and the primer bar now FILL their row (Jörgen: "tip bar should be wider and record button also so it fills the row").** Both were content-sized islands with dead space either side: `.tp-record-main` was `flex: 0 0 auto` with `padding: 15px 36px` (≈170px in a 390px row), and `.tp-primer` was `max-width: 22ch; margin: 0 auto` (≈210px, centred). v503 block appended after the v498 one (so it beats both the base rules AND the mobile `@media` overrides — the record padding override lives in a media query, so an earlier insertion point would have lost): **`.teleprompter-controls .tp-record-main { flex: 1 1 auto; justify-content: center }`** → the gear keeps its 44px on the left, the spacer its 44px on the right, and Record takes everything between (258px at 390px); **`.teleprompter-body .tp-primer { max-width: none; margin-left/right: 0 }`** → 342px, edge to edge inside the body's 24px padding. Both selectors are 0,2,0 so they win on specificity without `!important`. **`.tp-script` deliberately left at its 17ch cap** — a narrow measure is the point for a teleprompter (eyes shouldn't travel across the phone while reading); only the chrome widened. Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, CSS braces balanced, block position asserted after BOTH the base record rule and the base primer rule, all 5 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v502 = deleted the "Talk like you're on FaceTime with a friend" tip (Jörgen: "that appears for some seconds when opened" — circled over the Record button).** A v500 side effect I should have predicted: `.tp-tip` is `position:absolute; top:96px` (v480 override) — i.e. exactly where the Record pill sits — with `animation: tpTipFade 4s ease forwards`, and it's gated on `.cam-on`. Until v500 `.cam-on` was only added when Record was pressed, so the tip flashed during the 3-2-1 and nobody noticed; now the camera comes up at open, so it fades in ON TOP of the primary button for four seconds every single time. Removed the markup outright rather than repositioning it: it's exactly the generic filler he already rejected in v489 ("one random tip that doesnt really say anything imprtant"), and the collapsible primer now carries the real, specific guidance. CSS rules left in place (orphaned, harmless, one-line restore). **LESSON: when you change WHEN a state class is applied, grep everything gated on that class — `.cam-on` also drives `.tp-tip`, the body scrim and the script text-shadow, and only the tip was positioned assuming the class arrived late.** Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, zero `tp-tip` references outside the stylesheet, all 5 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v501 = A/V SYNC — THE ACTUAL CAUSE, found by reading the whole render function instead of patching the symptom again (Jörgen, 2nd report: "again the voice ahead and lips behind not in sync. how are you doing these mistakes why are the things you do not hardened so we need to come back to them several times").** **THE BUG WAS ORDER OF OPERATIONS, not draw speed.** `rec.start()` was called **BEFORE** `await vid.play()`. So the MediaRecorder opened its timeline on a **blank canvas** with a **paused (silent) audio track**; audio only began flowing when `play()` resolved, hundreds of ms later. The muxer anchors the first audio sample at the start of the file, so the sound sits ahead of the picture by exactly however long `play()` took — a **constant offset from frame one**, which is precisely what "voice before, lips on delay" describes. **v483 misdiagnosed this as a per-frame layout cost** (pre-rendering the beat layers + `requestVideoFrameCallback` were both worthwhile, but they addressed cumulative drift, and this was never cumulative — that mismatch between symptom and hypothesis was the tell I missed). New order, commented in the code so it can't be casually reordered: **`play()` → await ONE real decoded frame (rVFC, 5s-guarded) → paint it → `pushFrame()` → `rec.start()`.** Both tracks are live and matched at t=0. **Also switched to manual frame push:** `cv.captureStream(0)` + `vTrack.requestFrame()` after every paint, so one canvas frame is emitted per decoded source frame and the video track follows the video's own clock instead of a free-running 30fps sampler that duplicates under load; falls back to `captureStream(30)` when `requestFrame` is unavailable. **HARDENING (the answer to "why do we keep coming back to these"): the render now MEASURES ITSELF.** After muxing, a hidden `<video>` probe reads the output blob's duration and compares it to the footage actually consumed (`lastT - _t0`); a mismatch >0.4s means the timeline was distorted, so `tpOfferSplit` says "came out out-of-sync on this phone" and hands back the plain take instead of shipping a silently broken clip. **PRINCIPLE: for anything I cannot test on his device, ship a check that detects the failure automatically — an unverifiable fix is a hypothesis, and hypotheses come back.** Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, all 13 greps green, and the play→first-frame→record ordering is asserted by index comparison inside the function body (not just grepped). NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v500 = the camera now comes up when the teleprompter OPENS, not when you hit Record (Jörgen: "why isnt this half tarnsparent but black in the beginning?").** Not a styling bug — the `.cam-on` scrim rules were all correct, there was simply **no video behind them yet**. `getUserMedia` lived inside `startTpRecord`, so until you pressed Record `tpCameraStream` was null, `.cam-on` was never added, and the overlay showed its flat ink `#16130F` background. Worse, the permission prompt then landed mid-flow and the camera only appeared during the 3-2-1. Extracted the acquisition into **`tpEnsureCamera(quiet)`** and called it (fire-and-forget) from all THREE open paths — `openTeleprompter` statement branch, its script branch, and `tvOpenTeleprompter` — so you see yourself and can frame the shot before filming; `startTpRecord` is now just `if (!(await tpEnsureCamera(false))) return false;`. Three guards, because a camera is easy to leak: **(1)** `window._tpCamPending` holds the in-flight promise so a fast Record tap AWAITS the open-time request instead of firing a second `getUserMedia`; **(2)** if the overlay is no longer `.open` when permission resolves (user closed it while the prompt was up) the stream's tracks are stopped immediately rather than left running behind a dead screen; **(3)** `quiet` suppresses the error toast on open — merely opening the prompter shouldn't nag about permissions, only pressing Record should. Teardown was already correct (`closeTeleprompter` → `stopTpCamera` stops tracks + clears `cam-on`). Side benefit: the `.tp-tip` and the 55%-dark body scrim (both gated on `.cam-on`) now render from the first frame as designed. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, all 10 greps green incl. an assertion that `startTpRecord` no longer holds its own `getUserMedia`. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v499 = framing-preview copy was jargon (Jörgen circled it: "what does this mean?").** The v493 control read `↑  nudge the framing  ↓` — two bare arrows around a phrase that assumes you already know there IS a crop and that it can be moved. Replaced with buttons that state their own action — **"↑ Move up" / "↓ Move down"** — plus a one-line caption above the preview, shown only once the frame actually decodes: **"Here's how it will look. Happy with where you sit in the frame?"** That names what the little picture is (most of the confusion — an unexplained thumbnail appeared where there wasn't one before) and turns the buttons into the obvious answer to its question. Caption is `display:none` by default and revealed in `v.onloadeddata` alongside the preview, hidden again in `v.onerror` and when the render starts, so it can never sit there captioning nothing. **COPY RULE: a control with no label needs the surrounding copy to do the explaining — if a first-time user has to infer what a widget is for, the widget is unfinished.** Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, all 9 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v498 = the teleprompter OPTIONS row (gear) was overflowing off the right edge (Jörgen circled it: A- clipped, A+ gone entirely, play button squashed into an oval).** Measured cause: `.teleprompter-advanced` is a plain `display:flex` with `gap:12px` and **no `flex-wrap`**, so all SIX controls (play · Follow me · "Speed" · slider · A- · A+) were forced onto one line — 363px of fixed content plus a `flex:1` slider inside 358px of usable width at 390px. Flexbox resolved the overflow by shrinking whatever could shrink: `.tp-play-btn` (52×52, no `flex-shrink:0`) got squeezed horizontally into an **oval**, and the font buttons were pushed past the edge. Fix is a v498 CSS block appended at the END of the first stylesheet (so it beats the `@media` mobile overrides at ~L3539 on equal specificity — **that ordering matters, an earlier insertion point would have lost**): `.teleprompter-advanced { flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: center; gap: 10px }`, `> * { flex: 0 0 auto }` so nothing can ever be squashed again, explicit `order:` 1-5 to re-sequence around the DOM order (play · Follow me · A- · A+ · Speed · slider), and **`.tp-speed-slider { order: 5; flex: 1 1 100% }` so the slider always takes a clean row of its own**. Play back to a true 44px circle, font buttons trimmed to 40px min-height. Row 1 now measures 323px of 358px available — fits with room. Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, CSS braces balanced, block position asserted to be after the mobile override, all 7 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v497 = the dead pause at the start of a take (Jörgen: "there is a delay in the beginning when the script starts to move") — three causes, all at t=0.** **(1) THE JUMP TO LINE ONE WAS ITSELF BEING SMOOTH-ANIMATED.** v494 added "position the first line on the reading line before rolling" — but `.teleprompter-body` carries `scroll-behavior: smooth`, and v494's `scrollBehavior='auto'` override lives inside `tpStartTimedScroll`, which runs AFTER that assignment. So every take opened with a ~0.4s glide before the scroll engine even started. `tpRecordTap` now sets `scrollBehavior='auto'` BEFORE the assignment (restored by `stopTpScroll`). **LESSON: `scroll-behavior:smooth` on a container silently animates every `scrollTop =` too, not just `scrollTo()` — set it to auto around ANY programmatic jump you want instant.** **(2) VOICE-FOLLOW MOVES NOTHING UNTIL THE FIRST MATCH LANDS** — ~1s of recognition latency after you start speaking, during which the script is genuinely frozen while you're already talking. Added a **creep bridge**: `tpVoiceBridge`, a 30ms interval at **55% of the computed reading pace**, starts the instant recognition does, so the page is never dead. The first real `tpVoiceScrollTo` clears it and snaps to the true position; `stopTpVoiceFollow` clears it too, so it can never outlive a take. **(3) The very first advance still demanded TWO matching words.** From a standing start there is nothing to jitter backwards to — `tpVoiceMatch` now needs only **1** confident word while `tpVoiceCursor === 0 && !tpVoiceLastAdvanceDone`, then reverts to 2. New flag `tpVoiceLastAdvanceDone` is set in `tpVoiceScrollTo` and reset in `tpBuildVoiceIndex` (i.e. per script render, so a retake starts eager again). Net: ~1.4s of visible nothing → moving from frame one, locked to his voice by ~0.9s. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, all 10 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v496 = fixed the two things v495 BROKE (Jörgen: "huh. whats wrong be smarter. no brakes now between pragaraphs also no dropdown").** **(1) THE CSS MISTAKE: `em` on a `font-size: 0` element computes to ZERO.** v494 hid the "·" glyph with `font-size: 0` and drew the dots via `::before`; v495 then moved the whole paragraph gap onto that element as `margin: 1em 0` **while also stripping `.tp-blk`'s own margin** — and because `em` resolves against the element's OWN font-size, both margins evaluated to 0. Result: no space anywhere between paragraphs. Margins are now **px** (`margin: 30px 0`), and `.tp-blk` gets its own **18px floor** with `.tp-blk:has(.tp-beat){margin-bottom:0}` so a block that has dots keeps the symmetric 30/30 while a block without them still breathes — spacing can never again depend solely on the beat. **WRITE THIS ON YOUR HAND: never size margins in `em` on an element whose font-size you zeroed to hide its text; and don't remove a container's margin in the same edit that moves the gap onto a child.** **(2) THE PRIMER HAD SILENTLY EXPIRED** — `tp_primer_v2` capped it at 3 opens and he'd burned all 3 across v489/v491/v494, so on v495 there was no bar at all and it read as "the dropdown is broken." The counter made sense when the primer was a 4-row card; now that it's ONE COLLAPSED LINE it costs nothing, so the cap is **deleted** — it always renders, closed, openable any time. Also removes a permanent confusion source (a UI element that vanishes on a schedule is indistinguishable from a bug). Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, CSS braces balanced, all 8 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v495 = the two nits from Jörgen's v494 shot — caret invisible, breath dots not centred in the gap.** **(1) CARET** — `.tp-primer > summary::after` inherited the summary's `font-size:11px` + `letter-spacing:1.2px`, so the ▾ rendered as a squashed speck. It now carries its OWN type (`font-size:20px; line-height:1; letter-spacing:0`, lavender at 85%) and the summary became `display:flex; justify-content:space-between` so the caret sits at the right edge of the row instead of trailing the text. **(2) BREATH DOTS SAT HIGH.** `.tp-blk` had `margin: 0 0 1.15em` and the beat lived INSIDE the block with `margin: .55em 0 .15em` — so the gap above the dots was .55em while the gap below was .15em + the block's 1.15em = **1.3em, more than double**. The dots read as belonging to the sentence above rather than sitting between the two thoughts. Fix: the block's bottom margin is removed (`.tp-blk { margin: 0 }`) and the WHOLE gap now lives on the beat (`margin: 1em 0`), so it's symmetric — 34px above, 34px below at his font size. Margin-collapsing carries the beat's bottom margin out through the (now marginless, padding-free) parent to meet the next block, so the spacing is exact. Every mid-block has a beat (`tpFormatScript` adds one to all but the last), so no block loses its gap. Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, CSS braces balanced (2599), all 7 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v494 = Jörgen's 3-item list, done in steps: breath mark visible · primer collapsed · THE PACE BUG FOUND (3rd report, and this time the cause was mechanical, not arithmetic).** **(1) BREATH MARK** — `.tp-beat` was a single `0.5em` dot at **28% opacity**, i.e. a speck you cannot see from arm's length while filming. Glyph hidden (`font-size:0`) and replaced with a `::before` **lavender "•••"** at 15px / `.42em` tracking with real margin above and below. **(2) PRIMER → COLLAPSED `<details>`** — open, 4 rows pushed the first line of script way down the screen ("the text starts from so low"). Now a native `<details class="tp-primer">` **closed by default**, summary "Before you start — what the marks mean ▾" (custom `::after` caret, `list-style:none` + `::-webkit-details-marker{display:none}`). No JS, can't get stuck open, still discoverable. **(3) PACE — FOUR causes, and the two big ones were mechanical:** **(a) THE KILLER — `tpVoiceRec.lang = navigator.language`.** His phone is not on an English locale, so an **English script was being transcribed by a non-English recogniser** → zero word matches → voice-following silently did nothing on every take. That is why "it doesn't take into account my reading speed" survived v488 and v492: the feature was never actually running for him. Now `/^en\b/.test(navigator.language) ? navigator.language : 'en-US'` — keeps a real English accent when the device has one, otherwise listens in English because that's what the app writes. **(b) `scroll-behavior: smooth` on `.teleprompter-body` was fighting the timed scroll.** Every `scrollTop += step` (30ms) started a smooth animation that the next tick interrupted, so the element chased a moving target and NEVER ran at the computed rate — the v488 maths was correct and the browser was overriding it. Timed scroll now sets `scrollBehavior='auto'` for its duration (restored in `stopTpScroll`); voice-follow is untouched because it requests smooth explicitly via `scrollTo({behavior:'smooth'})`. **(c) The travel distance included the primer card** — `dist` was `el.offsetTop + el.offsetHeight - ch*0.62`, so the scroll had to cover the chrome above the script within the time it takes to SAY the script. `end - start` reduces to **`el.offsetHeight - clientHeight*0.24`**, which is primer-independent and scale-invariant (so a mid-take fallback from voice→timed still gets the right rate). **(d) The take started at `scrollTop = 0`**, above the primer, so the first seconds scrolled empty chrome; `tpRecordTap` now positions the FIRST LINE on the reading line (`sc.offsetTop - clientHeight*0.38`) before starting. **LESSON: when the same complaint survives two arithmetic fixes, stop refining the arithmetic and check whether the platform is honouring it at all — `scroll-behavior:smooth` silently voided the rate, and a locale default silently voided the whole feature.** Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, CSS braces balanced (2598/2598), all 15 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v493 = SPLIT-SCREEN CROP FIXED — I had misread the complaint and gone the wrong way (Jörgen on v492: "layout got worse… you are trying to do something else here and this is not the right direction… you need to centre the video and other dimansions and or crop it. to fit the split screen part").** **MY MISREAD: his first report "the video is half way visible" meant HIS FOOTAGE IS HALF CUT OFF, not "the footage occupies half the frame."** I read it as a ratio complaint and shipped v490's 62/38 split + vertically-centred caption — both wrong, and the actual defect (the crop) went untouched for two rounds. **LESSON: when a report is one ambiguous clause, resolve the ambiguity BEFORE building — a `show_widget` with 2-3 rendered options + AskUserQuestion costs one round; a wrong build costs two. This is the second time that lesson has paid (see the v326 animation note).** Settled it this time by rendering three crop strategies as an SVG mockup and asking; he picked **crop-anchored-on-the-face** + **text back at the top**. **THE ACTUAL BUG: `spComposite` cover-cropped at dead centre** — `ctx.drawImage(vid, (W-w)/2, (half-h)/2, w, h)`. Filling a 9:16 phone take into a 720×640 half throws away HALF the source height, so "centre" is a coin flip — and a handheld teleprompter take systematically puts the face BELOW centre (you're looking down at the phone), which is exactly what chopped his chin. Measured from his screenshot: his face spans ~48-70% of the source height, and the centred window showed 25-75%, cutting at 67%. Fix: new **`spAnchor()`** (0 = source top, 1 = source bottom, **default 0.62** → shows 31-81%, i.e. the whole face with room) and the draw becomes `(half-h) * spAnchor()`. **PLUS the part that ends the guessing for good: a framing PREVIEW on the offer sheet** — `spSetupPreview(blob)` decodes one real frame (seeks to `min(0.6s, dur/3)`), `spDrawPreview()` composites it into a 150×267 canvas exactly the way the renderer will (same cover-crop maths, same anchor, cream panel below with placeholder bars), and **↑/↓ buttons (`spNudgeFrame(±0.08)`) re-draw it live** so he sets the framing in two taps BEFORE spending the render. `spKillPreview()` revokes the object URL on skip/cancel/render-start so the decoder is never left holding a blob. Reverted with it: **`half` back to `H/2` (true 50/50 — the ratio was never the problem)** and `spRenderBeat` back to a fixed `y = 56` top anchor (`bodyH` is still measured because the chips branch needs its row count). Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, all 16 greps green, crop windows computed per anchor against his measured face position. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v492 = TWO real bugs behind "only one bold word" + "speed still wasn't my speaking speed" — both found by reading, both measured.** **(1) SPEED — statements never set the reading estimate, so the v488 pace fix was starved on exactly the post he was filming.** `openTeleprompter`'s `statement` branch **RETURNS before `tpSetSmartSpeed(...)`** (that call sits below, in the script branch only — `tvOpenTeleprompter` does it for both, which is why this only bit one entry point). So `window._tpEstSecs` stayed 0/stale, and v488's `tpTimedBase()` fell through to `Math.max(4, 0)` → **the whole script scrolled in FOUR SECONDS** (measured: 14.2px/tick vs the correct 4.75 — a 3× race on a 28-word statement). So v488's maths was right and its input was missing. Fix: `tpSetSmartSpeed(_stTxt)` in the statement branch, AND — the belt-and-braces that matters more — **`tpTimedBase()` no longer trusts any caller**: if `_tpEstSecs` is absent it counts the words ACTUALLY on screen (`el.textContent`) and derives the estimate itself, with the floor raised 4s→5s. No future entry point can starve it again. **LESSON: an early `return` in one format branch silently skipped a setter the whole scroll engine depends on — when a fix "doesn't work", check whether its INPUT is being set on the path actually taken.** **(2) EMPHASIS — `TP_STRESS_RX` had no `/g`.** `String.replace` with a non-global regex replaces only the FIRST match, so at most ONE word per sense-line could ever bold; combined with a word list that omitted every contraction (`cannot`, `don't`, `won't`…), his script got 2 marks total across 6 lines and whole sentences got none. Replaced with **two GLOBAL priority classes** built by `tpStressRx(src)` — **A = negation** (never/nothing/nobody/none/zero/cannot/can't/won't/doesn't/don't/isn't/aren't/wasn't/didn't/not/no, apostrophe OR `\u2019`) and **B = absolutes & pivots** (only/every/always/all/most/worst/best/first/last/instead/without/unless/until/actually/before/after/even/still/must) — applied A-first so negation always wins the slot. Density is capped by a per-line **budget** (2 marks if the line has ≥7 words, else 1) because marking everything means marking nothing; numbers are drawn from the same budget. Measured on his real script: **2 → 4 marks**, and "they don't" / "a judge cannot" now carry weight where they previously had none. NOTE: `emphasis` from the generator (v485) still takes priority when present — this heuristic only runs for ideas generated before that, which is most of his library. Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, all 9 greps green, both behaviours simulated against his actual lines. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v491 = two primer rendering nits caught in Jörgen's v489 screenshot (he sent it with no complaint — the content was right, but the render wasn't).** **(1) The first row's hairline swatch was INVISIBLE.** `tpPrimer` built each key as e.g. `<span class="tp-primer-k line">` and then the row map wrapped it in ANOTHER `<span class="tp-primer-k">` — so the inner span was a nested inline element whose only content was `&nbsp;`, i.e. about 4px wide, and its `::after { left:3px; right:3px }` hairline collapsed to zero width. The dot and ↻ rows survived only because they're text glyphs that don't depend on the box having width. Fix: the map no longer re-wraps (`'<div class="tp-primer-row">' + r[0] + ...`), each key carries `.tp-primer-k` itself (the underline swatch now takes `tp-primer-k tp-primer-u` so it keeps the 26px column alignment), and `.tp-primer-k.line` gets `align-self:center; height:1.2em` so the hairline has a box to sit on. **LESSON: a `::after` positioned with left/right needs its parent to actually HAVE width — an inline span containing only a space does not.** **(2) The fixed reading guide sliced straight through the primer card** — `.tp-read-line` is `position:fixed; z-index:1` and the card was translucent (`rgba(249,246,234,.05)`), so the line drew across the explainer. Card is now opaque `#221E19` with `position:relative; z-index:2`, so the guide passes behind it. Verified: 5/5 scripts parse, all 8 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v490 = SPLIT-SCREEN LAYOUT FIXED — 62/38 instead of 50/50, and the beat is CENTRED in its panel (Jörgen's first successful render, 4.1MB: "as you can see the video is half way visible" — his face got exactly half the frame while the bottom half was a mostly-empty white slab with two lines of text clinging to the top).** Both causes measured, not guessed. **(1) `half = H/2`** — a hard even split. But a talking head IS the video; the graphic is a caption under it. Now **`half = Math.round(H * 0.62)`** with a separate **`panel = H - half`** → footage 640→**794px (62%)**, graphics panel 486px. **(2) `spRenderBeat` drew from a fixed `let y = 70`** at the top of the panel, so his eyebrow + 2-line headline used ~170px of a 640px box and left **400px of dead white** — that void is what made a working render look broken. Rewrote it as **measure-then-draw**: it now computes the real body height per kind first (number = 128 + optional sub; chips = pre-wrapped into `rows` so the row count is known BEFORE drawing; statement = `spWrap` line count × 62 + optional sub), then starts at `y = max(30, (panelH - (EYE + bodyH)) / 2)` so the content sits **vertically centred**. Empty space below the text drops 400px → 159px, and it self-balances: 1-line beats start at y=190, 4-line at y=97, all still fitting inside 486px (verified across 1-4 lines). The chips branch was restructured on the way — wrapping used to happen inline while drawing, which is exactly why its height couldn't be measured. Also fixed a latent bug the even split had been hiding: the no-layer fallback in `spComposite` did `fillRect(0, half, W, half)`, which with an uneven split would have left an unpainted strip at the bottom → now `H - half`. Fonts nudged (`120→116px` number) to sit in the shorter panel. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, all 12 greps green, layout maths checked against his exact beat. NEEDS `vercel --prod`. **NOTE: the black bars either side in his screenshot are just the result-card `<video>` letterboxing a 9:16 clip — not part of the render.**
- **cs-v489 = the teleprompter primer now explains WHAT'S ON THE SCREEN, not a generic tip (Jörgen's screenshot: a statement post showing "BEFORE YOU START · Look at the lens and say it flat" while the text below it carried an underlined stress word, a breath dot and the reading line — "one random tip that doesnt really say anything imprtant what it had to").** MY BUG: `tpPrimer(kind)` branched on the POST FORMAT, and the `statement` branch returned a single generic filming bullet. But BOTH branches run `tpFormatScript`, so a statement gets the exact same sense-lines / `.tp-beat` dots / `.tp-em` underlines as a script — meaning the one screen where the conventions were visible was the one screen that explained none of them. Fix: **`tpPrimer(html)` now takes the ALREADY-FORMATTED markup and lists only the conventions actually present** — `h.indexOf('tp-em')` → "Underlined word: lean on it.", `h.indexOf('tp-beat')` → "A dot: take a breath, then carry on." — with the reading-line row always first ("Read at the line. The script follows your voice — pause and it waits.") since `.tp-read-line` renders in every branch. All 4 call sites (openTeleprompter statement+script, tvOpenTeleprompter statement+script) now build the formatted HTML into a local (`_stFmt`/`_scFmt`/`_tvFmt`) FIRST and pass it to the primer instead of a `kind` string — a small but important ordering change: **the primer must be built from the render, not from the data.** Content rule applied: every row is now something you could NOT work out by looking (the two mark conventions, that it follows your voice, and — replacing the "look at the lens" filler — "Fluff a line? Stop, then Retake — nothing is kept until you say so.", which is genuinely non-obvious and takes the pressure off take one). Counter key bumped `tp_primer_seen`→**`tp_primer_v2`** so everyone (Jörgen included, who already burned 2 of 3 views on the useless version) gets 3 fresh showings of the good one. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, all 12 greps green, and the row-selection logic was simulated across statement-with-marks / plain-one-liner / full-script — the plain one-liner correctly drops both mark rows instead of explaining marks that aren't there. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v488 = THE PROMPTER NOW ACTUALLY MATCHES YOUR READING PACE (Jörgen: "i felt like the speed of the text moving wasnt according to my speed of reading").** Read the code instead of guessing and found FOUR separate causes, in order of blame. **(1) THE BIG ONE — the timed scroll's speed was a number with no relationship to anything.** `tpStartTimedScroll` did `scrollTop += speed` where speed was the raw slider value (1.5 / 2 / 2.5 px per 30ms tick, picked by word count in `tpSetSmartSpeed`). That ignores font size (which the A+/A- buttons change!), screen height, line-wrapping and the actual pixel length of the script — so the same 2px/tick is wildly wrong on a long script and wildly wrong again if you bump the font. Measured: a 90-word script (37s to say at 145 wpm) finished scrolling in **14 seconds — 2.6× too fast**. New **`tpTimedBase()`** derives px/tick from REAL geometry: `distance ÷ (estSecs × ticks/sec)`, where distance = how far the script must travel for its last line to reach the 38% reading line, and estSecs is the existing 145-wpm estimate. It now finishes exactly when the read finishes, at any font size, on any phone. **The slider became a MULTIPLIER** (`value/2`, so 2 = natural pace, 5 = 2.5×) and `tpSetSmartSpeed` just centres it at 2 — "faster/slower" is now a meaningful adjustment around a correct baseline rather than a blind guess. **(2) The voice matcher was too brittle to survive real speech.** `tpVoiceMatch` required the last 4 heard words to line up ONE-FOR-ONE from a fixed start (`tpVoiceWords[i+j] === tail[j]`) — but ASR constantly drops articles, mis-hears endings and inserts "uh", and a single insertion/deletion shifts every later offset so the score collapsed to 0-1 and the script SAT STILL while he talked. Rewrote it to walk the tail through the script **allowing gaps** (each heard word may skip up to 2 script words to find its place), tail widened 4→6, window 60→45, plus **`tpWordNear()`** so plural/tense/near-miss words still count (same first 4 chars, length within 3). Tie-break now favours the FURTHEST-FORWARD match so it keeps up when you speed up. **Benchmarked against 400 simulated ASR tails with realistic noise (15% dropped, 15% mis-heard endings, 10% filler inserted): advance rate 92%→99%, landed-on-the-right-word 91%→97%.** **(3) No safety net when recognition runs but never lands.** Only `onerror` fell back — so a session that was working fine but matching poorly (accent, noise, a heavily-edited script), or one receiving NO audio at all (mic held by the MediaRecorder, permission quietly refused), left the script frozen with no way out. Added a 1s **watchdog**: clearly-speaking-but-no-advance-for-5s → hand over to timed scroll; **zero results at all 8s after starting** → same (that's a dead session, not a pause — a genuine silent pause never triggers it because `tpVoiceHeardAt` stays 0 only when nothing is heard AND the 8s branch is the one that catches it). `tpVoiceFallback(auto)` toasts "Couldn't hear you clearly — scrolling at a set pace" so the handover is visible, never silent. Watchdog cleared in `stopTpVoiceFollow`. **(4) Nudging the speed slider tore down voice-following.** The `input` listener did `stopTpScroll(); startTpScroll()` — killing the recognition session mid-take. Now it only restarts the timed interval when one is actually running. **PLUS the diagnostic half: a `#tpMode` chip under the timer says "following your voice" (lavender) or "auto-scroll" (dim) while recording** — so "the speed felt wrong" is never again an unanswerable report; he can see which engine is driving. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, all 21 wiring greps green, matcher benchmarked, pace maths checked against a worked example. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v487 = THE SPLIT-SCREEN RENDER CAN NO LONGER HANG (Jörgen: "i tested and it got stuck here: and stayd stuck there. had to close the app." — screenshot showed "Building your split screen…" with the bar frozen at 0%, Make-it-a-split-screen greyed, no way out except force-quitting).** ROOT CAUSE CLASS: `renderSplitScreen` was a chain of **unguarded awaits**. Three of them could never resolve on a bad clip: (1) `await new Promise(r => vid.onloadedmetadata = r)` — a MediaRecorder blob the decoder won't parse fires NEITHER `loadedmetadata` NOR `error` on some Android builds → dead at 0% forever, which is EXACTLY the frozen-bar symptom; (2) `await vid.play()` — can reject (autoplay policy after the tab loses focus) or simply never settle; (3) the frame loop only exited on `t >= dur`, so if `vid.currentTime` never advanced it spun until the tab was killed. **THE PATTERN NOW BAKED IN: every await in a long render is time-boxed, and the loop is watched, not trusted.** New **`_limit(p, ms, what)`** Promise.race helper wraps each await with a named timeout that surfaces in the error message. Metadata: skipped entirely when `vid.readyState >= 1` (already parsed), else 12s + an explicit `vid.onerror` reject. Play: 8s, and a **rejection retries once with `vid.muted = true`** (audio still records — it comes from `vid.captureStream()`'s track, not playback, so muting costs nothing and beats autoplay refusal). Loop: a **700ms `watch` interval** compares `vid.currentTime` against `lastT` — advancing resets `stalledSince`; **6 seconds of no movement ends it**, and crucially it **keeps a partial render if `lastT > 0.5`** (better to hand back 8 of 12 seconds than nothing) and only fails outright if playback never started. Plus a **`hardStop` ceiling** at `max(45s, dur*4000+30000)` so even a pathological slow-motion render terminates. All exits route through **`finish()`** which clears BOTH timers — no orphaned intervals firing after resolve. **THE UX HALF (equally important — a fix he can't see is not a fix): a "Stop and just save my video" link now sits under the progress bar from the moment the render starts.** It sets `window._spCancel` (read by the watchdog), tears down the sheet and calls `tpShareOrSave` — so his take is ALWAYS one tap away, even if some future failure mode slips past all three guards. `window._spCancel = false` is reset at render start (a stale true would abort instantly), and the catch block returns early when it's set so cancelling never also shows a failure message. Failure copy is now honest and specific — "Split screen failed (reading the clip) — saving your plain video." instead of a generic shrug — because the timeout label tells you which stage died, which is the difference between a diagnosable report and another guessing round. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, all 17 wiring greps green, and the watchdog logic was SIMULATED against a clip whose `currentTime` never moves → **fails at ~7s and returns the plain video, instead of hanging forever**; a healthy clip keeps it silent. NEEDS `vercel --prod` — and note his stuck test ran on an older build, so **v486's teleprompter primer + bold-underline ship in this same deploy.**
- **cs-v486 = teleprompter primer moved to the TOP + stronger emphasis (Jörgen: "the words in bold maybe underlined or a bit more bold… the tip in the end of the script needs to be probably in the beginning… a tip that what bold means and all the other things a first time user should know in brief, breathing breaks etc").** (1) **`.tp-em` 800→900 weight + a lavender underline** (`text-decoration-color: rgba(231,218,249,.6)`, `.055em` thickness, `.18em` offset) so the stress word reads at a glance from arm's length instead of blending into the cream. (2) **New `tpPrimer(kind)` renders a "BEFORE YOU START" card ABOVE the script** (a tip printed AFTER the script is a tip nobody reads — the statement branch's `.tp-screen-section` "How to film it" was doing exactly that and is now DELETED from both entry points). Script version explains the three conventions in one line each: underlined = lean on this word · dot = a breath, stop then carry on · the line = speak here, the script follows your voice — each with a live mini-swatch (real underline, real dot, a rendered hairline) so the legend LOOKS like the thing it describes. Statement version keeps the old "look at the lens, say it flat" advice, now placed before rather than after. (3) **Shows for the first 3 opens only** (`tp_primer_seen` counter in localStorage, try/catch-guarded) — after that it stops appearing entirely; it also scrolls away the instant filming starts, so it never costs a veteran anything. Wired at all 4 render sites. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, style blocks balanced, all 11 greps green, counter behaviour simulated (shows 1-2-3, silent from 4). NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v485 = SCRIPT SET FOR SPEAKING, not reading (Jörgen: "how to make a person read more naturally… otherwise its just one block" — he picked all four: sense lines, breath space, reading line, AND emphasis driven from the script).** Broadcast prompters never break on line width, they break on BREATH. Four pieces: (1) **`tpFormatScript(text, emphasis)`** — splits the script into one `.tp-blk` per SENTENCE, then `tpSenseLines()` breaks long sentences into ~7-word speakable lines, cutting BEFORE connectors (and/but/so/because/which/when…) and AFTER commas, with an orphan guard that re-joins a trailing 1-2 word fragment; (2) **`.tp-beat` "·" between blocks** = the visible breath mark; (3) **`.tp-read-line`** — a fixed hairline + dot at 38% viewport height so the eye anchors to ONE spot (the same 38% the voice-follow scrolls to, so your line is always sitting on the guide); (4) **EMPHASIS FROM THE GENERATOR** — `api/generate-ideas.js` schema gained an **`emphasis: []`** array (2-5 short phrases copied VERBATIM from the script — the hard number, the flip word, the payoff; explicit "never mark a whole sentence" + "empty for non-spoken formats" guidance). **Deliberate design choice: emphasis is a SEPARATE FIELD, not `**markers**` inside the script string** — markers would leak into copy/paste, the pipeline detail view, remix payloads and the beats API, and I'd have had to sanitise every one of those surfaces. `tpEmphasise()` bolds the generator's phrases when present, else falls back to a heuristic (numbers with units, and the flip words never/not/only/instead/…) so EVERY existing script benefits immediately. Also: measure narrowed to `15ch` (17ch on small phones) so eyes don't travel. **CRITICAL COMPANION FIX: `tpBuildVoiceIndex` was parsing `innerHTML` with a regex** — with the new markup (blocks, lines, `<b>`) it would have wrapped TAGS as words and broken both voice-following and the formatting. Rewritten to walk TEXT NODES via `createTreeWalker` and wrap words through the DOM, so it's safe with any structure (and skips the `.tp-beat` dots). Wired at ALL FOUR render sites (Pipeline + Quick Post "Film it", each with a statement and a script branch), every one keeping `|| nl2br(raw)` as fallback. Smoke-tested: a 3-sentence script broke into 3 blocks / 5 sense lines at the right joints. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js + generate-ideas.js parse, style blocks balanced, all 13 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod` — NOTE the emphasis field only appears on NEWLY generated ideas; older scripts use the heuristic.
- **cs-v484 = GRAPHICS CUED TO THE SPOKEN WORD, not to an even split (Jörgen: "check the words spoken and the motiongraphics and stock photos would be in sync not delayed and also on point").** Before this, `per = dur / beats.length` spread beats evenly across the take — so if he lingered 20s on the hook, every graphic after it was wrong. **The fix reuses the v482 voice-following recognition, which already knows which word he's on:** (1) `tpVoiceScrollTo` now also logs `{w: wordIndex, t: secondsSinceRecordStart}` into `window._tpVoiceTimeline` (only while actually recording; reset at the top of `startTpRecord` so a retake never inherits the previous take's timings); (2) **`api/video-beats.js` gained a `cue` field** — the first 4-8 words of the script sentence where that beat belongs, copied VERBATIM (prompt demands script order + non-overlapping cues); (3) new **`tpBeatTimes(beats, dur)`** matches each cue forward-only through `tpVoiceWords` (needs ≥60% of the cue's words, min 2), converts the matched word index to a timestamp by interpolating between timeline entries, fills unmatched beats by spreading between the anchors that DID match, then forces strictly-increasing times clamped inside the clip; (4) `renderSplitScreen` builds `cueTimes` and picks the layer via `beatAt(t)` — **falling back to the old even split whenever there's no usable timeline (iOS, follow-me off, silent take)**. Smoke-tested with a simulated take containing a deliberate mid-clip pause: cues resolved to 0 / 2.0 / 8.6 / 16.5s where even spacing would have fired at 0 / 5 / 10 / 15 — i.e. the graphic now lands on the sentence being said. **Stock photos will inherit this timing for free, since a photo is just part of a beat.** Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js + video-beats.js parse, all 10 greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod` + a filmed test with a deliberate long pause mid-script.
- **cs-v483 = A/V SYNC FIX in the split-screen render (Jörgen: "my voice and lips movement dont match as voice is before and my lips on delay").** DIAGNOSIS: audio is passed straight through from the source clip's track, but the VIDEO half was being rebuilt from scratch every frame — `spDrawFrame` re-ran the whole text layout (measureText, `spWrap`, roundRects, letterSpacing) 30-60×/second. When the draw loop can't hold real time the canvas shows an older video frame while audio keeps playing → picture drifts behind the voice, exactly the reported symptom (and the drift GROWS with clip length). **Two fixes:** (1) **pre-render each beat ONCE** — `spDrawFrame` split into **`spRenderBeat(beat, W, halfH)`** (draws that beat's graphics into its own offscreen canvas; called `beats.length` times total, in `const layers = beats.map(...)` before recording starts) and **`spComposite(ctx, vid, layer, …)`** (the per-frame work is now just: footage blit + `drawImage(layer)` + progress rect — two blits and a rect); (2) **drive the loop off `requestVideoFrameCallback`** when available so the canvas paints on ACTUAL decoded frames and tracks the video's own clock, with `requestAnimationFrame` as fallback. **LESSON: for canvas-recorded video, per-frame text layout is the sync killer — anything static must be pre-rendered to an offscreen canvas, and the loop should follow `requestVideoFrameCallback`, not rAF.** Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, all 11 greps green, zero stale `spDrawFrame` references. NEEDS `vercel --prod` + a re-film to confirm lips track the voice (test with a LONGER take — drift was cumulative, so a 30s+ clip is the real check).
- **cs-v482 = VOICE-FOLLOWING TELEPROMPTER — the script moves at YOUR pace (Jörgen: "did you add the thing that understands how quickly im speaking?" — no, v479 only pre-guessed a speed from word count and then scrolled blind).** Web Speech API (`SpeechRecognition`/`webkitSpeechRecognition`) transcribes while filming; the script scrolls to wherever the speaker actually is. **How it works:** `tpBuildVoiceIndex()` wraps every word of `.tp-script` in a `<span class="tp-w">` (splitting on `<br>` first so line breaks survive) and records the DOM node + a normalized key; `tpVoiceMatch(heard)` takes the last 4 spoken words and scans **FORWARD ONLY** from the current cursor over a 60-word window (so a word repeated earlier in the script can never drag the scroll backwards), requiring **≥2 matching words** before it moves — that threshold is what stops jitter on filler words; `tpVoiceScrollTo(idx)` smooth-scrolls that word to 38% viewport height (the natural reading line) and marks everything before it `.said` (fades to 32% opacity, so you can see at a glance what you've covered). **Robustness:** `continuous + interimResults` so it tracks mid-sentence, `onend` auto-restarts (Android drops the session on pauses), `no-speech`/`aborted` errors ignored as normal pauses, any OTHER error → `tpVoiceFallback()` silently hands back to timed scrolling **without interrupting the recording**. `startTpScroll` now tries voice first and calls the extracted `tpStartTimedScroll()` as fallback; `stopTpScroll` always kills the mic. **Toggle:** "◦ Follow me" pill in the options row (lavender when on, pulsing dot), preference saved in `tp_voice_follow`, and **hidden entirely when `TP_VOICE_SUPPORTED` is false (iOS Safari) so nobody flips a dead switch** — those users keep the v479 smart timed scroll. NOTE: recognition runs alongside the MediaRecorder capture; both use the mic, which is fine on Android Chrome but is one more reason iOS stays on the timed path. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, style blocks balanced, all 14 wiring greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod` + a real filmed test (talk slowly, then fast, then pause — the script should track and wait). **REMAINING from his list: stock photos in the graphics half.**
- **cs-v481 = SPLIT-SCREEN RESULT SCREEN — fixes "it finished and then it disappeared, couldn't share it" (Jörgen's first real end-to-end test: filmed → chose split → render completed → video vanished).** **ROOT CAUSE (my bug, and the spike should have taught me): `navigator.share()` REQUIRES transient user activation.** v478 called `tpShareOrSave` automatically the instant `renderSplitScreen` resolved — but that's 15-40s after the tap, by which time Chrome has expired the activation, so `share()` threw, the `.catch` silently fell through to `tpDownloadBlob`, and the file landed in Downloads behind a 3s toast he never saw. **`render-test.html` worked precisely because Share was its own button** — I ported the pipeline but not that property. **Fix: new `tpSplitResult(bd, outBlob, ext, rawBlob, rawName)`** replaces the sheet's contents when the render finishes: "Your split screen ✓ · N MB · ready to post", the composited video in a `<video controls>` (max-height 46vh), then **[Share it →]** (lavender primary — `navigator.share` now runs on a FRESH tap, so it works), **[Save to my phone]** (explicit `tpDownloadBlob`), and **[Use the plain video instead]** (falls back to the raw take). Object URL revoked on close. Also made the download fallback honest: `tpDownloadBlob`'s toast "Video saved! Check your downloads" → **"Saved to your phone — check Downloads" at 6000ms** (and fixed the call — `showToast(msg, duration, onTap)`, so passing `'success'` as arg 2 was being coerced to the default 3000; a 3rd numeric arg would have landed in `onTap`). **PERMANENT RULE: never call `navigator.share()` after an await that can take seconds — always hand the user a button.** Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, all 10 wiring greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`.
- **cs-v480 = TELEPROMPTER RESTYLED minimal + on-brand (Jörgen: "can we make telepromter better looking minimal sleek on brand").** It was the last generic-dark-app screen: pure `#000`, `#1a1a1a`/`#333` boxy close button, hard `#222` rules across the camera, a **teal `#4ecdc4`** tip (a colour that exists nowhere else in the brand), red pill record. **All CSS-only, appended as one clearly-marked v480 block** (reversible; sits after the base rules so same-specificity wins, `!important` only where a `.cam-on` variant would otherwise beat it). The 1 remaining `#4ecdc4` in the file is elsewhere, not the teleprompter. Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, 4 style blocks brace-balanced, all 10 markers/greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`. **STILL QUEUED from his "all of them are good": v481 voice-following scroll, v482 stock photos.**
- **cs-v479 = TELEPROMPTER: "Keep it / Retake" review + pacing readout (first of the 4 upgrades he greenlit: "all of them are good").** THE GAP: `tpMediaRecorder.onstop` went STRAIGHT to share (and since v478, to the split-screen render) — so a fluffed line meant a wasted share AND a wasted render/credit. Nobody nails take one. **New `tpReview(blob,fname)`** inserts itself first in the onstop chain: a `.tp-review` layer INSIDE the teleprompter overlay (so the camera UI stays behind it) with the take playing back (`autoplay controls`), **[Keep it →]** (lavender primary → hands off to `tpOfferSplit` → `tpShareOrSave`, exactly the v478 chain) and **[Retake]** (revokes the object URL, clears `tpRecordedChunks`, scrolls the script back to top, `setTimeout(tpRecordTap,250)` → 3-2-1 and rolls again; the bad take is never saved or shared). Guards: returns false when the blob is empty or the overlay was closed mid-record, so the old direct-save path still runs in those cases. **Pacing readout:** `tpSetSmartSpeed` already counts the script's words, so it now also stores `window._tpEstSecs = words/145*60` (145 wpm conversational); `updateRecTimer` renders `0:12 · 0:35 left` (dimmed `.tp-left` span, "over" once past estimate). Verified: 5/5 scripts + sw.js parse, style blocks balanced, all 9 wiring greps green. NEEDS `vercel --prod`. **NEXT in the agreed set: v480 voice-following scroll (Web Speech, Android-first, degrades to timed), v481 stock photos in the graphics half (imageQuery per beat → Pexels via a SAME-ORIGIN proxy so the canvas is never tainted → duotone brand treatment).**
- **cs-v478 = SPLIT-SCREEN WIRED INTO THE REAL FLOW — film with the teleprompter → "Make it a split screen" → composited mp4 → share. All on-device (Jörgen: "wire it").** The teleprompter's `tpMediaRecorder.onstop` (the v446 one-tap path, ~L8100) used to share/download the raw take immediately; now it first calls **`tpOfferSplit(blob, fname)`** — a sheet reading "Filmed ✓ / Want the split-screen version… it builds right here on your phone — nothing uploads" with **[Make it a split screen]** + **[Just the plain video]**. The raw-share logic was extracted to **`tpShareOrSave(blob,fname)`** so both lanes share one path; every failure route falls back to it, so a compositing error can NEVER cost the user their take. **`renderSplitScreen(videoBlob, beats, onProgress)`** is the production port of the proven spike: 720×1280 canvas, top half = footage cover-cropped, bottom half = `spDrawFrame` (statement / number / chips, lavender highlight box, progress bar), `captureStream(30)` + the video's own audio track → `MediaRecorder` mp4-when-supported @8Mbps → Blob + ext. **Beats timing now stretches across the ACTUAL take** (`per = max(1.6, duration/beats.length)`) instead of a fixed 3.25s, so graphics never run out mid-video. New `spWrap()` word-wraps headlines to the canvas (max 4 lines) — the preview had CSS to wrap for it, canvas does not. **Credits: `beatsForIdea(id)` caches per idea in `window._beatsCache`, and `openBroll` now writes its result into the same cache — so tapping B-roll and then filming spends ONE credit, not two.** If no beats are cached the render fetches them on demand ("Reading your script for the graphics…") — deliberate: the user explicitly asked for the split screen, so spending the credit then is honest, whereas prefetching on every teleprompter open would burn credits silently. `openTeleprompter` stashes `window._tpSplitIdeaId`. Verified: 5/5 inline scripts + sw.js parse, all 12 wiring greps green. **NEEDS `vercel --prod` + his real test: Pipeline → video post → Teleprompter → Record → Stop → "Make it a split screen".** **STILL UNVERIFIED: iPhone/Safari.**

- **cs-v443 = REMIX "Upload Video/Audio" FIXED — it was dead for every real video since it was built (Jörgen 2026-08-02 screenshot; NEEDS `vercel --prod` + ONE-TIME SUPABASE SQL below).** ROOT CAUSE: `handleTranscribeUpload` base64-encodes the file (+33%) into a JSON body → **Vercel hard-caps serverless request bodies at ~4.5MB**, so any file >~3MB (= virtually every video) got a platform 413 before our code ran; the `module.exports.config bodyParser '25mb'` line in transcribe.js is Next.js-style and NEVER applied (left in place with a warning comment — do not raise it expecting bigger bodies). The button/input/handler wiring was all correct. FIX = **Supabase Storage relay**: frontend (`handleTranscribeUpload`) now splits — files ≤3MB keep the inline base64 path (no bucket dependency); files >3MB upload via `sb.storage.from('transcribe-tmp').upload(uid+'/'+ts_rand.ext, file)` (status shows "Uploading (N MB)…" then "Transcribing…") and POST `{storagePath}` instead of `{audio}`. Backend (`api/transcribe.js`): accepts `storagePath` — validates charset + no `..` + **must start with `<userId>/`** (nobody can transcribe/delete another user's upload), downloads via SERVICE_ROLE from `/storage/v1/object/transcribe-tmp/...` (25MB cap, 30s timeout), then **best-effort DELETEs the object immediately** (single-use tmp; buffer already in memory) → same Groq whisper-large-v3 flow. Bucket-missing upload error → friendly "Upload storage isn't set up yet" message. **JÖRGEN ONE-TIME SETUP (Supabase SQL editor) — without this, >3MB uploads show the not-set-up message:** `insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public) values ('transcribe-tmp','transcribe-tmp', false) on conflict (id) do nothing;` then `create policy "transcribe tmp own-folder uploads" on storage.objects for insert to authenticated with check (bucket_id = 'transcribe-tmp' and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text);` (private bucket, upload-only for users into their OWN folder, service role does read+delete — no select policy needed). Verified: transcribe.js + 5/5 inline scripts parse, v443 markers both files. TEST after deploy+SQL: Remix → File → upload a >3MB mp4 → transcript lands in the description box.

Tap to see it →", else "Added to your Pipeline — tap to see it →") whose tap → `switchView('pipeline')`; if `_apJumpId` is null it falls back to the old "Got it — more like this" ack (so nothing else changes). - Code is at **cs-v309** (SW rewrite; NOT deployed yet). **v309 supersedes v308's approach.** Root problem: **app.html is 824 KB and the precache set is 1.8 MB; Jörgen's connection is ~0.5 KB/s → a cold download is 30–60 min = the "app hangs on splash / won't install" he keeps hitting.** After the v308 stale-while-revalidate ship he reported the app STILL "didn't install itself in the end" (he confirmed: the phone app hung, NOT the Terminal deploy). Two things were still wrong in v308: (a) it **bumped the cache name every deploy and deleted the old cache on `activate`** → forced a full COLD re-download every single deploy; (b) SWR **re-downloads the whole app in the background on EVERY launch** → saturates his 0.5 KB/s pipe so the generate/API calls he actually wants stall. **v309 fix (sw.js fully rewritten):** **STABLE cache name `cs-shell` that survives every deploy** (never renamed) + **cache-FIRST fetch handler** (serve cached INSTANTLY, no per-launch background re-download) + updates ship by bumping the new **`const BUILD='vNNN'`** marker (byte-changes sw.js → browser detects new worker → `install` pulls fresh app.html into the SAME stable cache in the background while the OLD copy keeps serving instantly → new content one launch later, pipe stays free between deploys). `activate` prunes old caches **only once `cs-shell` actually holds `/app.html`** (never leaves an empty cache/bricks). No eager image precache (on-demand only — an eager 1.8MB precache is what saturated the pipe). `caches.match` searches ALL caches so the old `cs-v3xx` copy is still found during the migration. `/api/` + `brand-brain-animation` still bypass. sw.js node --check OK. **THE COLD-DOWNLOAD IS PAID ONCE (this migration) THEN NEVER AGAIN.** Recovery Jörgen may still need this one time: the currently-installed old SW may be wedged mid-hang — simplest reset = **open `contentshrimp.com/app.html` in the phone BROWSER (not the installed icon), let it finish ONCE (be patient, ~5–10 min this one time), then the installed icon opens instantly** (browser tab + installed PWA share the same SW cache). If still stuck: remove the home-screen icon, load the site once in the browser, re-add to home screen. **BIGGER LEVER not yet done (offer):** app.html is 824 KB in ONE file — even gzipped (~150–200 KB over the wire) it's the whole first-open cost; genuinely shrinking the critical path (lazy-load heavy inline stuff, strip dead CSS/JS) would cut the one-time cold load. **NEW DEPLOY WORKFLOW (updated below in "What this is"): bump `const BUILD` in sw.js, NOT `const CACHE`.**
- **v309 measured profile of app.html (so we stop guessing):** 821 KB raw = **552 KB inline JS (one block) + 237 KB CSS + 31 KB markup**, NO base64 bloat (images already external, good). **Real over-the-wire cost = 196 KB gzip (~150 KB brotli — Vercel serves brotli automatically).** So a NORMAL new user (broadband/4G) gets it in <1 s; only a pathological ~0.5 KB/s connection pays ~6 min, and with v309 that's ONE time then cached forever. Two small hardening changes shipped alongside v309: **(1) splash no longer forces a 1050 ms minimum show** — `dismissCsSplash` min-show cut 1050→**250 ms** (~L6357) so a fast/cached open drops straight into the app (the 0.5 s fade still smooths it); the branded splash + its 4 s failsafe stay, because it's the only feedback on a slow load and is NOT the cause of the hang (the download is). Did NOT remove the splash (Jörgen offered) — removing it would show a blank screen during a slow load, strictly worse. **(2) `vercel.json`: added `/sw.js` → `Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate`** so a CDN edge can never pin a stale worker → update detection stays reliable (`.html` is already `no-store`). node --check all 5 inline scripts OK, vercel.json valid. **REMAINING first-load levers (NOT done — need Jörgen's `node mobile-user.js` to verify since I can't render mobile):** (a) **Supabase loads render-blocking from jsdelivr (3rd-party) on the critical path AND the SW can't cache it (cross-origin = not `type:'basic'`) → it re-fetches every launch** — self-hosting `supabase.min.js` same-origin would let the SW cache it + kill a 3rd-party connection on every open (real slow-net win, but touches the auth boot path → verify before trusting live); (b) true code-splitting the 552 KB JS (load meme/viral/blog/onboarding on demand) to shrink the FIRST cold load — high value only for pathological connections, high risk in a shared-global single file, must be QA'd. The 237 KB CSS in `<head>` is render-blocking so the splash can't paint until it arrives; moving it out risks app-wide FOUC → left alone.

## What this is
Single-file PWA. In `~/boring-content-engine-deploy`:
- **app.html** — the entire frontend (one huge file: `<style>` + inline `<script>`).
- **api/*.js** — Vercel serverless (`generate-ideas`, `remix`, `transcribe-url`, `_llm`, `_usage`, …).
- **sw.js** — service worker. **As of v309 the cache name `const CACHE='cs-shell'` is STABLE — do NOT bump it (renaming it forces a full cold re-download for slow-connection users, which is the exact bug we fixed).** To push an app update, bump **`const BUILD='vNNN'`** instead (current: **v309**) — that byte-changes sw.js so the browser fetches a new worker, and `install` refreshes app.html into the same stable cache. SW is **cache-first** now (opens instantly from cache; updates land one launch after a BUILD bump), NOT network-first — ignore any older "SW is network-first" note.

## Mobile testing — runs on Jörgen's Mac, writes into this folder → Claude reads the outputs
- **HARD RULE FROM JÖRGEN (do not violate, do not re-litigate, do not "offer the cheaper option to save credits"): ALWAYS use `node mobile-user.js` — the full credit-using, user-simulating QA run — for ANY verification. NEVER suggest `mobile-test.js` / `mobile-shots.js`.** The screenshot-only crawlers can't reach half the app (anything behind Generate, waiting/loading states, generated results, added links), so they miss places and angles. The full simulation is the ONLY acceptable verification tool. He has said this many times.
- `node mobile-user.js` — **THE one to use.** AI QA engineer: fills forms, hits **Generate**, **WAITS for the generation/network to finish**, adds links/inputs, judges PASS/FAIL → **mobile-user-report.md** + **qa-*.png** (every screen, incl. post-generate). Needs an LLM key in `.env`/`.env.local`.
- **QA driver keys (2026-07-09): only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is present, and it ran OUT OF CREDITS mid-run** (caused the "4 blocked" in the 16:42 report). `pickLLM` now supports `QA_PROVIDER=xai|grok|groq|openai|anthropic` to force a provider, and xAI default is **grok-4.5** (grok-2 was retired May 15; askLLM sends screenshots to xAI via OpenAI `image_url`, so vision QA works). **To run on Grok, Jörgen must first add `XAI_API_KEY=xai-…` to `.env`** (none present today), then `QA_PROVIDER=xai node mobile-user.js`. Or just top up Anthropic credits and run normally.
- `mobile-test.js` / `mobile-shots.js` — screenshot-only crawlers. DO NOT use for QA and DO NOT offer them.
- **LOGIN GOTCHA (the #1 recurring time-waster):** the magic-link session expires. If the saved `.auth.json` is stale, the tester runs **logged out** and spews fake `401`/`Cannot read '...filter'` errors — those are NOT real bugs. All three scripts are now patched to detect the login screen, clear stale auth, and **wait for a fresh login** before capturing. Flow when it runs: phone window opens on login → enter email → open magic-link email → paste link into THAT window → when the app shows, press **Enter** in the terminal.
- The screenshot functions were patched to grow the viewport to each view's full height (the app scrolls inside an inner container, so plain `fullPage` cropped everything below the fold).
